3d.output_is_binary_gltf_glb_the_web: Output is binary glTF (GLB) — the web-standard 3D container every engine and viewer reads. Inspection accepts .glb and .gltf from any public URL, up to the documented size cap.

3d.start_free_upgrade_only_when_a_draft: Start free. Upgrade only when a draft isn't enough. Paid tiers settle per-call in USDC over x402 — still no account, still no key.
3d.text_3d_draft_nim_trellis_single_subject: Text→3D draft (NIM TRELLIS): single subject, GLB, no rigging
3d.this_is_a_live_gltf_binary_rendered: This is a live glTF binary rendered in your browser. The free /api/3d/inspect endpoint reports exactly what's inside one of these — vertices, triangles, materials, textures, animations, extensions — and a prioritized plan to make it smaller and faster.
3d.yes_no_account_no_api_key_no: Yes. No account, no API key, no wallet. Free endpoints have a generous per-IP rate limit that only blunts abuse. The free draft generation tier runs on a shared GPU lane — it's honest about being a prototyping tier (draft geometry, GLB only, no rigging).

artifact_index.models_over_6_mb_are_rejected_because: Models over 6 MB are rejected, because Claude's artifact panel can hang on huge inlined payloads. Inlining base64-encodes the model, which costs four bytes per three, on top of the flat 565 KB viewer: a 6 MB model lands at roughly 8.6 MB of HTML. That total, not the model, is what the size stat grades.
artifact_index.paste_a_single_url_into_a_claude: Paste a single URL into a Claude conversation. The response is one self-contained HTML document: three.js, GLTFLoader, and your agent's GLB are all inlined. No script blocked by Claude's sandbox CSP, no fetch that ever leaves the page.
artifact_index.the_response_sets_a_csp_mirroring_claude: The response sets a CSP mirroring Claude's own, so behavior in the live preview matches behavior inside Claude.ai. No surprises between staging and prod.
artifact_index.three_js_gltfloader_and_the_glb_are: three.js, GLTFLoader, and the GLB are all inlined. The page renders with zero network calls, fully compatible with Claude's sandbox CSP that forbids fetch and external scripts.

assembly.explain1_body: Both machines are built when the page loads. Dimensions become profiles, profiles get revolved or extruded, and the results are merged into the parts you can see. A cylinder barrel is one revolved sawtooth, a rail is one closed cross-section swept down the track, and a propeller blade is a stack of NACA sections lofted with twist.
assembly.explain2_body: Pistons come from the exact planar slider-crank. The valve gear closes a four-bar chain by intersecting circles every frame. That is why a longer rod visibly dwells at top dead centre, and why a rod length that cannot physically reach refuses to move rather than stretching.
assembly.explain2_title: The motion is solved, not keyframed
assembly.explain3_body: Every machine is a small JSON object of numbers. Copy the spec, hand it to an agent, get a different machine back. Export the result as GLB and it drops straight into an avatar scene, a product page, or the glTF viewer.

avatar-cli.ci_gate1_note: Catches the re-export nobody mentioned, the lossy optimization pass, the teammate who swapped the model and kept the filename, and the CDN that started serving an error page with a 200.
avatar-cli.ci_gate2_note: xargs exits non-zero if any single invocation failed, so one bad manifest fails the whole step. Wire it into whatever already runs on release.
avatar-cli.ci_gate2_title: 02 Is every manifest still valid?
avatar-cli.ci_lede: A manifest that is only correct on the day you wrote it is a document, not a guarantee. Two checks turn it into one. Neither needs network access.
avatar-cli.ci_title: Fail the build, not the page
avatar-cli.cmd_hash_desc: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of a file, alone on stdout so it composes. The same digest init writes into mesh.sha256, which is what makes drift detection a one-line comparison.
avatar-cli.cmd_init_desc: Scaffolds a schema-valid manifest from a wallet, a name, and a mesh file. Reads the mesh once to compute its SHA-256 and size, so the document cannot disagree with the bytes it was built from.
avatar-cli.cmd_lede: No config file, no project scaffold, no state directory. Each command does one thing to one file and tells you what happened.
avatar-cli.cmd_preview_desc: Validates, then prints a resolver URL, an <agent-3d> snippet paired with the loader that registers it, and a zero-install iframe. Warns when mesh.uri is still a local path.
avatar-cli.cmd_validate_desc: Checks a manifest against @three-ws/avatar-schema and prints every error at the instance path where it happened. Non-zero exit makes it a build gate rather than a report.
avatar-cli.cta_docs: Read the docs <svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3 7h8M7 3l4 4-4 4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg>
avatar-cli.hero_sub: Scaffold a hash-anchored avatar manifest from a wallet and a GLB, validate it against the published schema, and print an embed snippet that actually renders. Offline, deterministic, and safe to put in a release script.
avatar-cli.live_fallback_body: The component loader did not register. The snippet is still correct; see the web component reference.
avatar-cli.live_lede: This is not a screenshot. The markup below is exactly what preview prints, pasted into this page unmodified. If it ever stopped working, this section would break in public.
avatar-cli.live_note: Both lines matter. <agent-3d> is an unknown element until the loader registers it, so pasting only the tag gives you an empty box with no warning. That is why preview always prints them together. The viewer opposite is this exact markup; only a stylesheet rule caps its width on narrow screens, which the element handles by re-laying out.
avatar-cli.live_title: The snippet on the left is rendering on the right
avatar-cli.manifest_field_id_note: A CAIP-10 account, or a name service handle ending in .eth, .ws, or .sol.
avatar-cli.manifest_field_mesh_note: Content address for the model. The field that catches a silent re-export.
avatar-cli.manifest_field_owner_note: Chain-scoped account, so ownership is unambiguous off-platform.
avatar-cli.manifest_field_skeleton_note: One of avaturn, mixamo, rpm, vrm-humanoid, custom. Decides which animation library retargets onto the rig.
avatar-cli.manifest_lede: Seven required fields. uri says where the mesh is, sha256 says what it must be. Those are different promises, and only the second one survives someone re-uploading a different model to the same path.
avatar-cli.manifest_more: Five optional fields the schema also accepts: animations, accessories, traits, creator, and signature. The last one is the interesting one: everything else is a claim you are making, while a signature is a claim someone else can verify without trusting your server.

brownout.hero_p: A fallback is code that only runs when something is broken, which makes it the least-tested code in any codebase. So this platform does two things about it. Every response says where its data came from and how fresh it is, in a header you can read. And every fallback below has been executed for real, with the provider it protects against genuinely refusing, inside the same request path a user hits. The receipts are underneath. Read the reference for the header grammar and how to run a probe yourself.
brownout.live_h2: A live call, from your browser, just now
brownout.meta_desc: Every response this API sends says where its data came from and how fresh it is, and every fallback is proven by breaking the upstream it protects against. Read the receipts: which provider refused, which one caught the request, and how old the answer was.
brownout.og_desc: Fallbacks are the least-tested code in any codebase, because the thing they protect against does not happen on demand. So we break it on purpose, and publish the receipts.
brownout.proven_p: Each card names an upstream, the failure injected into it, and what the endpoint did anyway. A verdict of not exercised is reported as plainly as a failure: it means the fault was accepted but a warm cache answered before any upstream call happened, so nothing was actually proven. A proof that did not run is not a pass.
brownout.reading_p1: Every endpoint answers with x-brownout, and adds x-brownout-trace when something degraded. Freshness is a lattice rather than a flag, and a response reports the worst tier that contributed to it: live came off the wire during your request, cache is a hit inside its intended lifetime, stale is older than that because an upstream could not answer, and fallback means a different provider or a different method answered the question. A page assembled from one live read and one half-hour-old reading is not live, so it does not get to say it is.
brownout.reading_p2: The @three-ws/brownout package parses these headers, and gives your own tests the same fault injection this page is built on, so you can assert that your integration degrades the way you think it does.
brownout.twitter_desc: We break our own providers on purpose, in the real request path, and publish what came back.

bundles.desc_placeholder: What a buyer gets, in one line.
bundles.hero_lede: Sell several of an agent's skills as one purchase. The hard part was never the bundle, it was the price, so three.ws prices it from your own sales: it finds the buyers who already bought two or more of these skills separately and shows what the bundle would have earned from those same people. See the docs for the API.
bundles.live_p: Live on this agent right now, served publicly at /api/agents/<id>/bundles and bought in one payment that unlocks every skill inside. Pausing one hides it from buyers and leaves it here, dimmed, so you can put it back. How checkout works.
bundles.meta_desc: Bundle an agent's skills into one purchase and price it from your own sales. three.ws backtests any price against the buyers who already bought two or more of those skills separately, so you can see what the bundle would have earned before you publish it.
bundles.og_desc: Bundle an agent's skills into one purchase, priced from your own sales rather than a rule of thumb.
bundles.pick_sub: Only skills with an active price can be bundled, because a bundle has to be worth less than its parts to mean anything.
bundles.price_idle: Select at least two skills to see pricing.
bundles.price_sub: Every number here comes from this agent's confirmed, paid purchases. Trials and access granted by an earlier bundle are excluded, so nothing inflates what you see.
bundles.step1_body: Choose two or more priced skills. The sum of their list prices is your ceiling.
bundles.step2_body: Move the price and watch the backtest against buyers who really paid.
bundles.step3_body: The bundle goes live on the agent. One payment unlocks every skill in it.
bundles.sum_label: Sum of the parts <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="What a buyer pays today if they buy every selected skill one at a time. Your bundle price should sit below this." aria-label="What sum of the parts means">?</button>
bundles.tile_backtest: Bundle would earn <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="The same buyers, at the price above. This is a backtest over real history, not a forecast: it says nothing about buyers you have not had yet." aria-label="What bundle would earn means">?</button>
bundles.tile_better: Better off <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="How many of those buyers spent more piecemeal than this bundle costs. These are the ones the bundle wins on value." aria-label="What better off means">?</button>
bundles.tile_buyers: Multi-skill buyers <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="People who already bought two or more of the selected skills separately. This is the population a bundle would have converted, so it is the only one worth pricing against." aria-label="What multi-skill buyers means">?</button>
bundles.tile_delta: Revenue delta <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="Backtest minus what they really paid. Negative means this price would have left money on the table with the buyers you already had." aria-label="What revenue delta means">?</button>
bundles.tile_paid: They paid <button type="button" class="bd-tip" data-tip="What those buyers actually spent across the selected skills, at your list prices, in confirmed purchases." aria-label="What they paid means">?</button>

capture.film_a_room_a_street_an_object: Film a room, a street, an object — and get back an explorable 3D point cloud. A feed-forward Geometric Context Transformer reconstructs dense world-space geometry from the frames, then streams a coloured .ply you can orbit right here. Already have a point cloud? Drop it in or paste a URL.
capture.frames_stream_through_a_feed_forward_tra: Frames stream through a feed-forward transformer that grounds coordinates, reads dense geometry, and corrects drift across the whole clip — no per-scene optimisation. The result is a world-space coloured point cloud. Output renders with WebGL THREE.Points; this is a point cloud, not a Gaussian splat.

choreograph.footnote: A routine is a list of slots and holds, not a list of animation files: the same routine looks different on an agent that has remapped its own gestures on the vocabulary page, which is the point. The wire format, the storage shape and the playback API are documented in docs/choreography.
choreograph.hero_lede: One gesture is a beat. A routine is a performance: wave, then think, then present the thing you just made. Build one on the timeline, watch the whole thing on a live avatar, then save it to your agent and play it by name from any embed.

choreograph.palette_p: The fixed slot vocabulary. A step names a slot, so a routine shared with another agent still plays that agent's own take on each gesture.
choreograph.routine_p: Each row is one beat. Drag to reorder, set how long it holds, and point any step at a different clip. The stage follows every edit.
choreograph.save_lede: Sign in to save this routine to an agent. Everything else on this page works without an account, and your routine is already in the URL.
choreograph.ship_p: Save the routine to an agent you own and it travels with that agent: the public manifest carries it, and any embed can play it by name.
choreograph.stage_empty_body: Start from a routine below, or add a gesture. Nothing 3D loads until you do.
choreograph.stage_error_body: The clip is fine: the shared preview rig could not bind it. Swap the step's clip, or preview it on its own in the gallery.
choreograph.stage_error_title: That step did not fit the preview avatar.
choreograph.start_p: Five performances built from the shipped slot vocabulary. Load one, then change anything: they are starting points, not templates you have to keep.

companion.default_voice_hint: Real speech from Voice Lab lanes, spoken in the browser.
companion.feed_sub: Every message that came in, what it scored, and why. Quiet ones are kept here instead of being spoken.
companion.hero_sub: A 3D character that walks on and tells you the things worth interrupting you for. Connect what you already use, give the people who matter their own face and voice, and let everything else stay quiet.
companion.meta_desc: A 3D companion that delivers your important messages in person. Connect Telegram, your calendar, your inbox, or your phone, give each contact their own avatar, and hear what matters out loud.
companion.og_desc: A 3D companion that delivers your important messages in person. Bring your own keys, give your contacts a face, and hear what matters out loud.
companion.pitch_card1: 📱 Your phone, your Mac, anything One token, one endpoint. An Android profile, a Shortcut, a Mail rule, a build script, or an agent that decided you need to know.
companion.pitch_card2: ✈️ Telegram A bot you create yourself relays only the chats you add it to. Revoke it and the connection is gone, with nothing left behind here.
companion.pitch_card3: 📅 Calendar The private iCal link Google, Apple, Outlook and CalDAV all publish. It tells you the meeting is starting while you can still make it.
companion.pitch_card4: ✉️ Email IMAP with an app password. Read only, headers and a preview, and your unread state is never touched. Or triage it on your own machine and send nothing but the sentence.
companion.pitch_foot: It reaches you here, as a push on your phone, and on your desktop as a character that walks across your screen. Developers get all of it as an SDK, a CLI, and an MCP server.
companion.pitch_h: Your phone buzzes forty times a day. Two of those mattered.
companion.pitch_lead: The companion reads what comes in from the accounts you already use, decides what a person would actually want a tap on the shoulder for, and then walks over and says it. Everything else stays quiet, in a feed, with the reason it stayed quiet.
companion.pitch_signin: Sign in and set it up
companion.pitch_step1: 1 Connect what you already use. Every credential is yours, and encrypted here.
companion.pitch_step2: 2 Give the people who matter a face and a voice. Their messages arrive as them.
companion.pitch_step3: 3 Set the bar, and the hours you will not be disturbed. That is the whole product.
companion.quiet_hint: Inside this window messages are stored, never spoken.
companion.settings_sub: The bar a message has to clear before anyone walks on stage.
companion.sources_sub: Bring your own keys. Nothing is stored that you cannot revoke from the other side in one click, and every credential is encrypted before it touches the database.
companion.stage_empty: Nothing delivered yet. Connect a source below, or send a test message from your phone, and whoever it is from will show up here.
companion.stage_sub: The most recent delivery, exactly as your companion performs it.
companion.threshold_hint: Lower hears more. Higher keeps it to the things you would want a tap on the shoulder for.
companion.timezone_hint: Detected from this browser and used for quiet hours.

connect.add_three_ws_to_claude_chatgpt_cursor: Add three.ws to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or Claude Code and your assistant can generate 3D models and avatars, run your agents, read their wallets and pay for services over x402. Sign in once in your browser: there is no API key to copy. Every tool is listed in the MCP tool catalog.
connect.any_client_that_speaks_streamable_http_m: Any client that speaks Streamable HTTP MCP can connect. Clients with OAuth support sign you in automatically from the server's WWW-Authenticate header. Clients without it can send an API key from Dashboard → API as Authorization: Bearer.
connect.back_in_apps_connectors_click_create_nam: Back in Apps & Connectors, click Create. Name it three.ws, paste the URL, choose OAuth, and create it.
connect.bob_shell_reads_the_same_files: Using Bob Shell? It reads the same files but names the URL key httpURL, so rename url to httpURL. Or let the CLI write it: npx three-ws setup --clients bob.
connect.chatgpt_adds_custom_mcp_servers_through_: ChatGPT adds custom MCP servers through Developer mode, on the plans where OpenAI offers it. There is no pre-filled link, so copy the URL first.
connect.click_connect_and_sign_in_to_three: Click Connect and sign in to three.ws. Read the permissions before you approve.
connect.click_the_button_above_check_the_name: Click the button above, check the name and URL, then click Add. Adding it by hand instead: Customize → Connectors (Settings → Connectors on some accounts), Add custom connector, paste the URL.
connect.config_format_from_ibm_bob_s_mcp: Config format from IBM Bob's MCP docs.
connect.each_tool_declares_whether_it_only_reads: Each tool declares whether it only reads, writes, or does something irreversible, so your client knows what to ask you about. The tool catalog has a ready-made trust policy to paste in.
connect.every_client_you_connect_appears_under_d: Every client you connect appears under Dashboard → Settings → Connected apps. Revoking one stops that client within an hour, when its current access token expires. Your agents and balances are untouched.
connect.every_hosted_server_with_its_auth_and: Every hosted server, with its auth and resources, is listed machine-readably at /.well-known/mcp.json.
connect.for_github_copilot_agent_mode_in_vs: For GitHub Copilot agent mode in VS Code. The button opens VS Code's install prompt; the server signs you in on first use.
connect.grok_bot_adds_custom_mcp_servers_as_conn: Grok Bot adds custom MCP servers as connectors. There is no pre-filled link: enter these three settings. They follow the server you picked in step 1.
connect.grok_localhost_note: Use the public https://three.ws URL only. A localhost or private-network URL never works, because Grok Bot connects from xAI's cloud, not from your machine.
connect.grok_own_allowance: Grok Bot shares one network address with other hosted agents. For your own generation allowance, generate a private connector URL below. The full walkthrough is on the Grok page.
connect.grok_step_ask: Start a task and ask for a 3D model or an avatar. Grok Bot calls the three.ws tools on your behalf.
connect.grok_step_enter_fields: Set the transport to Streamable HTTP, paste the URL above, and choose the authentication shown above. The free servers need none. Every other server uses OAuth: sign in to three.ws when Grok Bot asks. On the Grok server, use the OAuth URL instead to add your agents.
connect.grok_step_open_connectors: In Grok Bot, open the connectors settings and add a custom MCP connector.
connect.in_a_chat_open_the_menu_then: In a chat, open the + menu, then Connectors, and switch three.ws on for that conversation.
connect.in_a_new_chat_open_the_menu: In a new chat, open the + menu, choose Developer mode, and tick three.ws.
connect.ibm_bob_reads_mcp_servers_from: IBM Bob reads MCP servers from .bob/mcp.json in your project, or ~/.bob/settings/mcp.json for every workspace. Pick 3D Studio (free) above to connect with no sign-in; a server that needs sign-in runs Bob's built-in OAuth flow on first connect.
connect.in_claude_code_type_pick_the_server: In Claude Code, type /mcp, pick the server you just added and choose Authenticate.
connect.in_settings_apps_connectors_advanced_set: In Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings, turn on Developer mode.
connect.link_format_from_cursor_s_install_link: Link format from Cursor's install-link docs.
connect.link_format_from_vs_code_s_mcp: Link format from VS Code's MCP developer guide.
connect.in_the_bob_panel_open_settings: In the Bob panel, open Settings → MCP and click Edit Project MCP (or Edit Global MCP), paste the entry, and save.
connect.links_open_your_client_with_the_server: Links open your client with the server filled in. You still review it and confirm.

cookbook.hero_p: Not walkthroughs. Every recipe here is a real file that was executed against the live API before it was published: a command-line tool, a batch pipeline, an MCP server, a CI gate, a self-correcting agent loop. Copy one, run it, change it.

cookbook.outro_p: A recipe is a file that runs, plus the prose explaining why it is shaped that way. If you built something on the 3D API worth copying, send it.

cookbook_index.one_rule_keeps_this_honest_the_loop: One rule keeps this honest: the loop gets a budget of exactly one retry per prop. One retry captures most of the win; after that, ship the draft or flag it for a human.

cookbook_index.the_critic_is_calibrated_to_the_tier: The critic is calibrated to the tier. A draft lane judged against production standards fails everything, and an over-eager critic writes 1,000-character "revised prompts" that a single-subject generator cannot use. The system prompt tells the critic what normal looks like at this tier, to fail only on identity (could a stranger name the subject?), and to keep any rewrite short and concrete.
cookbook_index.the_draft_lane_is_single_subject_and: the draft lane is single-subject and unrigged by design; three.ws serves higher-poly PBR and rigged lanes with the same tool shape when quality matters
cookbook_index.the_free_draft_lane_is_per_ip: the free draft lane is per-IP rate-limited; keep max_workers modest (four here) or move to a keyed lane
cookbook_index.the_free_lane_is_the_draft_tier: The free lane is the draft tier: one subject, draft-fidelity geometry, no rigging. It has a generous per-IP rate limit protecting a shared GPU allocation; over the limit it returns 429 with a Retry-After header.

cookbook_index.the_model_looks_like_a_dense_feathery: The model looks like a dense, feathery bush in a dark round pot rather than a trailing pothos: the leaves are elongated/serrated instead of chunky heart-shaped, there’s no gold variegation, and the coral half‑moon planter and sunlit, collectible look are missing.

cookbook_index.the_render_clearly_presents_a_warped_dri: The render clearly presents a warped driftwood ticket sign with peeling crimson stencil letters, rusted iron brackets, embedded green/blue sea glass, and a corroded bulb—it reads as the requested haunted seaside ticket sign and matches the eerie, decayed mood.

cookbook_index.the_render_depicts_a_single_triangular_r: The render depicts a single triangular red pennant on a weathered wooden pole with long frayed streamers and worn cloth; despite soft detail, it reads clearly as a tattered seaside carnival flag and suits the haunted vintage theme.
cookbook_index.the_render_is_an_indistinct_white_blob: The render is an indistinct white blob with no clear doll silhouette, facial features, clothing, or base—none of the fortune-teller automaton details (shawl, eye, brass crank, tarot card) are readable, so the subject is unrecognizable and fails the theme.
cookbook_index.the_render_looks_like_a_dark_multi: The render looks like a dark, multi-leaf palm/fern in a brown ribbed pot rather than a small Monstera sapling: leaves are umbrella-like with radial cuts instead of three broad glossy Monstera leaves with simple fenestrations, and the pot reads as dark wood rather than mustard-yellow enamel, so the subject is ambiguous.
cookbook_index.the_render_shows_a_chunky_golden_barrel: The render shows a chunky golden barrel cactus body but the concrete pot, saucer, and pebble topdressing are missing—so it fails the ‘potted houseplant’ prop requirement and doesn’t match the set theme. cookbook_index.the_render_shows_a_small_ornate_carousel: The render shows a small ornate carousel platform and canopy but no standalone horse — the subject is a carousel structure rather than a single barnacled carousel horse, so a viewer couldn't identify the intended prop. crews.found_copy: Two steps. The tag is a short badge worn over your avatar in world; the name is what people read. Both are public and the tag is unique across the whole site.
crews.hero_sub: A crew is a group of accounts whose agents fly one tag. Every member stands in this headquarters as their own agent, lit when they are live in the world and unlit when they are not. Found one, invite your people, and share the link.
crews.invite_empty: Type at least 2 characters of a name or username.
crews.invite_note: Someone already in a crew shows their tag instead of a button.
crews.invited_copy: Accepting one clears the rest. You can be in one crew at a time.
crews.meta_desc: Found a crew, invite your people, and watch the whole roster stand in one 3D headquarters. Every member appears as their own agent, lit when they are live in the world.
crews.og_desc: A crew is a group of people whose agents share one tag and one headquarters. Found one, invite your people, and see who is live in the world right now.
crews.roster_copy: Owner first, then by the day they joined. Presence is the same signal the in-world friends list reads, so “in world” means the same thing in both places.
crews.signedout_copy: A crew is tied to your account, not to a browser, so the roster and the tag follow you everywhere you sign in. Browsing the directory below needs no account at all.

data_desk.empty_body: The fresh-wallet workers buy a dataset roughly every minute and a 3D prop every few minutes. The first purchases will appear here with their receipts as soon as they settle on Solana.
data_desk.error_body: Something went wrong loading the bought datasets.
data_desk.how_1: A brand-new keypair is generated and stored encrypted. It has never appeared on chain.
data_desk.how_2: One funding transaction gives it the exact USDC price of its job plus enough SOL to stay rent-exempt and pay two network fees.
data_desk.how_3: The wallet calls the paid endpoint, receives the 402 challenge, signs one USDC transfer and gets the data back. The settlement is a normal Solana transaction anyone can verify.
data_desk.how_4: The wallet sends any leftover USDC to the treasury, closes its token account so the rent goes back to the funder, and sends every remaining lamport home. It ends at zero and is never used again.
data_desk.how_more: Lane statistics and every wallet's three signatures are public at
data_desk.lede: Every minute the platform mints a few Solana wallets that have never existed before, gives each one exactly one job's worth of USDC, and lets it buy a real dataset from the three.ws market-data storefront over the x402 payment protocol. The answer lands here with its receipt: the wallet that paid, the price, and the settlement transaction. Then the wallet is emptied and closed. No curation, no mocks: this is the agent economy doing real work, one paid call at a time.
data_desk.ledger_lede: Every row is one wallet's single purchase. The wallet did not exist before the minute it paid and was closed right after; the receipt link opens the settlement on Solscan.
data_desk.meta_description: Live market data bought minute by minute by brand-new agent wallets over x402. Every dataset carries its receipt: the wallet that paid, the price, and the Solana settlement transaction.

demos_audio2face.powered_by_nvidia_audio2face_3d_over_nvc: Powered by /api/a2f (NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D over NVCF gRPC) and /api/tts/speak (NVIDIA Magpie). The blendshape→morph mapping lives in src/voice/a2f-player.js — it reuses the ARKit/VRM/Oculus vocabulary in src/voice/arkit-blendshapes.js, so any humanoid rig lip-syncs without a per-rig allowlist. See the amplitude-only lipsync demo for the fallback path on its own.

demos_audio2face.type_a_line_it_s_spoken_in: Type a line. It's spoken in NVIDIA Magpie's voice, and that exact audio is sent to NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D, which returns a per-frame ARKit blendshape track. The avatar's mouth and face animate frame-for-frame with the real voice — mapped onto whatever morph-target convention the loaded GLB ships (ARKit, common avatar-platform, VRM, Oculus visemes). If Audio2Face is unavailable, the avatar still speaks and falls back to amplitude lipsync — never a frozen face.

demos_livepeer_inference.meta_description: Same prompt, two providers. Compare three.ws default inference against a decentralized AI gateway side-by-side: latency, token counts, and the full reply from each.
demos_livepeer_inference.powered_by_livepeer_ai_gateway_decentral: Powered by Livepeer AI Gateway on the decentralized side. The default reply comes from the three.ws provider chain, and each card names the provider and model that actually answered it. The public decentralized gateway takes no key, so it is rate-limited and often has no orchestrator online for a given model.
demos_livepeer_inference.same_prompt_two_providers_real_responses: Same prompt, two providers, real responses. The left card hits the three.ws inference chain, which answers from whichever provider is fastest to respond. The right card routes the identical request through a decentralized AI gateway whose orchestrators run open-weight models on commodity GPUs. Phase 4 of the roadmap: decoupling inference from any single vendor so agents stay online when one provider doesn't.

diff.explain1_body: Objects are matched by name, then by content hash, then by similarity, the same three-tier strategy git uses for file renames. An exporter that renumbers Mesh.001 reads as a rename, not as a rewrite.
diff.explain2_body: Vertex data is compared at a quantum of 1e-4 units, so the float drift a re-export or a Draco round trip introduces does not register while a genuine edit does.
diff.explain2_title: Tolerant on noise, strict on edits
diff.explain3_body: none, cosmetic, minor, major, breaking. Breaking means something a consumer references by name is gone: a clip, a joint, a mesh. That is the failure that renders fine and never moves.
diff.explain4_body: This page, the glb-diff CLI, and the free API all run @three-ws/glb-diff, so a verdict in CI can never disagree with what you see here.
diff.hero_sub: A checksum says two files differ. It cannot tell a lossless recompression from a rig that quietly lost three finger joints, and only one of those takes your avatar off the screen. Drop a .glb on each side and get the change set: geometry, materials, textures, skeletons, and clips, with renames and moves detected the way git detects them.
diff.hero_title: What actually changed between these two models?
diff.meta_desc: Drop two .glb files and see exactly what changed: geometry, materials, textures, skeletons, and animation clips, with git-style rename and move detection and a severity you can gate a build on. Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
diff.og_desc: Two models in, one change set out: what moved, what was renamed, which joints disappeared, and whether anything downstream just broke.
diff.page_title: Model Diff · What changed between two 3D models · three.ws
diff.stage_empty_body: Overlay the after on top of the before, wipe between them, or set them side by side.

docs_freshness.does_this_documentation_still_describe_t: Does this documentation still describe the code?
docs_freshness.every_doc_names_the_files_npm_scripts: Every doc names the files, npm scripts, and API routes it is about. That makes each page measurable: bind it to the source it names, then ask git whether that source was committed to after the doc was last written or last reviewed. Code that moved since is code the page has never been checked against. Reading a page and finding it already correct counts too: that check is recorded as a review, so real work never has to be faked with a cosmetic edit.
docs_freshness.meta_description: Which three.ws docs still describe the code that ships. Every doc is bound to the source files it names, and git decides whether that source moved after the doc was written.
docs_freshness.meta_og_description: Documentation drift, measured. Each doc is bound to the code it names; git decides whether that code moved after the doc was last written.
docs_freshness.meta_twitter_description: Does this documentation still describe the code? Every doc is scored against the source files it documents, and this dashboard ranks the drift so the stalest pages get fixed first.

All figures come from real walk activity; nothing is sampled or estimated.

docs_walk_analytics.owner_only_the_dashboard_api_requires_a: Owner-only. The dashboard API requires a signed-in session (or a bearer token with the avatars:read scope) and verifies you own the avatar — others get a 403.

docs_walk_analytics.the_ingest_accepts_this_batch_all_fields: The ingest accepts this batch (all fields optional unless noted):

docs_walk_analytics.the_top_10_embed_hosts_by_session: The top 10 embed hosts by session count.
docs_walk_analytics.the_walk_runtime_accumulates_two_running: The walk runtime accumulates two running totals — horizontal distance and session wall-clock — and flushes a compact batch to POST /api/walk/metrics roughly every 60 seconds, plus once on page hide via navigator.sendBeacon. One batch becomes a single per-day rollup row, so an hour of walking is a handful of rows, not thousands.

docs_walk_chrome_extension.requires_chrome_109_or_newer_manifest_v3: Requires Chrome 109 or newer (Manifest V3). To package a store-ready zip, run npm run build:extension:prod, which emits dist/extension-<version>.zip.

docs_walk_chrome_extension.the_extension_requests_the_minimum_it_ne: The extension requests the minimum it needs and injects only on explicit user action.
docs_walk_chrome_extension.the_three_ws_walk_avatar_extension_v1: The three.ws Walk Avatar extension (v1.0.0) puts a floating 3D avatar on any website you visit. It walks alongside you and can read page sections aloud — a living browsing companion. It only ever runs on tabs you explicitly enable.
docs_walk_chrome_extension.with_narration_on_the_extension_parses_t: With narration on, the extension parses the page's main article (using a bundled Readability extractor), pulls out headings, paragraphs, list items, and blockquotes, and watches which section is in view. When a section becomes the focus it requests speech audio from the three.ws text-to-speech service and plays it, while telling the avatar to show a speech bubble and switch to an idle pose. You choose the voice, can mute mid-read, and narration honours prefers-reduced-motion. Authors can mark sections with data-walk-narrate (or skip them with data-walk-narrate="skip").

docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_a_three_ws_site: Companion mode is a three.ws-site feature. To put a walking avatar on your own site, use the one-tag JavaScript SDK; to walk your avatar on every site you visit, install the Chrome extension.
docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_the_platform_integrati: Companion mode is the platform integration of the publishable walk SDK. The three.ws navigation injects the companion script only when the companion is enabled — a page that never turns it on pays nothing for it. Under the hood it loads the avatar's pre-baked animation manifest and the same rendering engine the walk page and embeds use.
docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_the_site_wide_walking: Companion mode is the site-wide walking avatar on three.ws. Turn it on and your avatar detaches from the page chrome, walks around the screen, and follows you as you move between pages — complete with walk-aware page transitions.
docs_walk_companion_mode.detaches_and_roams_your_avatar_leaves_th: Detaches and roams. Your avatar leaves the page layout and becomes a free 3D character you can watch walk around.

docs_walk_companion_mode.waves_goodbye_and_hello_on_a_link: Waves goodbye and hello. On a link click the avatar plays a wave and sets a one-shot flag the destination page reads to wave back when it loads.

docs_walk_embed_api.source_is_the_real_authentication_the_if: Source is the real authentication. The iframe only accepts commands whose source window is its own parent; the SDK only accepts events whose source is the iframe it wraps. Spoofed origins can't inject either way.

docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_embed_is_designed_to_run_on: The embed is designed to run on any origin (it ships frame-ancestors *), so the host's origin cannot be allow-listed in advance. The real authentication is the message source: the iframe only accepts messages from its own parent window, and the host SDK only accepts messages from the iframe it mounted. As a belt-and-suspenders filter, a security-conscious integrator can pass an explicit allowOrigins list to the embed when the exact origin is known.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_host_page_and_the_iframe_talk: The host page and the /walk-embed iframe talk over window.postMessage. This is the wire contract: the message envelope, the commands you send in, the events the iframe sends back, and how origins are handled.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_legacy_flat_shape_a_bare_with: The legacy flat shape — a bare { type: 'walk:*' } with no channel/v — is still accepted inbound for backward compatibility with embeds shipped before this contract existed. New integrations should use the channelled envelope.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.using_the_javascript_sdk_it_does_the: Using the JavaScript SDK? It does the source check, channel guard, and event forwarding for you — just call ThreeWalkAvatar.on('walk:ready', …).
docs_walk_postmessage_events.when_you_listen_for_events_on_the: When you listen for events on the host side, always verify event.source === iframe.contentWindow before trusting a message, and check data.channel === 'three-walk' (or that the bare type is a known walk:* event).

economy_lab.duplicate_signature_retries_and_the_dust: Duplicate-signature retries and the dust guard are correct rejections, not capacity problems. Folding them into one number makes a healthy rail read as a starved one, so this page counts them separately and projects only against real demand.

economy_lab.every_figure_is_public_platform_wallet_b: Every figure is public: platform wallet balances, configured thresholds, and aggregate settle counts are already served by /api/x402-ring and /api/x402-status. No key material or per-user data is reachable from this page. The seed endpoint is /api/x402/runway-lab. Related surfaces: Money Pulse, Agent Economy Live.
economy_lab.every_three_ws_payment_passes_one_admiss: Every three.ws payment passes one admission check: can the fee wallet afford the next settle? This page runs that exact function, imported from the settle path, in your browser, against live production balances. Drag a knob and watch the rail survive or starve.

economy_lab.the_governor_recomputes_from_the_live_ba: The governor recomputes from the live balance on every settle, so spending shrinks the budget authorising the next spend. That feedback settles at spendable / (fee × (days + 1)) per day. At the stock three-day runway the rail delivers a quarter of spendable SOL per day, not a third: a 25% gap between the configured intent and the real throughput, and the reason “three days of runway” and “settlement stopped today” are not contradictions.
economy_lab.the_governor_s_budget_is_one_equation: The governor's budget is one equation with three independent terms, so a stall always has three possible fixes. Name the throughput you want and each lever is solved exactly, including the ones that cannot work.
economy_lab.the_last_24_hours_of_real_settle: The last 24 hours of real settle outcomes, next to what this model predicts for the same period. A gap between them is a bug in the model or a cause the model does not know about, and either is worth chasing.
economy_lab.the_only_knob_that_does_not_depend: The only knob that does not depend on the balance.
economy_lab.the_simulation_imports_and_from_the_same: The simulation imports walletDailyFeeBudgetLamports() and assessWalletFeeBudget() from wallet-fee-governor.js, the same module the live facilitator calls on every settle. Change the governor and this page changes with it. A parallel model would drift; this one cannot.

evm_wallet.grind_a_real_ethereum_evm_wallet_whose: Grind a real Ethereum / EVM wallet whose address starts or ends with characters of your choice — for your agent, treasury, or anywhere a memorable 0x address matters. The result is a normal secp256k1 keypair you can import into MetaMask, ethers, viem or Rabby. Runs entirely in your browser. The private key is never transmitted anywhere.
evm_wallet.hex_characters_only_0_9_a_f: Hex characters only (0–9, a–f). Each extra character is 16× harder. Mixed case (e.g. BeeF) matches the EIP-55 checksum — visually distinctive, ~2× harder per letter.
evm_wallet.meta_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address with the prefix or suffix of your choice. A real secp256k1 keypair — importable into MetaMask, ethers, viem. Runs entirely in your browser; the private key never leaves your device.
evm_wallet.meta_og_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address in your browser. A real keypair, importable into MetaMask. Keys never leave your device.
evm_wallet.meta_twitter_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address in your browser. Keys never leave your device.
evm_wallet.this_is_an_eoa_grinder_it_searches: This is an EOA grinder — it searches private keys directly, so you own the resulting address. (CREATE2 is the sibling tool for vanity smart-contract addresses, where you grind a salt instead of a key.) Keys are generated with your browser's CSPRNG, each match is re-derived and verified before it's shown, and the export below is an encrypted keystore by default.

exit-lab.honesty_h: What this can and cannot tell you
exit-lab.meta_desc: Replay the fleet's real closed trades under a different exit policy. Move the stop-loss, the trailing stop, the take-initials ladder and the moon-bag floor, and see what the fleet would have made on the SOL it already spent. Real positions, real on-chain fills, no synthetic data.
exit-lab.reasons_sub: Every closed trade is attributed to the one rule that fired. A policy that books its profit through a single rule is a policy resting on a single assumption.
exit-lab.share_btn: Copy a link to this policy
exit-lab.share_desc: Replay the fleet's real closed trades under a different exit policy and see what the SOL it already spent would have returned.
exit-lab.sub: The fleet already spent this SOL. This replays every real closed position through the exact exit code the live worker runs, with the rules changed to whatever you choose, and shows what those same trades would have returned. Nothing here is simulated: every entry, peak and final price is a recorded quote from a position that cost real money and settled on-chain.
exit-lab.sweep_sub: Replays the whole corpus against every combination on a grid and ranks the results. This is an exact search over trades that already happened, not a prediction: it tells you what the fleet's past would have paid, which is the only thing this data can honestly say.
exit-lab.title: Exit Lab
exit-lab.trades_sub: The positions where this policy diverges most from what the fleet actually did. Every row links to the buy and the sell on Solscan.

fade.honesty_1: A wallet's record counts only coins whose outcome is already known. A winner is a coin that graduated to an AMM or peaked at 3x or better.
fade.honesty_2: The odds above are measured out of sample: the cohort is rebuilt from coins labelled in the earlier half of the history, then graded on coins it could not have seen.
fade.honesty_3: A coin is scored only once at least five of its buyers have been observed. Below that the board says so rather than guessing.
fade.honesty_4: This is a probabilistic read on a hostile market, never a prediction, and never advice. A clear coin can still go to zero.
fade.honesty_5: The only coin three.ws promotes is $THREE. Every coin on this board is whatever the live feed handed us.
fade.honesty_h: What this is and is not
fade.kicker: Fade Radar · the inverse of smart money
fade.meta_desc: The inverse of the Smart Money Radar. Every pump.fun coin ranked by how much of its buy side comes from wallets with a judged record and not one winner in it, with the measured, out-of-sample odds behind each verdict.
fade.og_desc: Some wallets have bought dozens of coins and never once been right. When they crowd a launch, that launch wins 1.8% of the time against a 22% baseline. Here is where they are right now.
fade.page_title: Fade Radar: the wallets that are never right · three.ws
fade.share_title: Fade Radar: the wallets that are never right · three.ws
fade.sub: The Smart Money Radar asks who reputable is buying a coin. This asks the sharper question: how much of the buy side has never once been right. A reverse indicator here is a wallet the graph has watched buy at least five coins whose outcome is now known, with zero winners among them. They are not rare, and when they crowd a fresh launch that launch almost never goes anywhere. Nothing on this page is a short: on a bonding curve the only tradeable form of a fade is not buying.
fade.title: The wallets that are never right
fade.twitter_desc: The inverse of the Smart Money Radar: which coins the proven-losing wallets are crowding into right now, and the measured odds behind the call.

features.why_it_s_better_three_ar_methods: Why it's better: Three AR methods in one button — iOS Quick Look, Android Scene Viewer, and WebXR. The right one fires automatically. The agent stays live in WebXR, so conversation and animations work in AR.

fits.fineprint: Every figure here is read from the settled-sale ledger, never estimated: a row exists only after its USDC payment settled. Creator payouts route to the wallet resolved from the coin's launch records, so a split configuration can never redirect another coin's revenue. flow.canvas_label: Force-directed map of settled transfers between agent wallets. The same data is available as a sortable table below this graph.
flow.foot_source: Read live from /api/pulse?view=graph. Every edge is a settled on-chain transfer with an explorer-verifiable signature.
flow.hero_sub: Every other economy page here is a leaderboard. This one is the shape. Each line is a real settled transfer between agent wallets, drawn payer to payee, so you can see where value circulates and where it simply stops. Click any wallet to follow its money.
flow.how_to_read_body: Dot size is value handled. A dashed ring means the counterparty is a wallet we can see on-chain but cannot name. Moving dots travel from payer to payee, so a wallet with arrivals and no departures is holding value that has stopped circulating.
flow.meta_description: The shape of the three.ws agent economy: who pays whom, for which skill, and how much. Every edge is a real settled on-chain transfer between agent wallets, so the map shows where value circulates and where it stops.
flow.meta_og_description: A live map of the agent economy's topology: agents paying agents for real skills, drawn from settled on-chain transfers. See which wallets circulate value and which ones only collect it.
flow.meta_twitter_description: The topology of a machine economy: agents paying agents for real skills, every edge a settled on-chain transfer.
flow.search_label: Search wallets by name or address
flow.services_sub: Skill payments carry the name of the service they paid for, so the economy is legible down to the individual capability an agent sold.
flow.table_sub: The same data the graph draws, as text. Select a row to highlight it above.

gestures.atlas_desc: Every clip in the library, measured from its own keyframes and plotted by how energetic it is and how much of that energy is above the waist. Calm upper-body gestures gather top-left; explosive full-body dances and runs sit bottom-right. Colour is the region leading the movement. Click any point to play it, or to try it in the slot you have selected.

gestures.cta_sonar: Play these by hand, no camera
gestures.footnote: Slots, hints and clips are held together mechanically: tests/animation-slots.test.js scans every hint declared under src/ and fails the build if one resolves to no slot or to a clip that is not baked in public/animations/manifest.json. The full developer reference is docs/animations, and the walkthrough is Animate your agent.
gestures.grid_error_title: The clip library did not load.
gestures.hero_lede: An agent does not pick animation files. It names a slot, and the platform resolves that slot to a real clip. Skills name a slot indirectly, through a hint. This page is the whole vocabulary: what each slot plays, which skills trigger it, and how to point a slot at any other clip in the library.
gestures.hints_desc: A skill declares a hint when it starts. The hint resolves to a slot, the slot resolves to a clip, and the avatar plays it. Every row below is generated from the shipped skill definitions.
gestures.layers_desc: The walk state machine keeps a second, player-driven gesture library with a layer per gesture: upper gestures overlay locomotion, so an avatar waves or shrugs while it keeps walking; full gestures take the whole body and suppress movement until they end.
gestures.meta_desc: Every gesture a three.ws agent can play: the slot vocabulary, the clip each slot resolves to, the skills that trigger it, and a builder for overriding any slot on your own agent.
gestures.og_desc: The agent gesture vocabulary: 19 slots, the clip each plays, the skills that trigger them, and a live override builder.
gestures.override_lede: Point slot at any clip in the library, then save it straight to an agent you own.
gestures.similar_lede: Nearest clips in the measured motion space, not by name.
gestures.slots_desc: Fixed names an agent can override. A slot with no override resolves to the clip shown on its card.

globe.about_p1: Eleven layers of open data on one globe, refreshed continuously. Armed conflict, force posture and sanctions are classified from the GDELT event stream by CAMEO code and kept in a rolling window on three.ws, so the time control is real rather than decorative. Natural events come from the USGS earthquake feed and NASA EONET, severe weather from GDACS, connectivity loss from Georgia Tech's IODA project, and economic stress from World Bank indicators. Military bases, nuclear sites and maritime chokepoints are reference geography, and the chokepoint layer scores itself against the live feed rather than sitting still.
globe.about_p2: Every layer states the window it actually covered and every point links to its source. No credential is needed to read any of it. The full payload is one call: /api/globe/intel, documented in the globe reference.

guards.hero_p: This codebase has no CI. What protects it instead is a set of small, fast checks wired into paths nobody can skip: the prebuild, the gate, the deploy build, and the git pre-push hook. Every guard below exists because something broke once. Read the full reference or the tutorial on writing one.
guards.meta_desc: Every mechanical guard that protects the three.ws codebase, and the stage each one runs in. This repository has no CI, so correctness is enforced by fast local checks wired into the prebuild, the gate, the deploy build, and the git pre-push hook.
guards.more_p: A guard that is not wired into an unavoidable path protects nothing, and a guard nobody has proven still catches anything protects nothing either. Write the checker, give it an npm script, register it in data/guards.json with the violation it must reject, and wire it into a stage. npm run audit:guards tells you if the registry and the chains disagree; npm run prove:guards runs each guard against its declared violation and tells you whether it still fires.
guards.og_desc: No CI, by necessity. Every check that protects this codebase, what it protects, and the stage it runs in.
guards.twitter_desc: No CI, by necessity. Every check that protects this codebase, and where it runs.

herald.card_budget_body: An importance floor, a rate limit, quiet hours, dedupe with a TTL, and a freshness window. Scarcity is what keeps an interruption effective.

herald.card_silent_body: Every message that is not delivered comes back with a reason: duplicate, rate-limited, quiet-hours, below-importance-floor.
herald.def_batch: Said per burst, before the rest collapse into one line.
herald.def_dedupe: The same key is said once, however many times a feed repeats it.
herald.def_focus: Hold while the tab is in the background.
herald.def_freshness: Older than this is history, and history belongs in an inbox.
herald.def_minimportance: The interrupt floor. Below it, nothing is shown.
herald.def_quiet: Local window, wrapping past midnight, e.g. [22, 7].
herald.defaults_foot: Full API, recipes and the rail contract are in the documentation, and three.ws uses this to deliver its own notifications.
herald.defaults_sub: Chosen so that dropping this into a page cannot make it obnoxious.

herald.hero_lede: A notification is a badge you have to notice, in a tray you have to open, competing with forty others. This is the opposite: a 3D character walks into the corner of your page, looks at the person using it, and tells them, with a link to the thing it is about. One line of code. An accessible fallback when there is no GPU. And a CLI that announces when your build finishes.
herald.install_h: Put it in your own product
herald.install_sub: No build step required, and the 3D body is optional.

holo.hero_sub: A holographic foil sticker, rendered live. The die-cut outline, the iridescent foil, the light it reflects, and the peeling corner are all computed in your browser: no images, no model files. Tilt it with your pointer the way you would tilt the real thing, or type your own text and get it cut into a sticker of its own.
holo.how_body: The mark is rasterized, dilated by a disc the way a cutter adds a margin, and traced back into vector outlines with marching squares, holes included. The foil is a physical material with thin-film iridescence, and the peel is a vertex-shader cylinder roll, so the light on the curled lip is real.
holo.meta_desc: A real-time holographic foil sticker rendered in your browser. Tilt it with your pointer, peel the corner, switch foils, die-cut any text into a sticker, and download the frame as a PNG. All procedural, no assets.

Pair a three.ws satellite and the same pipeline you already use gets one, lip-synced to its own speech, on any screen in the house. Close this page and your assistant keeps working exactly as it did.

hood_portfolios.constituents_weights_schedule_the_origin: Constituents, weights, schedule, the originating prompt and the universe snapshot are hashed and signed. The hash goes on-chain; the document is content-addressed. It is immutable, so what you bought cannot change underneath you.
hood_portfolios.deliver_every_constituent_to_mint_receiv: Deliver every constituent to mint, receive every constituent to redeem. The fund never sells anything to let somebody in or out, so it eats no slippage and needs no price oracle to operate.
hood_portfolios.describe_a_portfolio_hold_it_on_chain: Describe a portfolio. Hold it on-chain.
hood_portfolios.elsewhere_refining_an_index_with_a_follo: Elsewhere, refining an index with a follow-up prompt changes the index you already hold. On-chain that is not a feature, it is the definition of a rug: the manifest is the only thing a holder relies on. So a refinement publishes a new portfolio whose parent pointer is the old one. Holders of the original keep exactly what they bought, and the fork pays its lineage a fixed slice of its fees. It is a budget, not a rule, so forking your own portfolio fifty times cannot pay out more than forking it once.
hood_portfolios.four_steps_and_only_one_of_them: Four steps, and only one of them involves a model. The interesting decisions are made before anything touches the chain; what happens on-chain is deliberately the least clever part.
hood_portfolios.meta_description: Describe a portfolio in a sentence and get a real basket of Robinhood Chain assets: tokenized equities, crypto majors and chain-native tokens in one index. Weights are committed on-chain as a signed manifest, held in kind, and rebalanced on a published schedule.
hood_portfolios.meta_og_description: A sentence in, a portfolio out. Tokenized equities, majors and memecoins in one index on Robinhood Chain, with the weights committed on-chain and rebalanced on schedule.
hood_portfolios.meta_og_title: Robinhood Portfolios: describe a portfolio, hold it on-chain · three.ws

hood_portfolios.nothing_here_is_investment_advice_and_a: Nothing here is investment advice, and a generated basket is not a recommendation. Tokenized equities on Robinhood Chain are tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Ltd and may not be offered, sold or delivered to US persons; this page is display and tooling only. A portfolio holding chain-native tokens can lose all of its value, and a halted equity leg suspends redemption for everyone until its issuer resumes it.
hood_portfolios.refining_mints_a_new_version_it_never: Refining mints a new version, it never edits the old one
hood_portfolios.robinhood_chain_is_the_one_place_where: Robinhood Chain is the one place where tokenized equities, crypto majors and memecoins trade against each other on the same chain. Write a sentence and a screen ranks that whole universe against it. What comes back is a real basket with target weights, held in kind by a vault that rebalances on a published schedule.
hood_portfolios.the_vault_holds_it_in_kind: The vault holds it in kind
hood_portfolios.what_do_you_want_exposure_to: What do you want exposure to?
hood_portfolios.when_the_published_interval_comes_due_th: When the published interval comes due, the move is offered as a descending-price auction any address can fill. There is no function that lets a manager trade the fund's assets. Every portfolio is backtested twice, on its schedule and never rebalanced, so you can see what the schedule actually did rather than assume it helped.
hood_portfolios.your_prompt_and_the_chain_s_holdable: Your prompt and the chain's holdable universe go to the model. Every token it returns is checked back against that universe, so anything invented is dropped, never repaired into something plausible.

hood_portfolios_universe.every_asset_a_portfolio_may_hold_and: Every asset a portfolio may hold, and the numbers that decide whether it may hold it. A token needs a live pool and a readable price to be selectable, because a constituent that cannot be bought cannot be issued into a basket or rebalanced out of one, however large its market cap.

hood_portfolios_universe.nav_premium_is_how_far_a_tokenized: NAV premium is how far a tokenized equity's on-chain price sits from its Chainlink reference. It is blank for anything without a feed, which is most of the chain: 34 of the 95 registry equities carry one, and no memecoin does. A portfolio never depends on a feed to operate, because issuance and redemption are in kind.

ibm_hello.every_avatar_here_is_generated_and_rigge: Every avatar here is generated and rigged on demand — no template library, no canned characters. The rig maps to three.ws's canonical skeleton, so the same idle, walk and emote clips play on whatever you describe. Want image→3D, your own GLB upload, or AR preview? Open the full Forge tool ↗ The free lane has an hourly cap so it stays free for everyone; if it's busy it tells you exactly when to retry. Generation runs on NVIDIA NIM and auto-falls back across lanes, so a model always comes back.

Orbit the mannequin, grab a limb to move it (inverse kinematics on hands and feet), nudge a joint with the sliders, or tap a preset to morph the whole pose. It's the exact rig behind the full Pose Studio, running live on the page.

The paid Forge settles real USDC — or $THREE — from your own wallet; the rest are free, no wallet needed. Nothing is mocked.

ibm_hello.x402_revives_the_dormant_http_402_paymen: x402 revives the dormant HTTP 402 Payment Required status as a real payment rail. You call an endpoint normally; if it's paid, the server answers 402 with an exact price, asset, and address. Your wallet signs a gasless authorization, you resend with an X-PAYMENT header, and the call settles on-chain — all in one round trip, no account or API key.
ibm_hello.yes_the_paid_demos_move_real_funds: Yes. The paid demos move real funds from your own wallet — USDC, or $THREE on Solana — and settle on Base or Solana mainnet. Nothing is simulated and nothing is mocked; the price you see is read live from the server's own 402 response, and you get an on-chain settlement receipt.

ibm_hello.you_ll_need_the_phantom_wallet_on: You'll need the Phantom wallet on Solana — holding the model's price in USDC, or the equivalent in $THREE, on Solana mainnet. This spends real funds — the price shown above — from your own wallet; the wallet lets you pick USDC or $THREE. The payment itself is a gasless signature: the network fee is sponsored by the x402 facilitator, so it isn't added to your cost. Generation runs once the payment verifies and takes roughly a minute. No wallet? Forge one free below — no wallet, no key, no payment.
ibm_hello.you_sign_a_gasless_usdc_authorization_re: You sign a gasless USDC authorization, resend with an X-PAYMENT header, and the call settles on-chain — your data comes back.

inspect.lede: This runs the exact quality gate three.ws applies to its own catalog entries against any .glb you give it. Same module, same thresholds, same decision. It runs entirely in your browser: nothing is uploaded, and the verdict is instant.

inspect.note_gate_p: The page imports the same module the seeding cron runs, so the rules here cannot drift from the rules in production. Read the full gate documentation for the vision stage that runs after this one.
inspect.note_strict_p: A creator who generates a coarse mesh chose to, and can regenerate. A visitor browsing the catalog chose nothing: every entry is the platform vouching for itself. One melted blob on the storefront costs more trust than ten rejected generations cost compute.
inspect.note_structure_p: These checks measure whether a model is built well enough to publish: density, weight, texture, bounds, assembly. Whether it looks good is judged separately by a vision model on the catalog path.

integrity.agent_wallets_on_three_ws_are_custodial: Agent wallets on three.ws are custodial — we hold the keys and sign on your behalf. So we make custody provable, not promised. Here's exactly what is shared, what is not, and how your camera, motion, and location are used.

irl_privacy.reads_your_phone_s_gyroscope_so_agents: Reads your phone's gyroscope so agents stay locked in place as you turn to look around. Used in real time to position the scene; nothing is sent off your device.
irl_privacy.renders_the_live_ar_passthrough_so_agent: Renders the live AR passthrough so agents look anchored to the real world behind them. The video is drawn on your screen only — frames are never uploaded or stored.
irl_privacy.there_is_no_list_no_map_and: There is no list, no map, and no directory of where agents are — not for other users, and not public. Your own placements are visible only to you, in your dashboard. Everyone else can find an agent only by being near it in person.

irl_privacy.when_on_people_viewing_the_same_area: When on, people viewing the same area see you as a coarse ghost marker snapped to a rough area. The anonymous presence count is shared either way; your precise location never is.
irl_privacy.when_others_come_across_an_agent_nearby: When others come across an agent nearby, they see an avatar at a spot — never your account, your device, or who placed it. Owner identity is stripped before anything leaves our servers.
irl_privacy.when_you_place_a_3d_agent_at: When you place a 3D agent at a real spot on IRL, it isn't broadcast to a feed or dropped on a public map. It becomes visible to someone only when they're physically standing next to it and point their camera. You discover agents by walking up to them — never by browsing where they are.

irl_privacy.while_you_re_using_irl_the_only: While you're using IRL, the only thing visible to nearby people is anonymous presence — and a coarse ghost, if you choose to turn it on. Your exact position never leaves your device.

launch_week.1_010_members_in_the_x_community:
1,010 members in the X community.
From zero. In a week.
launch_week.267_8k_impressions_25_3k_engagements_9: 267.8K impressions. 25.3K engagements. 9.4% engagement rate. 5.1K profile visits. 7.2K likes, 1.5K reposts, 845 replies, 198 bookmarks, 61 shares. Reply-to-like ratio: 11.7% — well into live-conversation territory. Verified followers: 359. Following: 11.
launch_week.a_real_time_3d_agent_runtime_on: A real-time 3D agent runtime on Three.js + glTF. Multi-provider chat (Claude, GPT, Groq, OpenRouter) with sentiment-driven emotion. Native Solana wallet integration. Pump.fun trading skills as agent tools. Reverse-engineered the entire pump-fun-agent-payments-sdk — Anchor IDL, PDAs, event parsing, x402 layer — now editable source. Solana vanity grinder. Pump.fun create-coin co-signer. Live pump.fun feed.
launch_week.a_week_of_building_in_public: A week of building in public
launch_week.anthropic_claude_openai_gpt_groq_openrou: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Groq, OpenRouter — all behind one chat interface with real-time streaming via Server-Sent Events. The agent reads user sentiment and reacts with emotion + animation. Function calls, MCP tool use, artifacts. 100% open source.
launch_week.april_29_2026_nichxbt_posted_three_ws: April 29, 2026. @nichxbt posted three.ws — the open-source platform for 3D AI agents that talk, remember, hold wallets, and mint on-chain. 135,000 views in the first 24 hours. Same day: npm package live, listed on Anthropic's MCP Registry, listed on x402scan as a paid endpoint, native Pump.fun trading skills shipped, Solana vanity address generator deployed, voice + X Spaces agent demo.
launch_week.asymmetric_posture_is_a_signal_following: Asymmetric posture is a signal. Following 11. Followed by 3,675. The numbers say: we are a publisher, not a follow-back farm. Verified followers (359, ~10%) skew toward power users — exactly the cohort that pays for, builds with, and amplifies what we ship next.
launch_week.beyond_the_analytics_dashboard_three_ws_: Beyond the analytics dashboard, three.ws landed on the directories, registries, and platforms that matter most for an open-source developer tool.
launch_week.cloud_infra_googlecloud_web3_startups_pr: Cloud + infra: @GoogleCloud (Web3 Startups program), @alibaba_cloud (Marketplace listing). Exchanges: @Coinbase + @CoinbaseWallet, @Bybit_Official, @JupiterExchange, @CoinGecko, @CoinMarketCap, Investing.com.

The May 7 RT from @zhusu (50K views) was earned by the work, not the brand handle. Use both — founder voice for narrative, brand for ecosystem announcements.

launch_week.elevenlabs_voice_cloning_from_3_10_secon: ElevenLabs voice cloning from 3–10 seconds of speech, persona extraction from a short onboarding interview, and consented memory seeding from connected accounts — the avatar isn't just you, the agent acts like you.

Solana attestations on six event types: feedback, validation, task offers, task acceptance, revocation, dispute. ERC-7710 scoped delegations — grant/revoke time-bound, amount-limited permissions. Full reputation crawl every 5 minutes via cron.

launch_week.on_april_29_2026_nichxbt_posted_somethin: On April 29, 2026, @nichxbt posted: "something I've wanted for a while: an AI that isn't just a text box." Attached was the launch of three.ws — the open-source platform for building, embedding, monetizing, and minting 3D AI agents on-chain. Viewer, runtime, identity, payments, marketplace, and a one-line embed — one stack, one repo.
launch_week.one_week_one_brand_new_account_every: One week. One brand-new account. Every interaction below was earned organically — no paid amplification, no bought followers.
launch_week.peak_day_was_may_5_46k_impressions: Peak day was May 5 — 46K impressions, ~1,200 new followers in 24 hours. Driven by the Solana Frontier Hackathon listing (42K views, 621 reposts), the Coinbase + Coinbase Wallet listing of $THREE (12K views), and Jupiter Exchange verification.
launch_week.press_culture_voguemagazine_photo_vogue_: Press + culture: @VogueMagazine Photo Vogue feature, @BuzzFeed profile, @amazonmusic + @Spotify podcast launch. Embed proof shipped into @Shopify.
launch_week.reply_ratio_like_ratio_845_replies_on: Reply ratio > like ratio. 845 replies on 7,200 likes is an 11.7% reply rate — well into "live conversation" territory. The 1,010-member X community is the asset that ratio builds. Likes are sentiment; replies are people who showed up to talk.
launch_week.reply_to_like_ratio_11_7_the: Reply-to-like ratio: 11.7%. The community shows up to talk, not just lurk. That's the number to optimize for in week two.
launch_week.reputation_markets_staking_on_agents_sig: Reputation markets staking on agents' signed action histories, EIP-7710 skill royalties paid to skill authors per-call, and agent-to-agent autonomous payments through delegated signer wallets.
launch_week.ship_daily_name_the_partner_of_the: Ship daily. Name the partner. Of the 64 posts in this window, the highest-engagement ones were either (a) "we just shipped X, here's the link" or (b) "@PartnerName picked us up." Roadmaps and teasers do not exist in the top 20 by views. Every meaningful spike was a real shipped artifact or a real organization saying our name.
launch_week.ship_daily_name_the_partner_reply_ratio: Ship daily. Name the partner. Reply ratio over like ratio. Be a publisher, not a follow-back farm. Cross-pollinate founder voice with brand handle. Crypto X is awake on the weekend — that's when the biggest posts hit.

launch_week.standards_ai_anthropicai_mcp_registry_pu: Standards + AI: @AnthropicAI MCP Registry, @PulseMCP, W3C membership (proposing a new "3D AI Agents & Identity" Community Group), @Solana Frontier Hackathon via @colosseum.
launch_week.the_custom_element_loads_lazily_on_inter: The <agent-3d> custom element loads lazily on intersection, supports five widget variants (turntable, animation gallery, talking agent, ERC-8004 passport card, hotspot tour), and emits Open Graph and oEmbed metadata so links unfurl with rich previews. A point-and-click Widget Studio generates copy-paste embed code. three.ws Studio is a full in-browser 3D avatar editor — load a GLB, edit skeleton + materials, export. The Marketplace + Skills Marketplace + Agent Reputation system make agents discoverable, monetizable, and rateable. Versioned CDN bundles ship at /agent-3d/x.y.z/.
launch_week.the_flywheel_is_real_apr_29_founder: The flywheel is real. Apr 29 founder launch (135K views) → npm publish + MCP Registry + x402scan listing same day → Google Cloud announcement Apr 30 → Pump.fun skills + reverse-engineered SDK same window → Alibaba + CoinGecko May 2 → Solana Hackathon May 4 (42K views, 621 RTs) → Coinbase + Jupiter + Investing.com all stacked into May 5 (the 46K-impression peak day). One post earns the next.
launch_week.the_google_cloud_announcement_was_the_si: The Google Cloud announcement was the single highest-engagement post of the week (~6.9K impressions, 263 likes, 24 reposts) and the cloud infrastructure backing the next phase of the platform.
launch_week.the_inside_the_3d_agent_web_podcast: The "Inside The 3D Agent Web" podcast episode is published on Amazon Music and the companion blog "Beyond Chatbots: Why Your AI Agent Needs a 3D Body" went out via the Spotify-on-chain ecosystem. Two more distribution surfaces, one more week.
launch_week.the_may_5_peak_46k_impressions_and: The May 5 peak — 46K impressions and roughly 1,200 new followers in 24 hours — was driven by the Solana Frontier Hackathon listing landing, the Coinbase listing announcement, and the Jupiter Exchange verification all dropping in the same window.
launch_week.the_next_web_has_agents_in_it: The next web has agents in it. They need identity, embodiment, and a way to transact. We're building the spec — and the product, the SDK, the marketplace, and the on-chain economy underneath it.
launch_week.the_platform_shipped_as_a_partner_listin: The platform shipped as a partner listing on Alibaba Cloud, our first cloud-marketplace distribution channel. The associated launch tweet pulled ~7.1K impressions on its own.
launch_week.the_post_reached_135_000_views_in: The post reached 135,000 views in under 24 hours. Within a week, @trythreews had gone from a fresh handle to a verified profile with 3,675 followers, three live x402 paid endpoints, two npm-published SDKs, partnerships with Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud, listings on Coinbase, Bybit, Jupiter, CoinGecko, and CoinMarketCap, and an entry in the Solana Frontier Hackathon.
launch_week.the_roadmap_closes_the_gap_from_use: The roadmap closes the gap from "use a 3D artist" to "take a selfie." Four phases, scoped end-to-end in the public README.
launch_week.the_thesis_build_a_real_product_ship: The thesis: Build a real product, ship something every day, name the partners as you land them. The flywheel takes care of the rest.
launch_week.the_three_ws_x_community_is_the: The three.ws X community is the gathered audience — developers, agent-curious builders, and a crew of folks following along live. It's where the next wave of agent owners will come from.
launch_week.three_live_paid_endpoints_solana_token_t: Three live paid endpoints: /api/x402/mint-to-mesh (Solana token → themed 3D avatar, $0.01 USDC), /api/x402/model-check (paid glTF validator), /api/insights/revenue-vision (Claude-powered agent strategy, $0.001 USDC). Auto-discoverable at /.well-known/x402.json. CDP facilitator with ES256 JWT auth. Multi-network: Base (eip155:8453), Arbitrum (eip155:42161), Solana.
launch_week.three_live_x402_paid_endpoints_mint_to: Three live x402 paid endpoints — mint-to-mesh, model-check, revenue-vision — auto-discoverable at /.well-known/x402.json. Two npm-published SDKs: @three-ws/sdk and @three-ws/agent-payments v3.1. ERC-8004 on-chain identity. ERC-7710 scoped delegations. Solana attestations on six event types.
launch_week.three_selfies_left_center_right_gpu_back: Three selfies (left, center, right), GPU-backed multi-view face reconstruction, and a rigged, animatable avatar minted as a draft ERC-8004 token in under sixty seconds. Mobile-first capture UX with realtime quality gates.
launch_week.three_ws: three.ws
launch_week.three_ws_is_organized_as_four_communicat: three.ws is organized as four communicating layers, plus a backend and a contracts package. Every layer is in production at three.ws and ships as part of the open-source repo. Here's the inventory.
launch_week.three_ws_is_published_as_on_registry: three.ws is published as io.github.nirholas/three.ws on registry.modelcontextprotocol.io and discoverable via PulseMCP's curated directory. Any MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop included) can connect and drive avatars over JSON-RPC.
launch_week.we_built_the_platform_that_gives_it: We built the platform that gives it one. In a week: a full 3D AI agent stack — viewer, runtime, on-chain identity, payments, embed, and marketplace — plus two npm SDKs, three live x402 endpoints, partnerships with Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud, listings on Coinbase, Bybit, Jupiter, and CoinGecko, a W3C seat, and a community of 1,010 builders. This is the receipt.
launch_week.webgl_2_0_rendering_with_full_gltf: WebGL 2.0 rendering with full glTF 2.0 / GLB support: Draco geometry compression, KTX2 texture compression, Meshopt mesh optimization, HDR environment maps, PBR materials, skinned animation, morph targets, and embedded cameras. Validation is line-level via the Khronos gltf-validator. Lip-sync analyser drives mouth morphs from the agent's voice in real time. Selfie capture + AvatarTurn integration generate playable avatars from a phone camera. Drag-and-drop loading, OrbitControls with configurable auto-rotation, and a real-time dat.GUI for live tweaking.
launch_week.webgl_viewer_llm_agent_runtime_erc_8004: WebGL viewer, LLM agent runtime, ERC-8004 identity contracts, OAuth 2.1 server, MCP endpoint, and the <agent-3d> web component — everything you read about above. Live at three.ws today.
launch_week.weekend_doesn_t_sleep_the_biggest_single: Weekend doesn't sleep. The biggest single day (May 5) was a Sunday. The biggest single post (Solana Hackathon, 42K views, 621 RTs) hit on a Saturday. Crypto X is awake when most marketing teams aren't. Ship on the weekend.
