motion.a_motion_is_a_handful_of_beats: A motion is a handful of beats: where the body is at one instant, how long it takes to get there, and how long it stays. Once you animate something, every beat shows up here and you can jump to it.
motion.a_score_not_a_keyframe_dump: A score, not a keyframe dump
motion.an_arm_is_not_two_bones_on: An arm is not two bones on a fixed socket. The clavicle swings toward a distant target, worth ten to fifteen centimetres of reach and most of what makes a reach read as a whole body reaching rather than an arm being extended.
motion.ankles_are_placed_in_world_space_against: Ankles are placed in world space against the ground. The hips are then free to drop, lean and turn, and the legs absorb it through inverse kinematics, which is exactly what a real body does and why a crouch here looks like a crouch.
motion.describe_a_movement_in_plain_language_kn: Describe a movement in plain language. Known movements answer instantly; anything else is written by a language model into the same score format.
motion.every_other_way_to_get_a_new: Every other way to get a new animation needs data you do not have: a capture stage, a licensed clip library, or a diffusion model trained on one. This needs a sentence, because a human body is a solved kinematics problem once somebody writes down where it should be and when.
motion.feet_meet_the_floor_not_the_hips: Feet meet the floor, not the hips
motion.how_a_sentence_becomes_a_body: How a sentence becomes a body
motion.is_the_same_compiler_this_page_runs: npm i @three-ws/motion is the same compiler this page runs, with zero dependencies and no renderer. Read the docs or hit the API directly.
motion.meta_description: Describe a movement in plain language and watch any 3D avatar perform it. No motion capture, no model weights: a kinematics solver reads a Motion Score and produces a real animation clip you can scrub, edit beat by beat, and export as GLB.
motion.meta_og_description: Type a sentence, get a real full-body animation. No mocap, no model weights, no download.
motion.meta_title: Motion Studio · Type a sentence, get an animation · three.ws
motion.meta_twitter_description: Type a sentence, get a real full-body animation. No mocap, no model weights, no download.
motion.no_motion_capture_no_model_weights_nothi: No motion capture, no model weights, nothing to download. Describe a movement and a kinematics solver works out the joint rotations for every frame: feet on the floor, weight over them, shoulders doing what shoulders do. Scrub it, edit any beat, and export a clip that plays on any humanoid rig.
motion.reverse_any_two_of_these_and_the: Reverse any two of these and the result is subtly wrong in a way that is impossible to fix downstream. Solve the arms before the torso and every gesture sits where the chest used to be.
motion.root_where_the_hips_are_which_everything:
root where the hips are, which everything below hangs from
turn the body's heading, so limbs solve in the turned frame
torso lean, twist and side-bend, shared along the spine
legs ankles placed in world space, so dropping the hips bends the knees
balance the hips nudged until the weight sits over the feet
arms wrists placed against anchors that ride the posed chest
hands shape, after the wrist is where it belongs
gaze last, so a look is relative to the chest it ended up on
motion.send_any_motion_to_the_animation_studio: Send any motion to the Animation Studio to keyframe over it, then save it to your account, play it back across the platform, or sell it.
motion.the_centre_of_mass_is_a_mass: The centre of mass is a mass-weighted sum over the segments that carry a body's weight, and the hips move until it sits over whichever feet are actually carrying weight. Lift one foot and the body shifts over the other on its own.
motion.the_clip_plays_on_any_humanoid_rig: The clip plays on any humanoid rig through the one-tag embed and the retargeter, which maps Mixamo, Avaturn, VRM, Unreal and Daz bone names onto the same canonical set.
motion.the_intermediate_format_is_anatomy_and_t: The intermediate format is anatomy and timing: posture: "crouch", arms.right.at: "chin", gaze: "aside". No bone names, no quaternions. That is what makes it writable by a language model, readable in a diff, and editable by hand in the box above.
motion.the_order_each_beat_is_solved_in: The order each beat is solved in
motion.the_same_score_compiles_to_the_same: The same score compiles to the same clip, byte for byte, forever. That is what lets a motion be cached at the edge, diffed in review, and pinned in a regression test.
motion.type_a_movement_above_or_pick_one: Type a movement above, or pick one of the examples.
motion.type_a_sentence_get_an_animation: Type a sentence. Get an animation.
motion.use_it_in_your_own_code: Use it in your own code
motion.weight_time_and_flow_pick_the_easing: Weight, time and flow pick the easing curve, scale the travel, and set how far a limb overshoots before it settles. It is what makes the same three shapes read as a wave, a swat, or a salute.

motion_swap.a_server_worker_tracks_your_body_pose: A server worker tracks your body pose in every frame and solves it onto the platform's canonical skeleton — the same retarget engine that drives every avatar animation here. It also segments you out into a mask.
motion_swap.any_rigged_humanoid_glb_works_one_you: Any rigged humanoid GLB works — one you generated, captured from a selfie, or rigged from a mesh.
motion_swap.drop_a_video_of_one_person: Drop a video of one person
motion_swap.meta_description: Upload a video of yourself and get it back with your 3D avatar performing your motion instead of you. Pose tracking, person masking, and avatar retargeting — composited and exported in your browser.
motion_swap.meta_og_description: Stay off camera without staying off video. Your avatar performs your motion, pinned frame-by-frame over you.
motion_swap.meta_og_title: Motion Swap — Replace Yourself in Video with Your Avatar · three.ws
motion_swap.meta_title: Motion Swap — Replace Yourself in Video with Your Avatar · three.ws
motion_swap.meta_twitter_description: Stay off camera without staying off video. Your avatar performs your motion, pinned frame-by-frame over you.
motion_swap.meta_twitter_title: Motion Swap — Replace Yourself in Video with Your Avatar · three.ws
motion_swap.mp4_mov_or_webm_up_to_256: MP4, MOV, or WebM up to 256 MB. The first 90 seconds are processed. Full body in frame tracks best.
motion_swap.the_source_video_is_processed_transientl: The source video is processed transiently and the pose data contains no imagery — the motion clip is just skeleton rotations.
motion_swap.tracking_your_pose_frame_by_frame_and: Tracking your pose frame-by-frame and masking you out. A 30-second clip takes about two minutes.
motion_swap.upload_a_video_of_yourself_a_house: Upload a video of yourself — a house tour, a product demo, a talking walk-through — and get it back with your 3D avatar performing your exact motion instead of you. Pose tracking runs server-side; you stay pixelated under the avatar. Compositing and export happen right here in your browser.
motion_swap.video_motion_capture_body_swap: Video motion capture · body swap
motion_swap.your_browser_then_plays_the_original_foo: Your browser then plays the original footage, pixelates you under the mask, and pins the avatar over you frame-by-frame, matching your position and size. Export records the composite with the original audio.
motion_swap.your_video_your_avatar_not_your_face: Your video. Your avatar. Not your face.

Then it walks the infrastructure that makes each of those claims real.

news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_body_problem_text_or_a_photo: The body problem: text or a photo becomes a textured mesh, then a humanoid skeleton, then retargeted animation that plays on a rig nobody hand-authored.

news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_wallet_problem_agents_hold_real_keys: The wallet problem: agents hold real keys and settle per call in USDC over HTTP 402, so buying a capability is a request rather than a signup form.
news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_world_problem_those_bodies_inhabit_p: The world problem: those bodies inhabit persistent multiplayer scenes rather than sitting alone in a single embed.

news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.an_open_source_mcp_server_for_watsonx: An open-source MCP server for watsonx.ai. @three-ws/ibm-watsonx-mcp exposes watsonx.ai — IBM Granite and any model in your account — to any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor) as five tools: chat, text generation, embeddings, tokenization, and model discovery.
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.behind_the_3d_body_is_a_brain: Behind the 3D body is a brain — and that brain can run on IBM watsonx.ai. The integration is real, in production, and open source, with no mock path. Two layers connect three.ws to watsonx:
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.both_layers_run_on_your_own_ibm: Both layers run on your own IBM Cloud credentials — an API key is exchanged for a short-lived IAM token and every inference call is scoped to your watsonx.ai project, with no three.ws intermediary between your agent and IBM. A 3D agent embedded on any page can reason on IBM Granite, running inside your own watsonx.ai project, governed by your IBM Cloud account.
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.embedding_a_persistent_on_chain_3d_agent: Embedding a persistent, on-chain 3D agent into any platform should be as easy as embedding a YouTube video. One <agent-3d> tag deploys a full agent — no install, no plugin, no native app — rendered in any modern browser over WebGL. What lands on the page is a character with a face, a voice, memory, emotion, and an on-chain identity that persists across platforms. The goal of that frictionless deployment: onboard the next millions of people to embodied AI without asking any of them to download anything.

The open-source platform for 3D AI agents on-chain is the first fully Web3-native ISV to join APN with a Solana / EVM on-chain identity stack. AWS Marketplace SaaS listing shipping next.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.meta_twitter_title: three.ws Joins the AWS Partner Network
news_joined_aws_partner_network.pro_and_enterprise_tiers_per_agent_and: Pro and Enterprise tiers. Per-agent and per-inference metered pricing. SaaS Contracts via Private Offer for enterprise customers.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.the_aws_marketplace_channel_apn_software: The AWS Marketplace channel. APN Software Path members are eligible to list as SaaS products on AWS Marketplace, giving AWS customers a procurement path with consolidated billing, AWS credits, and EDP commit. The three.ws SaaS listing is in development.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.the_aws_marketplace_integration_is_alrea: The AWS Marketplace integration is already in the codebase at api/aws-marketplace — ResolveCustomer for fulfillment, signed SNS webhooks for subscription lifecycle, metered usage reporting, and contract entitlement checks.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.the_aws_partner_network_is_the_global: The AWS Partner Network is the global community of organizations building, marketing, and selling solutions on AWS. Membership in the Software Path is AWS's formal recognition that a company ships software products to AWS customers.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.the_full_three_ws_stack_is_open: The full three.ws stack is open source under Apache 2.0: github.com/nirholas/three.ws
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_home_news_rss_x_github: © three.ws · Home · News · RSS · X · GitHub
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_an_open_source_stack: three.ws is an open-source stack for autonomous 3D AI agents that run natively in the browser. Every <agent-3d> tag deploys an agent with a Solana NFT identity (Metaplex Core), an ERC-8004 wallet on EVM, a browser-native 3D body in WebGL via three.js, a Claude-powered LLM brain, and native x402 / HTTP 402 payments in USDC on Base, BSC, and Solana.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_apache_2_0_from: three.ws is Apache 2.0 from top to bottom — viewer, runtime, identity contracts, backend. AWS customers can audit the entire stack, fork it, and run their own deployment if they want full control. The platform is also already live on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace and listed in BNB Chain Dappbay, the Model Context Protocol Registry, and x402scan — AWS joins a deliberate multi-cloud distribution strategy.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_now_an_aws_partner: three.ws is now an AWS Partner. The platform has been enrolled in the AWS Partner Network (APN) Software Path as a Technology Partner — the official designation for independent software vendors building products for AWS customers.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_the_first_fully_on: three.ws is the first fully on-chain 3D AI agent platform in the AWS Partner Network. Every <agent-3d> tag the platform produces is a Solana-minted, ERC-8004-walleted, x402-payable autonomous actor — and that stack is now part of AWS's partner ecosystem.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_joins_the_aws_partner_network: three.ws Joins the AWS Partner Network
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_s_production_infrastructure_alr: three.ws's production infrastructure already runs on AWS us-east-1 and is registered in AWS MyApplications for unified cost and operations monitoring. The path from "we run on AWS" to "we're an AWS Partner" is the formalization of a technical alignment that's been in production for months.

news_text_to_3d_is_live.forge_is_live_on_three_ws_type: Forge is live on three.ws. news_text_to_3d_is_live.text_3d_runs_a_two_stage_pipeline: Text→3D runs a two-stage pipeline: the prompt is rendered into a reference image by a state-of-the-art image model, then lifted into full textured geometry by TRELLIS, a 3D reconstruction model. The output is a GLB — the open standard that loads in Blender, Unity, Unreal, three.js, and every major 3D tool. Quality tiers (Draft / Standard / High) trade speed for fidelity, and builders with their own Meshy or Tripo API key can plug it in — the key stays in the browser.

nvidia_index.generating_3d_used_to_require_a_workstat: Generating 3D used to require a workstation, a licence, and a skill you spent years acquiring. The reason a visitor can now type a sentence on a school laptop and get a real, textured, riggable model back for nothing is not one famous model getting good. It is an entire supporting cast getting good and getting free at the same time, most of it hosted by NVIDIA behind a single key. GPU capacity is the one hard constraint on how fast and how detailed that gets, which is exactly the constraint Inception helps relax.

oracle-lab.ladder_h: Does each tier earn what it claims
oracle-lab.ladder_sub: The score line is not a percentage: 86 claims a 45% chance, not an 86% one. Each rung is a public promise about measured frequency, so here is the promise next to the measurement, on launches the model never saw. A model whose top band stops clearing its own claim is refused by the promotion gate rather than shipped.
oracle-lab.lede: The Oracle watches every pump.fun launch for its first ninety seconds and scores it. This page is the machine that makes the score, not a summary of it: every bucket weight with the number of labeled launches behind it, what actually happened to those launches, the reliability curve it earned on data it had never seen, and the full history of every version it has tried, including the ones that were refused.
oracle-lab.lede2: It is a lookup table, roughly 32KB. Download it and you can reproduce any score we have ever published, offline, with no key.
oracle-lab.meta_desc: The Oracle's conviction model, published in full: every bucket weight with the sample count behind it, held-out reliability curves, the version history of what the machine learned and when, and a live scorer you can drive by hand.
oracle-lab.og_desc: Every weight, every sample count, every version. Download the model and reproduce any score offline.
oracle-lab.registry_h: What it has learned, and when
oracle-lab.registry_sub: The model refits every six hours and only takes over if it beats the incumbent on held-out ranking. Refused candidates are listed here too, with the reason: a registry that shows only the winners is a highlight reel, not a record.
oracle-lab.scorer_sub: Every control below feeds the real weights, in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere. This is the same arithmetic that scores the live feed.
oracle-lab.scoring_sub: The exact model this platform is using this second, with the numbers it earned on launches held out of its own training.
oracle-lab.twitter_desc: The Oracle's conviction model in full: every bucket weight with the number of labeled launches behind it and what happened to them, the held-out reliability curve for each tier, the version history of every refit including the ones that were refused, and a live scorer that runs the real weights in your browser. Download it and reproduce any score offline.
oracle-lab.twitter_title: Oracle Lab: the model, published · three.ws
oracle-lab.use_note: verify() is the important one. Feed it launches with outcomes you collected yourself and it re-measures our AUC, Brier score and reliability curve on your data. If our published numbers do not survive an independent sample, you should be able to find that out from us.
oracle-lab.use_sub: Zero dependencies. Node, Deno, Bun, Workers, browser. One request, then it is local arithmetic forever.
oracle-lab.weights_h: Every weight, and the evidence for it
oracle-lab.weights_sub: One row per bucket. Log-odds is what that bucket adds to the score. Win, rug and run are what actually happened to the launches in it, and n is how many there were. A claim with a small n is a weak claim, and you can see which is which.

oracle_docs.a_conviction_score_is_a_probabilistic_cl: A conviction score is a probabilistic claim, and a probabilistic claim is worthless unless it's checked against reality. Oracle joins every verdict to its ground-truth outcome and publishes the result on the page — including when the edge is thin. This is the part that separates a model from a vibe.
oracle_docs.a_dynamic_1200_630_opengraph_conviction_: A dynamic 1200×630 OpenGraph conviction card (SVG) for sharing a coin.

oracle_docs.a_high_score_is_the_weight_of: A high score is the weight of on-chain evidence, not a guarantee. pump.fun is adversarial and heavy-tailed — most launches fail, and even a calibrated edge loses often. Read the tier as odds, size accordingly, and never bet what you can't lose.
oracle_docs.a_long_lived_node_process_running_three: A long-lived Node process running three independent loops — score (keep verdicts warm), agent (act on armed watches), and settle (grade outcomes) — each self-scheduling so a slow pass never blocks a fast one.
oracle_docs.a_model_you_can_only_trust_when: A model you can only trust when it flatters you is useless. Here is what Oracle cannot do, where it can be wrong, and how it's hardened.
oracle_docs.a_pump_fun_coin_that_completed_its: A pump.fun coin that completed its bonding curve — the canonical success event.
oracle_docs.a_pure_side_effect_free_scoring_function: A pure, side-effect-free scoring function (convict()) plus a defensive data-assembly layer. Given a mint, it returns a score, tier, pillar breakdown, and reasons. No I/O during scoring — fully testable.
oracle_docs.a_scored_coin_is_a_win_if: A scored coin is a win if it graduated, or reached a ≥2× ATH multiple without rugging; a loss if it rugged or languished below 1.2×; flat in between. The "without rugging" clause matters: bundled launches routinely spike 2× from first sight before collapsing, and counting those wicks as wins would let pump-and-dumps inflate the very number that's supposed to expose them. Only resolved coins count toward a win rate — open positions are excluded, so the number can't be inflated by undecided bets.
oracle_docs.a_single_long_lived_node_process_runs: A single long-lived Node process runs three independent, self-scheduling loops. They share nothing but the database, so a slow scoring pass never delays an agent acting, and a stuck confirmation never freezes scoring.

oracle_docs.conviction_is_the_weighted_fusion_of_fou: Conviction is the weighted fusion of four independent reads. Each pillar is scored 0–100 on its own, for its own reasons, and contributes a fixed share of the final number.
oracle_docs.conviction_weighted_size_the_executor_th: Conviction-weighted size: size = base · (1 + clamp((score − min)/(100 − min), 0, 1)·0.5). The executor then applies the absolute ceiling: size = min(size, ORACLE_MAX_TRADE_SOL) — a guardian limit that overrides any per-agent setting.

oracle_docs.each_tier_s_realized_win_rate_is: Each tier's realized win rate is shown with a 95% Wilson confidence interval — the right tool for win-rate estimates on small samples, where a naïve ± would lie. A wide band means "not enough data yet," and the page says so.
oracle_docs.every_action_an_agent_takes_simulated_or: Every action an agent takes — simulated or live — is graded against ground truth and lands in its permanent win-rate ledger. This is what makes an agent's track record verifiable instead of asserted.
oracle_docs.every_field_here_is_also_available_progr: Every field here is also available programmatically from GET /api/oracle/coin?mint=… — see the API reference.
oracle_docs.every_new_wallet_judged_and_every_new: Every new wallet judged and every new launch resolved sharpens the WHO pillar and tightens the bands. The data flywheel is the moat — coverage compounds into calibration.
oracle_docs.every_one_of_those_facts_is_on: Every one of those facts is on-chain or one inference away from it. The bottleneck has never been availability — it is assembly and speed. No human watches every wallet across every launch and fuses it into a decision in seconds. A machine can.
oracle_docs.every_scored_coin_as_a_glowing_sphere: Every scored coin as a glowing sphere in a force-directed, category-clustered 3D field; size and color encode conviction and tier.
oracle_docs.every_section_opens_in_plain_english_wha: Every section opens in plain English: what it is, why it exists, and how to use it. If you only read the prose, you will understand the whole system and never see a formula you didn't ask for.
oracle_docs.everything_on_the_page_is_a_public: Everything on the page is a public endpoint. Reads are JSON, cached at the CDN and rate-limited per IP; live views are Server-Sent Events. Agent-config endpoints require auth scoped to the agent owner.
oracle_docs.finds_open_actions_whose_coin_now_has: Finds open actions whose coin now has a resolved outcome, grades each win/loss/flat, marks PnL to market, and closes the learning loop.
oracle_docs.finds_recent_launches_that_are_new_or: Finds recent launches that are new or stale (last scored >3 min ago), scores each — assemble → classify → fuse → persist — and appends history on material change. Keeps the cache warm.
oracle_docs.five_brain_tables_feed_every_score_oracl: Five brain tables feed every score. Oracle queries each one defensively — a missing or younger table degrades the affected pillar gracefully rather than failing the whole verdict.
oracle_docs.for_each_armed_watch_evaluates_freshly_s: For each armed watch, evaluates freshly-scored coins against the agent's bar and budget, executes a buy when the gates pass, and fires alerts. Dedups so an agent never acts twice on one coin.
oracle_docs.for_every_armed_agent_on_every_freshly: For every armed agent, on every freshly-scored coin, a pure decision function runs a sequence of gates. If any gate blocks, the agent passes; if all clear, it sizes and buys.

oracle_docs.full_intel_for_one_mint_conviction_pilla: Full intel for one mint — conviction, pillars, reasons, narrative, outcome, and the who's-in trader roster. Scores fresh (with LLM) on a cache miss.
oracle_docs.global_kpis_per_category_intel_symbol_se: Global KPIs, per-category intel, symbol search, the agent leaderboard, a single agent's record, and the global action feed.
oracle_docs.go_straight_to_the_edge_win_rate: Go straight to The edge. Win rate by tier with 95% confidence bands, a calibration ladder, and a Brier score — shown even when the edge is thin. Proof, not promises.
oracle_docs.here_is_the_coin_drawer_the_product: Here is the coin drawer the product shows when you click any launch. It is the score, fully unpacked — the same object the API returns, rendered for a human.

oracle_docs.if_the_conviction_cache_is_empty_fresh: If the conviction cache is empty (fresh deploy), the feed endpoint scores a handful of recent coins on the spot — database-only, no LLM — so the UI is never blank while the score loop catches up. Every brain query is wrapped so a missing table yields a null slice, not a crashed pass.

oracle_docs.learned_weights_and_a_calibrated_probabi: Learned weights and a calibrated probability shipped in v2; the six-hourly refit behind a promotion gate shipped in v3. The next lever is the additive assumption itself: interaction terms or shallow trees over the same buckets, since the strongest observed patterns (holder concentration crossed with buyer count) are plausibly interactive and a sum of one-hot weights cannot express them.
oracle_docs.let_a_launch_be_a_feature_vector: Let a launch be a feature vector x. Oracle computes four pillar functions f_k(x) ∈ [0,100] for k ∈ {ped, str, nar, mom}, a weighted score, and a capped, clamped output:
oracle_docs.lifecycle_a_coin_must_be_actually_first: Lifecycle: a coin must be ≥… actually first-seen and within a 12h window to enter scoring; it's scored, classified, and cached; rescored when stale (every ~3 min if new data arrives); its history appended on material change; quote/stablecoin mints (USDC, wSOL, …) are excluded and purged. Nothing about a score decays purely with time — the engine is event-driven, reacting to new wallet activity, not a clock.
oracle_docs.live_conviction_feed_scored_coins_with_p: Live conviction feed — scored coins with pillars, badges, category, sparkline; plus a tier-level backtest summary. Filters: tier, category, min_score, limit, network.
oracle_docs.live_market_half_of_the_coin_page: Live market half of the coin page for one mint — price + 5m/1h/6h/24h changes, market cap, FDV, liquidity, 24h volume, holders, supply, bonding-curve progress, security (mint/freeze authority, mutable metadata, transfer fee, top-10 concentration), DEX pairs, ATH/ATL for listed coins, and every social/explorer link. Fused live across DexScreener, pump.fun, GeckoTerminal, GoPlus, Birdeye and CoinGecko.
oracle_docs.live_routing_builds_buy_instructions_via: Live routing builds buy instructions via the pump SDK with 10% slippage, fetches a fresh blockhash, and either sends a raw transaction (skip-preflight off, up to 3 retries, 60s confirm race) or, when Jito is enabled, prepends a small tip transfer to a rotating tip account and submits the pair as a bundle to the block-engine endpoint. The action is written as filled with the signature (or jito:<bundleId>), skipped if the agent has no wallet, or failed on any on-chain error — never silently dropped.
oracle_docs.live_trades_streams_the_coin_s_buys: Live trades streams the coin's buys and sells in real time, each annotated with the trader's wallet archetype.
oracle_docs.loss_the_coin_rugged_or_marked_below: Loss — the coin rugged, or marked below 0.5× / peaked below 1.2×. Loss conditions outrank a peak-based win: a 2× wick on a position now at zero was exit liquidity, not a win.
oracle_docs.machine_ready_a_buy_watch_skip_recommend: Machine-ready. A buy/watch/skip recommendation with confidence and a size factor, per mint or as the top N plays — built for agent polling.

oracle_docs.numbers_and_thresholds_quoted_here_are_t: Numbers and thresholds quoted here are the real production constants from the engine. Tier names are prime · strong · lean · watch · avoid. Pillars are nicknamed WHO (pedigree), HOW (structure), WHAT (narrative), MOVE (momentum) throughout the product and these docs.
oracle_docs.one_number_for_overall_calibration_error: One number for overall calibration error — the mean squared error of (score/100) against the binary outcome. Lower is better; 0 is perfect, 0.25 is a coin flip.
oracle_docs.one_of_the_four_independent_reads_who: One of the four independent reads: WHO (pedigree), HOW (structure), WHAT (narrative), MOVE (momentum).
oracle_docs.one_verdict_fully_unpacked_conviction_35: One verdict, fully unpacked. Conviction 35 (watch): the WHO/HOW/WHAT/MOVE pillars across the top, a plain-English “why this score” list, the structure read (organic-buy vs bundle), the who's-in wallet roster, and a live trade tape — all for a single launch.
oracle_docs.open_the_feed_sort_by_conviction_click: Open the feed, sort by conviction, click any coin. The drawer shows the four pillars and a plain-English reason for every point. A high score is an argument, not a promise — read the reasons.
oracle_docs.operational_safeguards_layer_up_a_global: Operational safeguards layer up: a global kill switch, a hard per-trade SOL cap enforced in the executor (independent of any per-agent setting), per-watch daily-spend and open-position caps, a 60-second confirmation timeout so stuck transactions don't block the loop, and a 60-second cache on decrypted keypairs to bound decryption overhead during bursts. Simulate is the default — the worker logs realistic actions with zero spend unless explicitly switched to live.
oracle_docs.oracle_as_a_calibrated_scoring_classifie: Oracle as a calibrated scoring classifier
oracle_docs.oracle_is_a_thin_fast_conviction_layer: Oracle is a thin, fast conviction layer on top of a full-coverage pump.fun data brain. It does not re-ingest the chain — it reads the brain's tables, adds two things the brain doesn't have (cultural narrative and an action loop), and closes the loop against outcomes.
oracle_docs.oracle_is_an_analytics_and_automation_to: Oracle is an analytics and automation tool. Conviction scores, signals, and agent actions are informational. Live trading risks real funds; simulate first, cap hard, and treat every number as one input among many.
oracle_docs.oracle_owns_five_tables_classified_story: Oracle owns five tables: oracle_narrative (classified story + virality), oracle_conviction (the live verdict cache, one row per mint), oracle_conviction_history (score time-series, written only on a ≥3-point change, 72h retention), oracle_agent_watch (armed-agent config), and oracle_watch_actions (the action ledger). Full columns in the data model.
oracle_docs.oracle_owns_five_tables_the_verdict_cach: Oracle owns five tables. The verdict cache is the heart; the rest are history, config, and the action ledger.
oracle_docs.oracle_reads_every_pump_fun_launch_the: Oracle reads every pump.fun launch the moment it appears and answers one question: how much conviction does the on-chain evidence actually support? It fuses four independent reads — who is buying, how the launch is structured, what story it rides, and how it is moving — into a single transparent 0–100 score, then lets your 3D agent act on the plays that clear your bar. This is the complete reference: the thesis, the exact math, the data, the evidence, the API, the limits, and where it goes next.
oracle_docs.oracle_reads_from_a_separate_full_covera: Oracle reads from a separate full-coverage data brain rather than touching the chain itself. The brain ingests pump.fun and maintains the reputation graph; Oracle assembles, classifies, and fuses. The separation is what keeps scoring a pure, fast function.
oracle_docs.oracle_s_wager_is_that_a_transparent: Oracle's wager is that a transparent, calibrated fusion of who / how / what / move beats both gut instinct and any single indicator, because the failure modes are independent. A great story (WHAT) cannot save a launch where the dev already sold (HOW). A pile of smart-money wallets (WHO) means little if they are already trimming (also WHO). Fusing independent reads cancels noise and surfaces the rare launch where every axis agrees.
oracle_docs.oracle_the_conviction_engine_end_to_end: Oracle — the conviction engine, end to end
oracle_docs.oracle_turns_the_full_on_chain_footprint: Oracle turns the full on-chain footprint of a launch into one transparent, continuously-calibrated conviction score — and then lets an agent act on it within hard limits, grading itself against the outcome every time.
oracle_docs.outcome_grades_win_graduated_or_2_ath: Outcome grades: win = graduated or ≥2× ATH; loss = rugged or <1.2×; flat = in between.
oracle_docs.pedigree_reputation_earned_with_a_cold_s: Pedigree: reputation earned, with a cold-start prior
oracle_docs.per_wallet_buy_sell_lamports_is_creator: per-wallet buy/sell lamports, is_creator, funder (cluster source)
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_buyers_strongly_ou: Plain-English drivers: buyers strongly outnumbering sellers, a rapid pile-in of unique early buyers, and a dev who put a sensible amount of skin in the game all lift the score. Heavy early selling cuts it, and an oversized dev buy is read as a honeypot risk and penalized.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_each_category_carr: Plain-English drivers: each category carries a prior (how durable that kind of story tends to be), and the model's virality estimate is blended with that prior, weighted by the model's own confidence. A confidently-viral culture coin scores high; an unclassifiable one is treated with caution. It's the lightest pillar on purpose — a story is a multiplier on a real launch, not a substitute for one.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_many_unique_early_: Plain-English drivers: many unique early buyers and low concentration push the score up. Bundles, a top wallet holding half the supply, 70% of volume sniped in the first seconds, armies of freshly-funded wallets, or a dev who already sold all push it down — and the worst of these cap the whole coin in the 38–55 range regardless of pedigree.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_more_proven_wallet: Plain-English drivers: more proven wallets in is better; a large share of the buy volume coming from proven money is better; a creator who has shipped graduated launches before is better. Conversely, flagged wallets, smart money already selling, and a creator with a rug pattern all cut the score — and a serial rugger caps it outright.
oracle_docs.point_a_3d_agent_at_the_conviction: Point a 3D agent at the conviction stream, set your bar and caps, and let it act — in simulate mode for free, or live with hard spend limits. Every action is graded against the outcome.
oracle_docs.position_size_is_the_agent_s_base: Position size is the agent's base per-trade amount, optionally scaled by conviction — up to 1.5× as the score climbs from the agent's minimum toward 100 — so the agent leans harder into the strongest plays without ever exceeding its caps.
oracle_docs.prefer_to_integrate_every_number_on_the: Prefer to integrate? Every number on the page is a public endpoint — jump to the API reference. Agents can poll /api/oracle/signal for a machine-ready buy/watch/skip recommendation.
oracle_docs.proof_not_promises_win_rate_by_tier: Proof, not promises. Win rate by tier with 95% confidence bands, and a calibration ladder plotting realized win rate against what each score band predicts. Snapshot from the live edge tab on 2026-06-30 — a low-conviction window, shown honestly rather than cherry-picked.
oracle_docs.proof_over_promises_every_verdict_is_che: Proof over promises. Every verdict is checked against ground truth — did it graduate, rug, or run — and the realized win rate, with confidence bands, is published on the page. When the edge is thin, the page says so.
oracle_docs.pump_fun_mints_thousands_of_tokens_a: pump.fun mints thousands of tokens a day. Almost all go to zero. The few that run, run violently. The entire game is a signal-extraction problem under extreme time pressure — and the edge is not a secret indicator, it is coverage.
oracle_docs.read_or_arm_an_agent_s_watch: Read or arm an agent's watch config — bar, sizing, caps, filters, mode. Server-side validation clamps every limit.
oracle_docs.read_the_reasons_not_just_the_number: Read the reasons, not just the number
oracle_docs.realized_pnl_is_marked_to_market_as: Realized PnL is marked to market as size · (current_mc / entry_mc − 1), and an agent's summary rolls up total, wins, losses, win rate, realized PnL, and ROI. The same grading powers the public agent leaderboard and the platform-wide activity floor, so every agent competes on a level, outcome-graded field.
oracle_docs.recommendations_map_from_tier_prime_stro: Recommendations map from tier: prime → buy/high/1.0, strong → buy/medium/0.75, lean → watch, watch/avoid → skip. Reads are cached 3s with stale-while-revalidate, so polling is cheap.
oracle_docs.reliability_calibration_ladder_partition: Reliability (calibration ladder): partition scores into bins B_j; plot empirical ŷ_j = (1/|B_j|)Σ 1[win] against the bin's predicted rate. Perfect calibration ⇒ ŷ_j ≈ s̄_j/100 for all j (the identity line).
oracle_docs.responsive_by_default_the_full_engine_on: Responsive by default. The full engine, on a phone.
oracle_docs.returns_a_recommendation_an_agent_can_ac: GET /api/oracle/signal?mint=… returns a recommendation an agent can act on directly:
oracle_docs.returns_the_is_a_hard_ceiling_on: Returns { score, reasons[], cap }. The cap is a hard ceiling on the final fused score — the mechanism by which a serial rugger can never produce a "prime" coin no matter how good the other pillars look. A wallet counts as "proven" if it is labelled smart_money/kol or carries a reputation score ≥70.
oracle_docs.round_clamp_to_the_0_100_integer: # round + clamp to the 0–100 integer line
oracle_docs.send_a_test_telegram_alert_to_verify: Send a test Telegram alert to verify setup.
oracle_docs.simulate_the_default_logs_a_realistic_ac: Simulate (the default) logs a realistic action — same gates, same sizing, same grading — but spends nothing, so an agent can build a verifiable paper track record before a cent is at risk. Live decrypts the agent's wallet, builds a pump.fun buy with slippage protection, optionally routes through a Jito bundle for MEV protection, confirms on-chain, and records the signature. Both paths write to the same ledger and are graded identically by the settle loop.
oracle_docs.smart_money_is_not_a_hard_coded: "Smart money" is not a hard-coded list — it is continuously re-earned from outcomes in the wallet_reputation graph. For wallets the brain hasn't judged yet, Oracle seeds a cold-start prior from a curated known-wallet set (sourced from public KOL/wallet intelligence), so a brand-new coin still gets a useful pedigree read on its first scoring pass. Precedence is always earned reputation > prior > unproven.
oracle_docs.smart_money_score_smart_wallet_count_pro: smart_money_score, smart_wallet_count, proven/total buy lamports, notable[]
oracle_docs.so_high_model_confidence_leans_on_the: So high model confidence leans on the virality estimate; low confidence falls back toward the category prior. With no estimate, score = prior. A news coin adds the reason "fast but fragile"; an unknown coin adds "treat with caution."
oracle_docs.streams_poll_the_database_today_for_serv: Streams poll the database today for serverless simplicity. Event-driven push (LISTEN/NOTIFY or a log tail) cuts verdict-to-screen latency toward the block, which on pump.fun is the whole game.
oracle_docs.structure_and_pedigree_can_veto_the_lowe: # structure (and pedigree) can veto — the lowest cap wins
oracle_docs.structure_wallet_graph_buy_pattern_expos: Structure / wallet-graph / buy-pattern expose the raw HOW inputs (organic-buy %, bundle %, the funder graph) so you can audit the guardrail.
oracle_docs.subscribe_a_telegram_chat_to_an_agent: Subscribe a Telegram chat to an agent's conviction signals.
oracle_docs.symbol_name_image_category_creator_bundl: symbol, name, image, category, creator, bundle_score, organic_score, snipe_ratio, fresh_wallet_ratio, concentration_top10, bubblemap_connectivity, risk_flags, buy/sell counts, dev buy/sold
oracle_docs.the_0_34_0_30_0_18: The 0.34 / 0.30 / 0.18 / 0.18 weights and every threshold are hand-set from domain knowledge, not yet learned from outcomes. That's a deliberate, transparent starting point — and the single biggest opportunity, covered next.
oracle_docs.the_95_confidence_band_on_a_win: The 95% confidence band on a win-rate estimate, correct for small samples.
oracle_docs.the_agent_is_already_at_its_concurrency: the agent is already at its concurrency cap
oracle_docs.the_agent_leaderboard_armed_agents_ranke: The agent leaderboard — armed agents ranked by their outcome-graded record.
oracle_docs.the_architecture_pure_scoring_over_a_cov: The architecture — pure scoring over a coverage brain, behind a cached API, with a closed outcome loop — was chosen because it extends along several axes at once without a rewrite.
oracle_docs.the_backtest_win_rate_by_tier_calibratio: The backtest — win rate by tier, calibration, Brier, edge multiple.
oracle_docs.the_base_is_anchored_to_the_brain: The base is anchored to the brain's organic-demand score: base = 30 + organic·0.55 (so structure alone lives in ~30–85), or a neutral 62 when organic isn't available. Then a battery of red-flag checks subtract and, for the severe ones, set a hard ceiling.
oracle_docs.the_bet_fuse_full_coverage_data_into: The bet: fuse full-coverage data into one honest number
oracle_docs.the_biggest_lever_replace_the_hand_set: The biggest lever. Replace the hand-set pillar weights with weights fit to outcomes (logistic regression / gradient boosting on the same features), and post-process the raw score through Platt scaling or isotonic regression so the number is the probability. The backtest infrastructure to measure the gain already exists.
oracle_docs.the_blob_on_each_conviction_row_is: The components blob on each conviction row is a full audit trail of the normalized inputs that produced the score — the reproducibility guarantee in storage form.
oracle_docs.the_cap_step_is_the_whole_philosophy: The cap step is the whole philosophy in one line: pillars add up, but a serious red flag in HOW (or a rugger creator in WHO) sets a ceiling the average cannot exceed. A coin with stellar pedigree and a bundle flag does not average out to "pretty good" — it is capped at ~46 and lands in watch, exactly where it belongs.
oracle_docs.the_coarse_band_a_score_falls_in: The coarse band a score falls in: prime / strong / lean / watch / avoid.
oracle_docs.the_default_feed_every_launch_in_the: The default feed — every launch in the last 12h, scored, filterable by tier/category/min-score, sortable by score/hot/new, with a conviction-breadth bar and per-card pillar breakdown + sparkline.
oracle_docs.the_fair_launch_guardrail_also_imposes_h: — the fair-launch guardrail; also imposes hard ceilings.
oracle_docs.the_final_integer_maps_to_one_of: The final integer maps to one of five tiers. Tiers are how humans skim the feed and how agents set a bar.
oracle_docs.the_first_seconds_of_a_launch_are: The first seconds of a launch are data-poor. Pedigree and momentum need wallets to show up before they say much; a brand-new coin leans on structure and a category prior. Scores sharpen as the footprint fills in — which is exactly why history and movers exist.
oracle_docs.the_formal_view_for_readers_who_want: The formal view, for readers who want the model stated as a model.
oracle_docs.the_four_pillar_bars_who_how_what: The four pillar bars — WHO / HOW / WHAT / MOVE — are the sub-scores from the section above. The big number is their capped, weighted fusion.
oracle_docs.the_four_pillar_scores_collapse_into_one: The four pillar scores collapse into one number by a weighted average — then the structural and pedigree caps clamp it down, it rounds, and it lands in a tier.
oracle_docs.the_four_things_the_backtest_publishes: The four things the backtest publishes
oracle_docs.the_fused_0_100_score_the_weight: The fused 0–100 score — the weight of on-chain evidence that a launch will win.
oracle_docs.the_how_pillar_is_a_guardrail_against: The HOW pillar is a guardrail against known manipulation — bundles, fresh-wallet farms, funder clusters — but launderers iterate. New evasion patterns are caught by the outcome loop (they rug, reputation updates) before they're caught by a rule. The defense is the closed loop, not any single check.
oracle_docs.the_intended_semantics_is_that_where_cal: The intended semantics is that s(x)/100 ≈ P(win | x), where win = graduated ∨ ATH ≥ 2×. Calibration measures the gap between intent and reality.
oracle_docs.the_live_floor_every_agent_action_simula: The live floor — every agent action, simulated or live, as it happens.
oracle_docs.the_live_oracle_is_eight_views_over: The live Oracle is eight views over one engine. Every state — loading, empty, error, populated — is designed; the empty states below are the real product telling you what's coming, not bugs.
oracle_docs.the_live_surface_every_launch_in_the: The live surface. Every launch in the last 12 hours, scored and ranked, with a live conviction-breadth bar and per-narrative averages. three.ws/oracle
oracle_docs.the_lowest_cap_triggered_wins_this_is: The lowest cap triggered wins. This is the formal statement of "structure is a veto": a launch with a serious structural defect is ceiling-limited before the weighted average is taken, so no amount of pedigree or narrative lifts it into a high tier.
oracle_docs.the_machine_ready_endpoint_and_the_actio: The machine-ready /signal endpoint and the action loop make Oracle a primitive other agents build on — discoverable, payable, and composable across the three.ws agent economy and MCP.
oracle_docs.the_pedigree_graph_made_browsable_every_: The pedigree graph, made browsable. Every wallet Oracle has judged, ranked by track record — early-buy win rate against dump/rug behavior. This is the raw material the WHO pillar reads. Top wallets tab
oracle_docs.the_pedigree_leaderboard_every_judged_wa: The pedigree leaderboard — every judged wallet ranked by track record.
oracle_docs.the_pillars_are_venue_agnostic_who_how: The pillars are venue-agnostic — who/how/what/move generalize to any launch venue with on-chain footprints. The brain abstraction is the seam where a new chain plugs in.
oracle_docs.the_problem_asymmetric_information_at_th: The problem: asymmetric information at the speed of a block
oracle_docs.the_product_is_keyboard_driven_focuses_s: The product is keyboard-driven (<kbd>/</kbd> focuses search, number keys jump tabs, arrows move between them), fully responsive, and built on a monochrome cool-gray palette where lightness encodes strength — brighter is stronger conviction.
oracle_docs.the_proven_wins_gallery_ordered_by_ath: The proven-wins gallery, ordered by ATH multiple, with a summary.
oracle_docs.the_question_is_real_buying_pressure_act: The question: is real buying pressure actually showing up, right now? Momentum reads the earliest footprint — the buy/sell balance, how fast unique buyers are piling in, and the size of the dev's own buy as a tell.
oracle_docs.the_question_is_this_a_fair_launch: The question: is this a fair launch or an engineered one? Structure is the guardrail. It reads the distribution and timing of the launch — bundle likelihood, holder concentration, snipe pressure, fresh-wallet farming, single-funder clusters, dev selling — and rewards broad, organic bases while punishing coordination and concentration.
oracle_docs.the_question_what_is_this_coin_about: The question: what is this coin about, and does the story have cultural legs? Narrative classifies the launch into one of eleven categories (meme, ai, culture, news, animal, celebrity, political, community, tech, utility, unknown) and estimates its virality — preferentially with a language model that is given live crypto headlines so it can recognize a coin riding today's news.
oracle_docs.the_question_who_is_already_in_this: The question: who is already in this coin, and what is their record? Pedigree rewards launches where wallets with a proven history of getting into winners early are already buying — and penalizes the presence of known ruggers, dumpers, and serial failed-launch creators.
oracle_docs.the_scoring_is_a_pure_function_of: The scoring is a pure function of assembled intel. Everything stateful — ingestion, persistence, execution, settlement — lives outside it. That boundary is why the math is testable, the verdicts are reproducible, and the same engine powers the live feed, the API, and an agent's decision with identical results.
oracle_docs.the_snapshot_above_is_a_thin_low: The snapshot above is a thin, low-conviction window — realized win rates sit below the band midpoints and few coins reached the higher tiers. That is shown, not hidden. The page is built to display a weak edge as readily as a strong one, because a backtest you only trust when it flatters you isn't a backtest.
oracle_docs.the_system_gets_sharper_the_more_it: The system gets sharper the more it watches, on two flywheels. The data flywheel: every resolved outcome updates the wallet-reputation graph that powers the WHO pillar, so the definition of "smart money" is continuously re-earned, never hard-coded. The calibration flywheel: every graded outcome tightens the backtest, exposing exactly where the score is over- or under-confident so the model can be re-weighted against reality rather than intuition.
oracle_docs.the_what_pillar_depends_on_a_language: The WHAT pillar depends on a language model and a news feed; both can misread a story or miss a fast-breaking one. It's the lightest-weighted pillar for exactly this reason, and it degrades to a deterministic classifier rather than failing.
oracle_docs.the_what_pillar_is_the_only_place: The WHAT pillar is the only place Oracle reaches outside the brain. To classify a launch's story, it fetches live crypto headlines from a public news API (cached ~90s), injects them into the language model's prompt, and asks for a category, a one-line narrative, a virality estimate, and a confidence. A coin literally riding today's headline gets recognized as such and scored higher. If the model is unavailable, a deterministic keyword classifier takes over so a verdict always ships.
oracle_docs.the_wins_gallery_resolved_calls_with_the: The wins gallery — resolved calls with their score-at-entry versus the realized outcome.
oracle_docs.the_worker_is_configured_entirely_by_env: The worker is configured entirely by environment. Selected knobs (with defaults): ORACLE_MODE=simulate, ORACLE_NETWORK=mainnet, ORACLE_SCORE_INTERVAL_MS=15000, ORACLE_AGENT_INTERVAL_MS=3000, ORACLE_SETTLE_INTERVAL_MS=60000, ORACLE_SCORE_BATCH=20, ORACLE_RESCORE_AFTER_SEC=180, ORACLE_MAX_TRADE_SOL=0.25 (absolute per-trade ceiling), and ORACLE_GLOBAL_KILL=1 (halts all agent + settle activity while scoring continues). Live mode additionally requires the secret used to decrypt agent wallets, and refuses to start without it.
oracle_docs.these_docs_are_written_in_two_layers: These docs are written in two layers so the same page serves a curious first-timer and a quant who wants the closed form.
oracle_docs.this_buy_would_exceed_the_24h_spend: this buy would exceed the 24h spend cap
oracle_docs.three_ways_in_depending_on_what_you: Three ways in, depending on what you want from Oracle today.
oracle_docs.transparency_over_magic_every_score_ship: Transparency over magic. Every score ships with the reasons that built it. There is no opaque model output you are asked to trust — you can read why a coin earned an 82 or got capped at 46.
oracle_docs.two_coins_can_both_score_70_for: Two coins can both score 70 for completely different reasons — one on pure pedigree with weak momentum, another on a viral narrative over a thin base. The tier tells you how strong; the reasons tell you why, and the why is what you trade on.
oracle_docs.two_design_commitments_make_that_bet_hon: Two design commitments make that bet honest:
oracle_docs.two_win_rates_are_published_deliberately: Two win rates are published, deliberately kept apart: the call win rate (resolved coins Oracle rated Lean, Strong, or Prime — the tiers it tells you to act on) and the market base rate (every scored launch — what blindly buying everything would return). Until real calls resolve, the call win rate reads "no calls resolved yet"; the base rate is never presented as the engine's skill.
oracle_docs.unlike_the_normal_approximation_the_wils: Unlike the normal approximation p ± z·√(p(1−p)/n), the Wilson interval stays inside [0,1], doesn't collapse to zero width at p=0 or p=1, and behaves correctly for the small n that young backtests have. It is the difference between an honest "we don't know yet" and a dishonest "0% ± 0%."
oracle_docs.walking_the_drawer_top_to_bottom_mirrors: Walking the drawer top to bottom mirrors the model exactly:
oracle_docs.weighted_average_of_the_four_pillar_scor: # weighted average of the four pillar scores
oracle_docs.when_a_coin_launches_the_people_who: When a coin launches, the people who win are the ones who already know things you can't see fast enough: whose wallets are buying (and whether those wallets have a track record or a rug history), whether the launch is organic or a coordinated bundle, whether the "community" is 200 real people or 200 freshly-funded burner wallets, and whether the story has cultural legs. By the time a human reads a chart, the asymmetry has already paid out.
oracle_docs.when_a_coin_s_outcome_resolves_the: When a coin's outcome resolves, the settle loop grades any open action on it:
oracle_docs.who_and_how_together_carry_nearly_two: WHO and HOW together carry nearly two-thirds of the weight because who is buying and how fair the launch is are the two facts that most reliably separate runners from rugs. WHAT and MOVE are lighter — they break ties and confirm, but a good story or a green first minute can't rescue a coin the harder pillars condemn.
oracle_docs.who_s_in_is_the_live_pedigree: Who's-in is the live pedigree roster — every notable wallet, its label, and its track record.
oracle_docs.why_this_score_is_the_array_each: “Why this score” is the reasons[] array, each line tagged to the pillar that generated it. In this example: "no proven wallets identified yet" (WHO), "clean, distributed launch structure" (HOW), "meme narrative, virality 45/100" (WHAT), "no clear momentum yet — too early" (MOVE). A clean-but-unproven young launch — correctly a watch, not an avoid and not a buy.
oracle_docs.wilson_1927_probable_inference_the_law_o: Wilson (1927), Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference — the score interval. Brier (1950), Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability. Platt (1999), probabilistic outputs for SVMs (Platt scaling). Zadrozny & Elkan (2002), isotonic calibration. Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana (2005), Predicting good probabilities with supervised learning.
oracle_docs.wilson_interval_the_95_score_interval_on: Wilson interval: the 95% score interval on each tier/bin win rate (derivation in the evidence deep-dive), correct for small n and bounded to [0,1].
oracle_docs.win_loss_isn_t_known_until_a: Win/loss isn't known until a coin resolves, so the backtest always trails the present. Recent windows are thin and their confidence bands are wide — and the page shows the width rather than hiding it.
oracle_docs.win_rate_by_tier_with_honest_error: Win rate by tier, with honest error bars
oracle_docs.win_rate_by_tier_with_wilson_cis: Win rate by tier with Wilson CIs, calibration ladder, Brier, and the edge summary. Filters: period, tier, network.
oracle_docs.win_the_coin_graduated_or_its_peak: Win — the coin graduated, or its peak multiple reached ≥2× on a coin that didn't rug and isn't marked below half entry.
oracle_docs.with_no_signal_yet_it_returns_too: With no signal yet it returns "too early," keeping the pillar neutral rather than inventing momentum that isn't there.

pill.skeleton_h: How the pill got a skeleton
pill.skeleton_intro: The mascot arrived the way generated and scanned models usually do: one sealed shell, no bones, no joints, frozen mid-stride, and dense enough to choke a phone. Our humanoid auto-rigger looks for a head on a neck and two long arms, and a capsule with four nubs has none of that. So it got its own pipeline, and that pipeline is in the repo: scripts/rig-pill-mascot.py.
pill.skeleton_outro: That last number is the one that matters past this page. The skeleton uses the canonical bone names, so the pill is not limited to the six clips it ships with: every animation on the platform drives it, including the ones you have not made yet. Full write-up in the docs.
pill.stage_canvas_aria: 3D stage. The pump.fun pill mascot, rigged and drivable.
pill.stage_help: A green and white capsule character with a smiling painted face, two stubby arms and two stubby legs, standing on a round stage. Use W, A, S and D or the arrow keys to walk it, Shift to run, Space to jump, E to wave and Q to dance. The buttons below play the same animations.
pill.stat_retarget: of the three.ws clip library retargets onto it
pill.step1: Find the limbs without being told where they are. Voxelize the mesh, take its distance transform, and the body is everything thicker than a limb. The four nubs fall out as whatever is left over.
pill.step2: Trace each nub back into the body. A minimum-cost path that prefers thick interior follows the limb's real curve instead of guessing a straight line, which is how the bent foot ends up with a bent foot bone.
pill.step3: Skin it by what is inside, not what is nearby. The sculpted pose rests one hand against the side of the head. Any distance measure calls those two surfaces neighbours and welds them, so the weights are decided by walking each vertex inward to the axis of the part it is skin for. Through the mesh, that hand is a whole arm away from that cheek.
pill.step4: Bind mid-stride, rest standing. glTF keeps the bind pose and the rest pose separate, and our retargeter replays clip motion as a delta on the rest pose. A walk cycle has to start from legs-under-hips, so the neutral stance is baked into the shipped geometry.
pill.step5: Animate for the proportions it actually has. Six clips, authored against a mascot with nub limbs and no neck rather than borrowed from a human mocap library: idle, walk, run, wave, jump, dance.

pill.verify_h: What the check mark actually buys you
pill.verify_p1: pump.fun verification marks a coin as officially belonging to the project behind it. That is the line between the real $THREE and the copies that share its name and its ticker, and it is the single fastest way for a buyer to tell them apart before spending anything.

play_economy.meta_description: Every price, prize and gate in the /play world economy: what the general store pays for what you gather, what it sells, how the bank protects your cash through death, what the $THREE boutique charges, and the full wheel paytable with real odds. Read from the same tables the game server prices trades with.
play_economy.meta_og_description: The complete /play economy reference: store prices, bank rules, the $THREE boutique, and the full wheel paytable with real odds. Never transcribed, read straight from the game's own tables.
play_economy.meta_twitter_description: Store prices, bank rules, the $THREE boutique, and the full wheel paytable with real odds.
play_economy.nothing_below_is_transcribed_by_hand_the: Nothing below is transcribed by hand. The page reads the same tables the authoritative game server prices trades with, so a number here is the number you will be charged.
play_economy.the_catalogs_gates_and_odds_on_this: The catalogs, gates and odds on this page are served by /api/play/economy, which imports them from the game's own modules rather than restating them, so this reference cannot drift from what the server charges. Cash is a game resource and never leaves the world; only boutique unlocks and paid spins touch the chain, and both are verified on-chain before anything is granted. The separate USDC cosmetics rail for the standalone character creator is documented under Fits.
play_economy.the_open_world_runs_a_real_economy: The open world runs a real economy: a purse you can lose, a bank that protects it, a store that prices every trade server-side, a cosmetics boutique that settles on Solana, and a wheel with published odds. Until now you had to walk up to each NPC to learn any of it. This is the whole thing, in one place.

play_solver.every_yield_rule_in_the_open_world: Every yield rule in the open world is a pure function of your skill level and the node you are standing at, and every swing has a fixed cadence the server enforces. That means the expected cash, XP and goods per hour are not something you have to grind out and average. They are solvable, exactly, in one pass.
play_solver.meta_description: The /play world economy, solved. Exact expected cash and XP per hour for every tree, rock and pond at every skill level, the optimal fish-and-cook time split, what the store costs in minutes and swings, the wheel's true expected value, and per-kill combat worth. Computed in closed form from the game's own tables, never measured.
play_solver.meta_og_description: Exact expected cash and XP per hour for every node in the world at every level, solved in closed form from the game's own tables. Move the level and watch the whole world reprice.
play_solver.meta_twitter_description: Every node in the /play world, priced exactly, at every level. Closed form, not measured.
play_solver.served_by_which_imports_the_authoritativ: Served by /api/play/solver, which imports the authoritative game modules rather than restating them: the yield curves from items.js, the cadences from activities.js, the prices from shop.js and the per-node tuning from world-features.js. No number on this page was measured, sampled or transcribed, so it cannot drift from what the server actually does. The model's assumptions are published with every result and listed at the bottom of this page, because a rate quoted without its assumptions is a lie. Cash is a game resource that never leaves the world; only boutique unlocks and paid spins touch the chain.
play_solver.so_we_solved_them_move_the_level: So we solved them. Move the level below and the entire world reprices: every tree, every rock, every pond, the wheel, the store and each mob in it.

preflight.meta_desc: Check whether any x402 seller can actually settle before you pay it. Fetches the seller's signed payability attestation and verifies the signature and expiry in your browser.
preflight.share_desc: x402 tells you what a resource costs. Preflight tells you whether the seller can actually take your money. Signed, time-bounded, verified in your browser.
preflight.sub: x402 tells an agent what a resource costs. It says nothing about whether the seller can currently settle what it charges, and the gap is paid for by the buyer: a signed transfer, a consumed blockhash, a 502, and no service. Preflight closes it. Paste any origin below and this page fetches its /.well-known/x402-preflight attestation and verifies the ed25519 signature, the expiry and the subject entirely in your browser. Nothing is taken on our word.

receipts.fineprint: / search · e export CSV. Each receipt is a signed artifact (JWS) from the x402 Offer & Receipt extension; the JSON download includes the signature so anyone can verify it against the three.ws issuer key. Some receipts omit the on-chain tx hash by design for privacy. The API behind this page is GET /api/x402/my-receipts, documented in the API reference.
receipts.meta_desc: Every x402 payment you ever made to three.ws, retrievable forever. Connect a Solana or EVM wallet, sign one message, and get back your signed proof-of-purchase receipts: endpoint, network, settlement tx, and the full artifact as JSON or CSV.
receipts.og_desc: Connect a wallet, sign one message, and retrieve every signed x402 receipt three.ws ever issued you: proof of purchase for every paid API call, exportable as JSON or CSV.

receipts.signin_copy: Sign a plain-text message stating your address and a timestamp. The signature authorizes a read of your own receipts and nothing else: no transaction, no approval, no fee. It expires after 5 minutes.
receipts.signin_h: Prove your wallet, get your receipts
receipts.signin_note: Works with Phantom, Backpack, and Solflare on Solana, and MetaMask or any injected wallet on EVM chains. Receipts are signed by three.ws under the x402 Offer & Receipt extension, so third parties can verify them without trusting us. Never made a paid call? Start at the x402 endpoint catalog.
receipts.sub: Every paid x402 call you make to three.ws issues a signed receipt, and we keep a durable copy. Lost the original payment-response header? Connect your wallet, sign one read-only message, and pull back every receipt ever issued to it. This is the buyer's side of the ledger: every receipt here is something you bought.

reputation_market_index.accepted_tasks_passed_validations_and_ta: Accepted tasks, passed validations and task-linked feedback add work. Failed validations, disputes and revocations add faults, charged at double the rate work pays.
reputation_market_index.back_an_agent_with_escrowed_sol_and: Back an agent with escrowed SOL and earn from what it actually did. Yield comes from the agent's signed, on-chain action history, split each UTC day between everyone staked on it. Principal is never slashed and can be withdrawn at any time.
reputation_market_index.each_epoch_has_a_funded_budget_split: Each epoch has a funded budget split by principal × time × weight. The market can never owe more than the escrow holds, and principal is never at risk.
reputation_market_index.every_constant_below_lives_in_one_place: Every constant below lives in one place and runs identically in your browser and on the server, so you can re-derive any payout yourself. Full contract: the spec.
reputation_market_index.meta_description: Stake conviction on an agent and earn from its attested action history. Escrowed principal, per-epoch yield derived from signed on-chain attestations, withdraw any time.
reputation_market_index.meta_og_description: Stake conviction on an agent and earn from its attested action history.
reputation_market_index.meta_twitter_description: Stake conviction on an agent and earn from its attested action history: escrowed principal, per-epoch yield derived from signed on-chain attestations, withdraw any time.
reputation_market_index.positions_belong_to_the_wallet_that_sign: Positions belong to the wallet that signed the stake, so anyone can look one up. Earnings shown for an open position are pending: they are recomputed on every read and only fixed when you withdraw.
reputation_market_index.ranked_by_net_principal_currently_escrow: Ranked by net principal currently escrowed. Epoch weight is today's yield weight derived from the agent's attested work and faults; realized is the annualised rate its stakers have actually been paid, never a projection.
reputation_market_index.three_ws: three.ws
reputation_market_index.weight_is_doubling_output_does_not_doubl: Weight is performance × log2(1 + work). Doubling output does not double yield, so spraying cheap attestations buys nothing.
reputation_market_index.where_quality_maps_the_1_5_feedback: quality × integrity, where quality maps the 1-5 feedback scale onto 0-1 and integrity is work / (work + 2 × faults). No feedback reads as neutral, not as bad.

rig-doctor.explain1_desc: Every clip in the three.ws library is authored against one canonical skeleton: Hips, LeftForeArm, RightUpLeg, 52 joints in total. A track that names LeftForeArm drives nothing on a rig that calls that joint lowerarm_l.
rig-doctor.explain2_desc: Nothing errors. The GLB loads, the material renders, the mixer runs, and the character stands in its bind pose. Nobody tells you why, which is why this page exists and why it runs before you upload rather than after.
rig-doctor.explain3_desc: Mixamo, Avaturn, Ready Player Me, Unreal, VRM, Daz, Rigify, Biped, HumanIK, Reallusion, MikuMikuDance, and MakeHuman all name the same joints differently. The canonicalizer already knows every one of those dialects, and it can rewrite your file in place.
rig-doctor.explain3_title: Most rigs are one rename away
rig-doctor.explain4_desc: A rig rarely fails outright. Far more often the torso and arms map and the legs do not, so the avatar glides across the floor with frozen knees. Scoring each limb group separately is the difference between "62% covered" and "your legs will not move".
rig-doctor.explain4_title: Partial rigs are the common case
rig-doctor.hero_sub: Animation clips address bones by name. A rig whose joints are called Bip001 L UpperArm loads perfectly, renders perfectly, and then stands frozen forever. Drop your .glb and know in one second, before you upload it anywhere.
rig-doctor.meta_desc: Drop a .glb and find out in one second whether it will animate on three.ws. Rig Doctor names your skeleton convention, scores every limb group, repairs non-standard bone names in your browser, and hands the fixed file back. Nothing is uploaded.
rig-doctor.next1_desc: Every motion your rig has to match, previewed. This is what the 52 joints are for.
rig-doctor.next2_desc: Scaffold, hash, and validate the manifest from your shell or from CI.
rig-doctor.next3_desc: What each verdict means, the full canonical joint list, and how to fix each one.

sign-mirror.camera_note: Hand tracking runs locally via MediaPipe. Close the tab and it is gone.
sign-mirror.chip: Handshape practice · graded on your device
sign-mirror.course_copy: Closed fists first, open hands next, then the pairs every beginner confuses. A letter turns green once you have held it correctly; your progress is kept on this device. You can also press any letter key to jump straight to it.
sign-mirror.course_h: The alphabet, in the order it is easiest to learn
sign-mirror.footer_note: This is the practice half of the signing loop. The reference for every letter and number lives at /asl-alphabet, whole words and signed chat replies at /sign-language, and the engine behind all three pages is documented in the sign language docs and shipped as the @three-ws/sign-language package, installable from a clone until its registry publish lands. The avatar, the target diagram, and the grader all read the same handshape spec, so what is taught and what is graded can never drift apart.
sign-mirror.hint_default: Turn the camera on to be graded, or just copy the diagram.
sign-mirror.lede: Watching a letter is the easy half. Here you make it: the avatar forms the target, your camera watches your hand, and the page scores the handshape live, finger by finger. Hold it right and the letter passes. Hold it wrong and it names the finger. Nothing your camera sees ever leaves this tab.
sign-mirror.meta_desc: Learn the ASL manual alphabet by making it, not just watching it. The avatar forms the letter, your camera watches your hand, and the page grades your handshape live and names the finger that is off. Everything stays on your device.
sign-mirror.page_title: Sign Mirror: make the letter, get graded live · three.ws

sign-mirror.video_idle: The camera is off. Turn it on to be graded live. The video, the hand landmarks, and every score stay in this tab: there is no network call in the practice loop. Or skip the camera and copy the target diagram by eye.
sign-mirror.video_loading: Downloading the hand tracker. About 8 MB, once per browser. It is cached after this, and it runs in this tab from then on.
sign-mirror.video_starting: Waiting for the camera. Allow the camera in your browser prompt and the grading starts.

sign_language.a_signer_spells_names_and_loanwords_and: A signer spells names and loanwords and signs everything else. These words have real signs in the avatar’s vocabulary: a handshape, a place on the body, and a movement, on one or both hands. Pick one to watch it. Everything else in a sentence still fingerspells.
sign_language.all_26_asl_letter_handshapes_plus_the: All 26 ASL letter handshapes plus the numbers 0-9, with the traced J and Z and the double-letter bounce. Type a word in the Animation Studio and export the signing as an animated GLB, or share it as a link.
sign_language.american_sign_language_live_in_3d: American Sign Language · live in 3D
sign_language.api_foot: Full reference: the sign API · /api/sign in the API reference · the reverse direction is /api/asl-recognition. Agents can call it as the sign_text tool on the three.ws MCP server.
sign_language.api_lede: Everything above compiles in the browser. The same compiler runs on the server, so any app, agent or engine can ask for a signed utterance and get one back: a three.js animation clip keyed to a canonical humanoid skeleton, plus the timeline it performs on. No account, no key, no SDK. Type below and watch the real endpoint answer.
sign_language.best_results_good_light_hand_in_frame: Best results: good light, hand in frame, one letter at a time. Numbers and the full A-Z alphabet are supported.
sign_language.click_start_fingerspell_a_word_at_your: Click start, fingerspell a word at your camera, then stop. Your browser turns the video into hand and body landmarks locally; only those coordinates are sent for recognition. Webcam fingerspelling is imperfect (expect the odd wrong letter), so review the text before you trust it.
sign_language.fingerspell_into_your_webcam_and_the_ai: Fingerspell into your webcam and the AI reads it to text: landmarks are extracted on your device, so the video never leaves your machine. The demo below runs the same recognizer.
sign_language.honest_scope_words_with_a_sign_are: Honest scope: words with a sign are signed, everything else is fingerspelled letter by letter. Signs are strung together in English word order, which is signed English, not ASL grammar: real ASL reorders sentences, inflects verbs through space, and carries grammar on the face. The vocabulary above is a starting set and is meant to grow. Read the full breakdown.
sign_language.it_signs_these_it_doesn_t_spell: It signs these. It doesn’t spell them.

sitemap_index.d_avatar_engines: A curated, factual atlas of the open-source and commercial engines that build high-quality and photoreal 3D human avatars: Gaussian-splat heads, single-photo humans, text→avatar generators, and the rigs three.ws already animates. sitemap_index.d_avatar_wallet_chat: An embeddable 3D AI avatar that holds a Solana wallet, chats, and can autonomously send SOL.

sitemap_index.d_clip_director: Turn any trader agent's real closed pump.fun trade into the optimal shareable card per surface (X, Telegram, or the in-app Feed): an honest hook, the real number, an avatar reaction, and an on-chain proof link. Wins and losses both get a card.

sitemap_index.d_contributors: A living thank-you to the developers, issue reporters, and community members improving the open-source three.ws platform.

sitemap_index.d_cookbook: Recipes you can run, not walkthroughs. A text-to-3D command line tool, a parallel asset-pack builder, an MCP server that gives your AI assistant a 3D tool, a CI quality gate, and a self-correcting generation loop. Every recipe ships a file that was executed against the live API.
sitemap_index.d_cookbook_asset_quality_gate: Generated geometry fails quietly. This gate inspects every model against an explicit triangle, size, and material budget and exits non-zero, so a bad asset fails the build instead of the launch.
sitemap_index.d_cookbook_mcp_3d_tool: A Model Context Protocol server that exposes text-to-3D generation and model rendering as tools, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or Cursor can build and then actually look at 3D models mid-conversation.
sitemap_index.d_cookbook_parallel_asset_pack: Fan a list of prompts across the free 3D lane at a sane concurrency, download every model, render a still of each, and emit a manifest plus a browsable gallery. Partial failure degrades instead of aborting the run.
sitemap_index.d_cookbook_self_correcting_3d: An AI art director turns a one-line brief into a themed set of real 3D props with parallel function calls, renders each result, inspects it with vision, grades it against the brief with structured outputs, and rebuilds whatever missed. Read it with interactive galleries, or download the notebook and run it.

sitemap_index.d_demos: Index of live demos across the platform: viewers, agents, payments, and experiments.

sitemap_index.d_docs_agent_economy_volume: /agent-economy-volume is the public roll-up of the agent-to-agent economy: the total USDC that three.ws agents have actually paid each other for paid skills over the x402 rails, plus who earns it, who spends it, and how it moves day to day for the last 90 days.
sitemap_index.d_docs_agent_identities: Every AI agent deserves a face. sitemap_index.d_docs_agent_shell: Every visitor gets a named agent within five seconds of arriving, and the shell makes that agent the way you use the site: a command palette that runs real commands, and navigation between pages that never unloads your agent.
