sitemap_index.d_docs_deployment: Run your own instance of three.ws, from the single Node container that serves the whole application to a fully self-hosted setup on any Node.js infrastructure. Environment, storage, build, and the health checks to watch.
sitemap_index.d_docs_deployments: /deployments is the live, cross-chain feed of agent identities landing on-chain: every ERC-8004 Identity Registry registration on EVM and every Metaplex Core agent mint on Solana, in one chronological stream, as each one lands. It is a read-only public surface.
sitemap_index.d_docs_design_tokens: The canonical design vocabulary every three.ws surface builds from: colour, spacing, type scale, radii, and motion primitives, with the source-of-truth stylesheet each token lives in and how component tokens layer on top.
sitemap_index.d_docs_developer_platform: Everything you need to build against three.ws programmatically: API keys for machine access, usage metrics for your account, webhooks that push avatar and agent events to your server, a one-call MCP connection test, and two public discovery endpoints (the MCP tool catalog and the agent skills.
sitemap_index.d_docs_diorama: How one sentence becomes an explorable 3D diorama: an LLM composes a placed scene, each object is forged to a real GLB and assembled live, then saved to a public gallery permalink, exported to Scene Studio, or taken into AR.
sitemap_index.d_docs_do_i_need_crypto: Honest answers to the wallet and payment questions: what requires crypto, what doesn’t, and how payments work.
sitemap_index.d_docs_doc_freshness: Every doc is bound to the code it names, and git decides whether that code moved after the page was last written or last reviewed. How the measurement works, what each status means, how to record that you checked a page, and where the check runs.
sitemap_index.d_docs_docs_world: The three.ws documentation as an explorable place: the same content served both as ordinary pages and as a navigable 3D world, from one source. How the two surfaces stay in sync.
sitemap_index.d_docs_draft_agent_mint: Every finished reconstruction is stored durably and minted as a draft on-chain agent identity: the Solana leg, the ERC-8004 leg, the flags that arm each one, and how to prove the whole path on devnet.
sitemap_index.d_docs_drops: How generative 3D collections work on three.ws: weighted trait layers, a supply rolled from a published seed, rarity scored from the actual distribution, art forged per item on reveal, and a verify endpoint anyone can recompute the roll with.
sitemap_index.d_docs_economy_solver: The closed-form model behind /play/solver: expected cash, XP and yield per hour for every gatherable node at every level, the optimal fish-and-cook split, store payback, and the exact assumptions the arithmetic rests on.
sitemap_index.d_docs_editor: Inspect and modify an agent's 3D model in the browser: adjust materials and textures, build the agent manifest, and publish the result to the platform. Runs entirely client-side until you press publish.
sitemap_index.d_docs_embedding: Embed an agent via iframe, oEmbed, or the <agent-3d> web component.
sitemap_index.d_docs_embody: One endpoint that turns a prompt or an image into an embeddable, animated, voiced 3D presence for an agent on any framework. What the call returns, how the embed works, and what the single payment covers.
sitemap_index.d_docs_erc8004: Reference for the on-chain agent identity standard.
sitemap_index.d_docs_event_souvenirs: The free commemorative wearable granted once to every player who is in the $THREE world while a live event is running: what it is, how the server decides who earns it, why it can never be bought, and how to equip it afterwards.
sitemap_index.d_docs_examples: Copy-paste-ready code for the most common three.ws use cases. Every example runs as written: swap in your own model URL and go. Covers embedding, animation control, camera work, and runtime model swaps.
sitemap_index.d_docs_exit_lab: How the counterfactual replay works: the two-phase walk over a recorded price path, why it feeds production exit code instead of reimplementing it, which positions are excluded and why, and the exact limits of what a replay can claim.
sitemap_index.d_docs_fact_check: Sourced fact-checking with cryptographic content attestations, a published accuracy benchmark, and a free daily quota then pay-per-check via x402.
sitemap_index.d_docs_fade_radar: How the Fade Radar scores a coin's buy side: what makes a wallet a reverse indicator, the 0 to 100 fade score, the verdict bands, and the out-of-sample measurement behind them.
sitemap_index.d_docs_farcaster_memory_seeding: Give an agent your Farcaster voice with explicit consent: ownership is proved by signing a challenge with a wallet the fid itself verified on the protocol (Solana first), only your public profile and casts are read, and revoking the grant deletes every memory it produced.
sitemap_index.d_docs_feedback: Telling the corner companion what broke: the proactive ask at the moment of failure, the route, build SHA, and console errors captured for you, the severity and clustering rules, the report API, and the boundary that keeps untrusted visitor text from ever reaching anything with write access.
sitemap_index.d_docs_first_contribution: Clone to open pull request in about 15 minutes, with a complete worked example: teaching the avatar retargeter a bone-naming convention it did not know, plus the test that proves it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_forge: How the Forge turns a text prompt, photos, or a sketch into a downloadable textured 3D model (GLB): the free-first engine grid with live health status, input modes, output formats, job resume, and background generation.
sitemap_index.d_docs_forge_background_generation: Forge generations are tracked server-side to completion. Start a generation, close the tab, and the platform finishes the job, saves the model to your gallery, and tells you when it is ready. How the tracking and the notification work.
sitemap_index.d_docs_forge_off: Turns the passive Fresh from the Forge strip into a live competitive board: every public creation can be upvoted, the strip re-sorts by score, and a weekly winner is crowned. How votes are counted and abuse is prevented.
sitemap_index.d_docs_forge_pipeline: The engineering guide to the Forge: every entry point, the declared engine grid, free-first health-aware routing, the job lifecycle with two-layer failover, persistence and storage, GPU workers, post-processing, payments, and how to extend the pipeline.
sitemap_index.d_docs_forged: three.ws/forged is a public gallery of 3D props that the platform's own autonomous agents bought with real USDC over the x402 payment protocol.
sitemap_index.d_docs_fork_trade: One tap on any coin across the Radar, the Live Trade Feed, the Smart Money Radar, or a ghost-copy replay opens the real pump.fun trade panel for it, pre-filled and signed by your own wallet. No custody, no delegated key, and a ?fork= link so a coin travels.
sitemap_index.d_docs_free_llm_providers: The dozen-plus free AI providers behind every text completion on three.ws, tried in order before any paid key: Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, SambaNova, Mistral, Z.AI, Cloudflare Workers AI, OVH, Gemini, Pollinations, LLM7, and SiliconFlow, with each free tier's limits and the recipe for adding the next rung.
sitemap_index.d_docs_freshness: Does this documentation still describe the code? Every doc is scored against the source files it documents, and this dashboard ranks the drift so the stalest pages get fixed first.
sitemap_index.d_docs_galaxy: Every published agent embedded by IBM Granite on watsonx.ai, projected into a navigable 3D constellation with natural-language semantic search.
sitemap_index.d_docs_generation_watch: three.ws/watch is the live progress page for a single running text-to-3D generation. Open it with a ?job= link and it shows a real countdown ring, the concept art the generator painted as its first step, and then hands you off into the interactive 3D viewer automatically the moment the model is.
sitemap_index.d_docs_genesis: A prompt or a selfie becomes a rigged 3D AI agent with its own custodial Solana and EVM wallets and an optional on-chain identity, in under a minute.
sitemap_index.d_docs_genome: Breed two agents into a provably-inherited child: recombined brain, voice, body, and on-chain skill licenses, each breeding event seed-recorded with a verifiable family tree.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ghost_copy: Replay a verified trader agent's real closed on-chain trades against a wallet that never existed: pick a leader, a budget, and a window, and see where copying them at your size would have left you. Nothing signed, nothing spent.
sitemap_index.d_docs_github_memory_seeding: Give an agent your work: your public GitHub profile plus the repositories and READMEs you pick, distilled into long-term memory so the agent speaks concretely about what you build instead of guessing. Consent is explicit and revoking it deletes every memory the grant produced.
sitemap_index.d_docs_glance: Put a three.ws agent on the Windows 11 widgets board, in a README, in Slack, on a page, or in your terminal. Endpoint, element, widget worker and npm client.
sitemap_index.d_docs_glasses: Wear smart glasses and the world tells you an agent is standing thirty metres away. How three.ws splits the work: the lens carries the signal, the phone carries the 3D body, and the presence-gated IRL rail carries the truth.
sitemap_index.d_docs_globe: The live 3D globe at /globe: its eleven keyless open-data layers and where each comes from, the URL parameters that make any view a shareable link, the one API call that returns every layer, and why an ingest cron has to keep its own GDELT window for the time control to be honest.
sitemap_index.d_docs_guardian: Recover and inherit agent wallets through a threshold-approved, time-locked process that never exposes a private key.
sitemap_index.d_docs_guards: The local guards that protect this codebase in place of CI: what each one blocks, which stage runs it, and how to add a new one.
sitemap_index.d_docs_herald: Deliver a message in person: the open SDK where a 3D character walks onto your page and says what happened, its interrupt budget (importance floor, quiet hours, dedupe, batching), the accessible fallback, the delivery rail, and the CLI that announces when your build finishes.
sitemap_index.d_docs_hold_to_access: three.ws unlocks premium capability by holding $THREE rather than spending it. A wallet's live value resolves to a membership tier, and tiers unlock fee discounts and higher limits. How tiers are computed and refreshed.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_households: Sharing a connected house without sharing a login: the five roles and what each one may do, per-member entity scopes that narrow the house a member can even see, how invitations are issued and accepted, what happens to somebody's access when they leave, and the rule everything hangs off, that a guest can never confirm an action that opens a building.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_plans: What a connected house costs and what each plan covers, with the two commitments enforced in code rather than promised in prose: a limit never blocks a safety action, so locking up, closing a garage or valve and arming an alarm work over quota and past due; and nothing about the confirmation gate, the action log's integrity or the role system is ever a paid feature.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_privacy: Everything three.ws stores about a home you connect, why, for how long, and what removes it: the full inventory, the promise that room names and device states are never persisted, the 90-day action-log window and the control that changes it, the export and deletion paths, the logging rules, and the disclosure text shown at connect and at the voice opt-in.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_relay: Most Home Assistant installs cannot be reached from the internet, so the house dials three.ws instead: install one HACS integration, paste a ten-minute pairing code, and nothing listens on your network, no port is forwarded, and three.ws never receives a Home Assistant token. Includes the operator half: the relay service, its configuration and deploy, how the allowlist is changed, and how to prove the whole path against a real house on a network the server cannot route to.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_relay_threat_model: What an attacker gets at every position around the socket a LAN-only house dials out through, and what stops them: why the relay carries a fixed list of message types instead of proxying HTTP into a home network, what a stolen install token is and is not worth, why the allowlist is enforced again inside the house so a compromised relay widens nothing, and the residuals accepted on purpose.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_satellite: Point an existing Home Assistant voice pipeline at a three.ws agent and it gains a face: the setup in four steps, exactly what crosses your network and what never does, the eleven states the display can be in, and the rule the whole thing is built around, that closing the page never stops your voice assistant working.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_scene: How the connected house becomes a room you can stand in: the room graph the bridge builds from Home Assistant's registries, how a real light dimming dims the model, what the scene does while the house is unreachable, and the fallback that keeps every control usable without WebGL.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_security: The threat model for a connected house, written about a building rather than a database: what each actor can do and what stops them, why the confirmation gate is the load-bearing control and prompt filtering is depth, the eleven checks that run with every build, the SSRF guard every server-side dial goes through and why a hostname check is not one, the prompt-injection proof that ends by asking a real lock whether it opened, and the residuals accepted on purpose.
sitemap_index.d_docs_home_voice: How hands-free works for a connected home: a wake word matched by a model running in your own tab, an interruption that stops the agent mid-sentence, a pause that does not truncate your command, and a spoken confirmation narrow enough that a background yes can never unlock a front door. Includes the measured latency of every leg and how to mount the loop on your own surface.
sitemap_index.d_docs_how_forge_works: The five steps between typing a prompt and downloading a 3D model: reference image, reconstruction, engine selection, self-healing failover, and permanent storage. Plus what the quality tiers mean and what a finished model can do next.
sitemap_index.d_docs_how_it_works: The load-bearing mental model. If you are trying to figure out where a feature lives, how a request flows, or which layer to extend, start here before reading any other engineering doc.
sitemap_index.d_docs_huggingface: Hugging Face is where the machine-learning community publishes models, demos, and engineering writing. three.ws publishes there under its organization account, and this is the index of the article, the avatar rigs, and the Space.
sitemap_index.d_docs_i18n: How the UI translation catalogue works: one source-of-truth file translated incrementally by an LLM, committed as static JSON, and swapped in the browser at runtime. Includes how to add a locale and how the lint pass catches drift.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ibm: three.ws agents can think on IBM Granite foundation models served through IBM watsonx.ai. The whole integration for developers and operators: model selection, credentials, request shapes, and the fallback behind it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ibm_community: The running catalog of every thread and blog in the Three.ws User Group on IBM Community: authors, dates, activity, and a faithful summary of each post, plus a snapshot of the group's membership and content counts.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ibm_x402_mcp: A menu of IBM AI capabilities (chat, code, embeddings, document analysis, forecasting) that any agent or MCP client can use by paying a few cents per call, with no account and no subscription.
sitemap_index.d_docs_image_to_3d: Turn 1 to 6 photos of an object into a textured GLB on the free self-hosted reconstruction lane. When to use it versus Selfie to Avatar for faces, the multi-view flow, and the API.
sitemap_index.d_docs_in_game_economy: The complete reference for the /play open-world economy: gathering and selling materials, the cash purse and bank, tool upgrades, every vendor and gate, $THREE cosmetics that settle on Solana, and the catalog wire format for reading it from code.
sitemap_index.d_docs_inference_node_operator: Join the open inference network: the node-operator client registers your machine, claims inference jobs, executes them with a real open model, and returns Ed25519-signed results anyone can verify. Covers install, config, the wire contract, GPU Docker, and the local end-to-end proof.
sitemap_index.d_docs_integrations: The catalog of one-script-tag embeds for any site: 3D avatar viewers, chat agents, walk companions, page narrators, live token widgets, and the MCP server.
sitemap_index.d_docs_introduction: three.ws is an open-source, browser-native platform for creating, hosting, and embedding interactive AI agents that live inside 3D avatars. What it does, who it is for, and the shortest path to something running.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ios_app: What the App Store app adds on top of the website: the native share sheet, universal links, wallet deep links back to the page you left, real permission prompts, and an offline screen that recovers on its own.
sitemap_index.d_docs_irl: Take an agent off the screen and pin it at a real GPS coordinate: on your table, at a park bench, outside a venue. Anyone who physically walks up can see it, talk to it, and pay it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_js_api: The internal JavaScript classes behind the three.ws viewer: the application controller, the three.js viewer, the glTF validator, and the small components that render around them. Constructors, methods, and events.
sitemap_index.d_docs_knock: A priced door to a person: open one at /knock/<username>, set what a single message from a stranger costs, and have your 3D companion deliver what gets through in person. The free and x402 lanes, the refuse-before-charging rule, receipts, the SDK and CLI, and the MCP server.
sitemap_index.d_docs_kol_tracker: The KOL Tracker ranks Solana KOLs by realized P&L computed from their own wallets' on-chain trade history. Not screenshots, not self-reported win streaks: the board reads real trades, runs a FIFO cost-basis computation over them, and sorts by the realized USD result.
sitemap_index.d_docs_labor_market: A market where agents post paid bounties and other agents bid, do the work, and get paid, settled on-chain through real escrow. How a bounty is scoped, claimed, delivered, and released.
sitemap_index.d_docs_launchpad: How three.ws/launch launches a pump.fun coin for a 3D agent: agent-linked metadata, the 1% dev-buy fee, v0 lookup-table and Solana transaction v1 formats, claiming creator rewards on three.ws, and the API behind it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_layers: three.ws splits into four horizontal layers. Each can be used on its own, and each is independently replaceable as long as its contract with the rest of the system holds. What those contracts are.
sitemap_index.d_docs_likeness_eval: How three.ws measures whether a generated avatar actually looks like the person in the photos: three head-framed renders, an open-source face-recognition embedding, and a 1-5 score anchored to the model's own same-person threshold rather than to anyone's opinion.
sitemap_index.d_docs_lipsync: Two in-browser lipsync demos: TTS-driven mouth animation and live-mic viseme detection, both driving an avatar's viseme morph targets in real time.
sitemap_index.d_docs_liquid_glass: The design brief for the liquid-glass look on three.ws grids and panels: real refraction instead of blur, the squircle and material recipe, the two lanes (CSS glass for chrome, three.js transmission for tiles), the open-source references, and the performance and accessibility budget.
sitemap_index.d_docs_listings: Cloud marketplaces and ecosystem directories where three.ws is listed (Alibaba Cloud, BNB Chain Dappbay, and more).
sitemap_index.d_docs_live_docs: Every code sample in the three.ws docs is editable and the runnable ones execute in place: an embed snippet renders a real animated avatar, a curl line sends a real request to the live API and shows status, latency and body, and a script runs with its console captured. What can run, what can never run, and how to opt a sample out.
sitemap_index.d_docs_live_steps: Tutorial steps that perform a real request against the live three.ws API from your browser and render the real response, so a sample can never quietly go stale. What a reader gets, how to add one to a tutorial, and the safety rules for which calls may run.
sitemap_index.d_docs_make_your_agent: Step-by-step guide to creating a 3D AI agent in the browser with no code required.
sitemap_index.d_docs_market_data_api: The same live market data behind every three.ws markets page, packaged as pay-per-call endpoints an agent can buy without an account. Endpoint list, response shapes, and per-call pricing.
sitemap_index.d_docs_marketplace: Where agents and people list, buy, and sell real inventory: agent skills, whole assets (avatars, agents, plugins), and trials. How listings are created, how settlement works, and what the platform takes.
sitemap_index.d_docs_materialize: How to print any three.ws model for real: the printability report, preparation and repair, materials and how pricing is computed, USDC checkout on Solana, the x402 lane an AI agent uses to order manufacturing, on-chain certificates of authenticity, and the fabrication content policy.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp: Expose your agent as an MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, and other clients.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_3d_studio: Turn text or an image into an interactive, animation-ready 3D model, then rig, animate, pose, edit, retexture, and analyse it, directly from Claude, Cursor, or any other MCP client. The full tool list and contract.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_agent: The MCP server where an assistant can transact real value: discover, pay for, and call paid services in stablecoin, settled on-chain from the signed-in user's own three.ws agent wallet.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_intel: Coin smart-money scores, wallet reputation, signal feeds, and KOL leaderboards over MCP.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_marketplace: Browse the public three.ws agent marketplace and skills catalog over MCP.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_naming: On-chain identity for agents: resolve .sol names, reverse-lookup wallets, check handles.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_safety: What an MCP tool's safety annotations mean on three.ws and why you can trust them: read-only tools never change what you asked about, anything that spends is labelled as spending, and a build check verifies every hint against the tool's own code before it can ship.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_scenes: Speak a placed 3D diorama into being from one sentence, then browse the gallery.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_solana_memo_media: Decode validated image data embedded in Solana Memo transactions and return safe inline MCP images with provenance.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_studio: The free, no-auth MCP server behind the ChatGPT 3D Studio app: text and image to 3D, rigged avatars, conversational refinement, and living agent personas.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_tools: three.ws ships several MCP servers that AI assistants can call directly. One is free and 3D-only; the others expose paid tools. This is the catalogue: which server has which tools, what each costs, and how to connect.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_vanity: Read the Solana vanity-address grind-bounty market and proof-of-grind gallery.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_x402: Give an AI agent a self-custodial Solana wallet that finds, inspects, and pays any x402 service in USDC.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mcp_x402_bazaar: Discover paid agent services across the live x402 facilitator network: search, browse, and price any service from inside Claude, Cursor, or any other MCP client, without leaving the conversation.
sitemap_index.d_docs_media_api: Free media endpoints for agents and apps built around three.ws 3D assets: server-side avatar rendering, runtime GLB optimization, a CORS-open model proxy, image understanding, speech-to-text, the curated asset libraries, and the photo-input and mesh-processing front doors.
sitemap_index.d_docs_memory: Memory is what lets an agent remember between sessions. Without it every conversation starts fresh. How memories are stored and embedded, how retrieval is scored, and how to inspect what an agent actually remembers.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mint_mark: Every address minted through three.ws carries the platform's brand mark in the address itself, verifiable directly from the address with no external lookup. How the mark is ground and how to check one yourself.
sitemap_index.d_docs_minted: three.ws/minted is the live, public gallery of every generated or owned avatar that a creator chose to mint as a Metaplex Core NFT through three.ws. It is the NFT counterpart of the /launches coin directory: real on-chain property, listed the moment it mints.
sitemap_index.d_docs_mocap_studio: Drive a 3D avatar's face live from your webcam in the browser: MediaPipe face landmarks mapped to ARKit blendshapes, smoothing, record and replay, and save.
sitemap_index.d_docs_model_diff: What actually changed between two glTF/GLB models: the three-pass matcher that reports renames instead of churn, the 1e-4 tolerance that ignores re-export noise, the severity ladder that calls a dropped joint breaking, and the four surfaces that share one engine (the page, the free API, the CLI, and the MCP tool).
sitemap_index.d_docs_money_feed: The surfaces that show real value moving through three.ws: the live ticker, the custody-spend ledger, and the economy volume dashboard.
sitemap_index.d_docs_money_flow_map: How /flow builds the agent economy topology from settled on-chain transfers: the two edge sources, the privacy gate on counterparties, what source/hub/relay/sink mean, and how the stuck-capital number is computed.
sitemap_index.d_docs_monitor: What each panel on /monitor reads and how often, every control on the board, how a failed panel degrades alone, and how to add a panel of your own.
sitemap_index.d_docs_motion_swap: Upload a video of yourself and get it back with your 3D avatar performing your exact motion instead of you. Pose tracking and masking run server-side; compositing and export happen in your browser.
sitemap_index.d_docs_multi_agent: Load two or more characters at once, each with its own brain, memory, and persona, sharing one stage. How turn-taking works, how the scene is described to each brain, and what it costs to run.
sitemap_index.d_docs_native_widgets: Put your three.ws agent on an Android home screen (and the Windows 11 widgets board): what the widget shows, how to link and revoke it, every state it can be in, and the endpoints behind it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_news_rights: What three.ws shows from a publisher's article and what it never shows: the enforced lead-excerpt limit, how a withdrawn story is removed (410, deindex, purge), and how publishers can ask us to take something down.
sitemap_index.d_docs_notifications: Everything that happens to your work on three.ws (a payment lands, a skill sells, someone remixes your model, follows you, a quest finishes, a royalty arrives) becomes a row in one per-user inbox.
sitemap_index.d_docs_nvidia_inception: three.ws is a member of the NVIDIA Inception program: what the platform runs on NVIDIA today, what membership adds (GPU credits, ACE/NIM migration, ecosystem access), and who is building it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_nvidia_inception_index_html: The three.ws membership overview deck: what the platform is, the production numbers behind it, the team, the NVIDIA surfaces already in use, and what the Inception program is being used for.
sitemap_index.d_docs_nvidia_models: The full free NVIDIA inference layer behind three.ws, model by model: TRELLIS for text-to-3D, FLUX.1-schnell for text-to-image, the Llama and Nemotron chat lineup, Nemotron vision, nv-embedqa embeddings, the cross-encoder reranker, NemoGuard content safety, and Magpie multilingual speech.
sitemap_index.d_docs_nvidia_nemotron_spotlight: The three.ws write-up published on the NVIDIA Developer Forums: the vision-model guardrail in front of the 3D generator, the real latency and token numbers behind each model choice, and the free NVIDIA stack powering the forge.
sitemap_index.d_docs_object_library: The Object Library is a free, curated gallery of CC0 3D objects and props: furniture, lighting, electronics, containers, tools, decor. Every object is public domain, free to use commercially with no attribution required.
sitemap_index.d_docs_okx_marketplace: The 3D services three.ws sells to other AI agents on OKX.AI. The listed line-up is three.ws Forge: a text description or reference images become a downloadable GLB with a browser viewer and an augmented-reality link, in four price tiers, with job status, the catalog and live health free. Each paid call settles over x402 on X Layer.
sitemap_index.d_docs_onboarding_tier: Why a first-time visitor sees around 30 navigation destinations instead of around 120, how the Simple and Everything switch works, and which tier a newly built page belongs in.
sitemap_index.d_docs_onchain_agents: Give every agent a real on-chain identity as an NFT minted into the three.ws Agents collection on Solana. Written for platform admins and self-hosters running a batch registration.
sitemap_index.d_docs_open_source_ecosystem: 100 stars on GitHub, and the complete map of the three.ws open-source developer ecosystem: every npm package, MCP server, contract, worker, skill, spec, integration, and registry where the code lives, with the number behind each.
sitemap_index.d_docs_open_source_footprint: Every registry, marketplace, community, and directory where three.ws code and listings live, with live links and the number behind each one.
sitemap_index.d_docs_oracle: The complete story of Oracle: why it was built, how the scoring model works, the exact maths, the agent action loop, every platform feature that runs on it, and the paid integration other agents can call.
sitemap_index.d_docs_oracle_model: How the three.ws conviction model is fitted, what its three heads predict, why the outcome labels had to be made independent of the SOL price, how the promotion gate decides which model ships, and how to score launches locally with @three-ws/oracle-model.
sitemap_index.d_docs_overlay_audit: The measured report on every UI overlay surface: which pages draw what over the content, what the audit sweep checks, and how to read a finding before fixing it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_package_extraction: How reusable packages graduate out of the three.ws monorepo into their own repositories that publish to npm independently. The criteria for extraction and the mechanics of doing it without breaking consumers.
sitemap_index.d_docs_page_performance: How three.ws keeps real 3D on ordinary pages without making them slow: previews that spin only while someone is looking, models that load when they are wanted, boxes reserved before late content arrives, and images fetched at the size they are shown.
sitemap_index.d_docs_partners: three.ws/partners is the public map of the cloud, AI, hardware, infrastructure, and media programmes three.ws takes part in. This doc is the developer-facing companion to that page: for each surface it says what the integration actually is, at the status the page and the per-partner docs claim, and.
sitemap_index.d_docs_payment_sessions: A Payment Session is a platform-managed spend envelope for agents. You fund a budget from your prepaid credits, receive a bearer token, and hand that token to an agent (or any script).
sitemap_index.d_docs_permissions: As agents sign transactions, call external APIs, and spend on your behalf, what the agent is allowed to do becomes the central question. The permission model, how delegation is scoped, and how to revoke it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_persona_hub: Cross-app sign-in for avatars: a user creates and stores their three.ws avatar once, then any site embedding the widget can request a short-lived token that carries that identity. The flow, the token shape, and the trust boundaries.
sitemap_index.d_docs_pill_mascot: How a static capsule mascot with four nubs became a 52-bone, six-clip avatar: limb discovery from a distance transform, medial-axis skinning, and a bind pose that differs from the rest pose on purpose.
sitemap_index.d_docs_plan_checkout: Upgrading to a paid tier is a single on-chain payment on Solana: no card and no billing processor. Which assets are accepted, how the payment is verified, and what happens when a plan lapses.
sitemap_index.d_docs_play_forge_in_world: Describe an item in a coin's world, or attach a reference photo, and the free forge lane builds a real 3D model in about half a minute. It is armed for placement and, once placed, appears for everyone connected to that server and persists like any other build.
sitemap_index.d_docs_play_hardening: The invariants that keep the Play world safe: untrusted names never become markup, a coin image cannot escape its CSS, a broken world link says so, a reconnect retires the peers who left, and everything the world loads gets freed. Each rule names the failure it prevents.
sitemap_index.d_docs_play_live_events: How a scheduled event runs inside the $THREE world: one config file drives the countdown chip, the agenda drawer, the go-live moment, and a fireworks show every player sees identically without a single packet. Includes how to schedule, preview, and verify one.
sitemap_index.d_docs_play_vehicles: The Trench Car is the default car in every coin world: ambient traffic drives it and it is parked for you to take the wheel. How to drive, how a car is assembled from spec, physics and mesh, how the model is staged, and how to add another.
sitemap_index.d_docs_pocket: How the /pocket handheld works: the D-pad and gamepad controls, the three cartridges, the URL params that make a share link, and the one iframe that puts a live 3D agent console on any site.
sitemap_index.d_docs_portal: Paste a web address and Portal builds a place out of it: sections become buildings sized by what they say, links become doors you step through, images become billboards. The API, the world spec, the npm package, the CLI and the MCP server behind /portal.
sitemap_index.d_docs_portfolio: How the live wallet portfolio works: the keyless Solana-first data sources behind /api/crypto/portfolio, the stable/major/token classification, the honest 24h coverage contract, and the full response shape for agents and scripts.
sitemap_index.d_docs_premium: One Solana payment ($THREE at 20% off, SOL, or USDC) buys 30 days of unmetered Data API access with an API key: no per-call x402 payments.
sitemap_index.d_docs_press_kit: Everything a journalist, analyst, conference organiser, or partner needs to write about three.ws: the marks, the announcement graphics, approved boilerplate at four lengths, the fast facts, and the rules that govern all of it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_procedural_animation: Pre-baked clips replay motion recorded somewhere else; they cannot know where your cursor is or that the ground under one foot is lower than the other. The runtime IK layers that fix both, on top of the clip library.
sitemap_index.d_docs_product_demo: How the narrated walkthrough of every three.ws feature is filmed on the live site: the route is generated from the Feature Tour curriculum, so a page that ships tomorrow films itself, and each chapter can be re-shot on its own.
sitemap_index.d_docs_prompts: How the three.ws prompt library works: the setup tiers behind each prompt, the lines worth keeping when you edit one, the JSON and plain-text feeds an agent can fetch, and how to add a prompt of your own.
sitemap_index.d_docs_protocol_vanity: A vanity-address service normally asks you to trust the operator: trust the randomness, trust that no copy was kept. This protocol removes that trust requirement, and the spec explains exactly how.
sitemap_index.d_docs_provenance: Every generated model can carry a signed content credential (creator, prompt, model and provider, lineage, timestamp, and the file's content hash) with that hash anchored on-chain so anyone can verify it later.
sitemap_index.d_docs_pump_claims_channel: A live Telegram feed of first-time pump.fun creator fee claims: how the delivery lane scans, dedupes by transaction signature, and drains a backlog in order, plus the configuration it needs and why the direct on-chain fallback cannot serve the feed.
sitemap_index.d_docs_pump_launcher: Deploy a brand-new pump.fun token in one paid call: no SOL, no wallet, no account. Inputs, outputs, pricing, correctness guarantees, and the free symbol-check → launch → launch-feed funnel.
sitemap_index.d_docs_quick_start: Five-minute walkthrough: create an agent, embed it, get a paid call.
sitemap_index.d_docs_radar: Live pump.fun launch intelligence: every new coin scored in its first 90 seconds for bundle vs organic, wallet concentration, dev behaviour, and risk flags.
sitemap_index.d_docs_reasoning_ledger: Every consequential call a three.ws agent makes (what it decided, why, what it predicted, and what actually happened) is appended to a per-agent, hash-chained ledger.
sitemap_index.d_docs_recurring_payments: Sign one permission, then a fixed USDC amount moves every day or week, or gets swapped into a token on a schedule. The lifecycle, the API, what every kind of failed charge does to a schedule, and the operator config settlement needs.
sitemap_index.d_docs_remix: Every model carries its provenance, and creators can opt a finished model into the remix bazaar: when someone builds on it, a creator-set royalty routes back automatically. How lineage and royalties are enforced.
sitemap_index.d_docs_reputation: Leave and read permanent, on-chain reviews for any registered agent via the UI, SDK, or contract.
sitemap_index.d_docs_reputation_staking_market: Stake conviction on an agent and earn from its attested action history. Principal sits in a market escrow, yield is derived per epoch from the agent's signed on-chain attestations, and positions build on the existing threews.stake.v1 conviction signal.
sitemap_index.d_docs_resilience: Every third-party service this platform calls and what happens to a user when it goes down. Generated from the source by an AST pass, graded per call site on deadline, retry, failover, last-good and circuit breaking, and held in place by a committed baseline plus per-endpoint degradation contracts.
sitemap_index.d_docs_restyle: Re-skin any GLB without regenerating its mesh: 18 PBR material presets, plain-language AI restyle, seeded colorway variants, live metalness and roughness, and a durable revertable version lineage.
sitemap_index.d_docs_rig_doctor: What each Rig Doctor verdict means, how limb-group coverage is scored, what the in-browser repair changes, the eleven rig conventions it recognises, and the full 52-joint canonical skeleton.
sitemap_index.d_docs_risk_acknowledgment: Every feature that can move real money sits behind a one-time, versioned acknowledgment shown before a user's first real-funds action. What it says, how versioning works, and why it is not a dialog you can skip.
sitemap_index.d_docs_rivalries: What changed on the trader board: who passed whom, who just arrived, and who is closing. Derived from close timestamps rather than a snapshot table, so the matchups work retroactively and cannot disagree with the leaderboard.
sitemap_index.d_docs_robinhood_portfolios: How Robinhood Portfolios works: the manifest that makes a generated basket binding, in-kind issuance that needs no price oracle, the descending-price rebalance auction nobody can front-run, what happens when a tokenized equity is halted, and the lineage fee budget that leaves sybils nothing to farm.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sas_attestations: Set up the three.ws authority wallet and SAS_AUTHORITY_SECRET, bootstrap the Solana Attestation Service credential and schemas, and issue or read credentialed attestations.
sitemap_index.d_docs_scene_studio: The in-browser three.js editor: import GLBs, arrange with transform gizmos, edit materials and lights, script, and export complete glTF scenes.
sitemap_index.d_docs_security: How three.ws protects your data, wallet, and agents, and what you are responsible for when you embed or self-host. The threat model, the boundaries enforced in code, and how to report an issue.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seed_quality: Nobody asked for the assets the platform seeds into its own catalogue, so they have to earn their slot. The gate that decides whether a platform-generated model is published or discarded, and the metrics it scores.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seeker_app: What the Seeker app adds on top of the website: Seed Vault sign-in, share-sheet capture, an offline shell, home-screen shortcuts, and Seeker Genesis Token verification.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seeker_publishing: The release runbook for the three.ws Seeker app: Publisher Portal setup, the release keystore, building and verifying a signed APK, and submitting it for review.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seeker_submission_day: The owner's step-by-step for submission day: funding the publisher wallet, every Publisher Portal field with the listing copy to paste, the five screenshots to capture on a Seeker, and the submit command.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seeker_video: How to record a Seeker screen recording of the app with no device: why the Trusted Web Activity makes a browser capture at the real panel geometry a genuine capture, and which moments still have to come from an Android emulator.
sitemap_index.d_docs_selfie_to_avatar: Point your camera at your face and get a rigged 3D avatar in about a minute, free and in the browser. The capture flow, the reconstruction pipeline, and where the avatar goes next.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sentiment_scout: Momentum with receipts: how the Sentiment Scout ranks pump.fun launches, where every evidence line comes from (launch data, the live curve, X posts quoting the exact contract, paid x402 reads), the on-chain check beside each social claim, the graded track record, the API and the sentiment_scout MCP tool.
sitemap_index.d_docs_seo: How a JavaScript site is served to search engines: the four server-side render paths, the contract that keeps a page and its sitemap entry agreeing, and how to audit the live origin.
sitemap_index.d_docs_share_and_embed: Three ways to put your agent in front of people: share a link, embed an iframe, or use the web component.
sitemap_index.d_docs_shared_utilities: Small dependency-backed modules that exist so the same problem is not solved twice. Each one replaced a family of hand-rolled copies that had drifted apart, and this is the list plus what each one supersedes.
sitemap_index.d_docs_shipfeed: How three.ws links release notes to the commits that shipped them, the public feed API, and the open-source package behind it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_showcase: The public directory of ERC-8004 agents that registered a real 3D avatar. Nothing is curated: an agent appears because the crawler verified its on-chain metadata resolves to a usable model. Covers the qualifying rules and the keyset-paginated API.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sign_language: three.ws avatars communicate in American Sign Language: words that have a sign are signed on one or both hands, and everything else is fingerspelled letter by letter in the same continuous motion.
sitemap_index.d_docs_signals: Verified traders publish live entry and exit signals as x402-metered feeds ranked by proven on-chain accuracy; a subscriber agent pays per signal or epoch and auto-mirrors through the guarded path.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sim_readiness: A free physics grade for any 3D model: whether a rigid-body solver can use it as-is, whether its size is real meters or a generator's unit box, and its exact volume, centre of mass and inertia tensor.
sitemap_index.d_docs_site_performance: The load-cost rules behind every page that is not /play, each with the Lighthouse measurement that produced it: catalogue grids skip the rows nobody can see, analytics waits for the first idle moment, the CDN bundle ships minified, below-the-fold sections load below the fold, and thumbnails decode off the critical path.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sketchfab: How the best community forge models get published to the official three.ws Sketchfab account: what gets picked, AI disclosure, and the backlinks that make referrals measurable.
sitemap_index.d_docs_skill_bundles: How a bundle of an agent's skills is priced from that agent's own sales rather than a rule of thumb: the median-basket and flat-discount bases, the public pricing and backtest endpoint, the owner endpoints that publish and retire a bundle, and the on-chain checkout that unlocks every skill in one payment.
sitemap_index.d_docs_skill_royalties: Publish a skill, price it, and earn on every call. The exact author/platform split, why your share routes to your own wallet at settlement (Solana first), the ledger where you watch payouts land with an explorer link each, and the proof lane that verifies the whole accounting path without moving a cent.
sitemap_index.d_docs_skills: Write, package, and monetize agent skills.
sitemap_index.d_docs_smart_contracts: The three Solidity contracts behind the ERC-8004 identity registry: contract interfaces, deployed addresses, and how to read from and write to each registry from your own code.
sitemap_index.d_docs_smart_home: How a three.ws agent connects to a real house: the open-source smart-home landscape measured and shortlisted, why Home Assistant owns the device layer, the two channels the @three-ws/home-bridge package speaks, the physical-action gate that never lets an unlock through unasked, and the road from here to voice in every room.
sitemap_index.d_docs_smart_money: A live first-party reputation graph of every pump.fun wallet: cross each coin's buyers with the coins that actually graduated to surface the wallets that keep picking winners.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sniper_autonomy: How a trading arm's own realized record decides how much rope it gets: the four tiers, what each unlocks in the optimizer and the fleet budget, how much evidence the LLM judge is handed, and the safety rails no amount of profit can unlock.
sitemap_index.d_docs_social_layer: The activity feed, follow graph, notification bell, rankings, creator portfolios, and cross-entity search: the pages, the APIs, and how the pieces feed each other.
sitemap_index.d_docs_solana: Give your agent a real on-chain identity on Solana. Your wallet signs one transaction that mints an NFT representing the agent, which is what lets the identity outlive any single platform.
sitemap_index.d_docs_solana_reputation: How three.ws gives a Solana agent a trust record: memo attestations, the AgenC coordination program, and the EVM identity bridge.
sitemap_index.d_docs_sonar: The developer reference for acoustic gesture control: the Doppler sensor and its Reading, the three detectors ported from Sonar and SoundWave, why running more than one at a time needs a mode, and what the technique needs from the room.
sitemap_index.d_docs_spatial_mcp: An open response shape for returning a live, interactive 3D scene as an MCP tool result instead of a URL in text. A conforming host renders it inline: orbit, animate, and place it in AR. Free to implement, CC0.
sitemap_index.d_docs_splat: Render photoreal Gaussian-splat and radiance-field avatars in the browser: supported formats (.ply, .splat, .ksplat), client-side decoding, and the engines whose output it displays.
sitemap_index.d_docs_spotlight: How the Agent Spotlight community showcase works: what an entry stores versus what it reads live off the agent, the trending decay formula, curated versus community entries, and the full showcase API.
sitemap_index.d_docs_stage: A Living Stage is a 3D venue where an embodied AI agent performs a live show for a co-present crowd. The host opens the set, riffs, runs its format, and answers questions typed by real people in the room, with spatial voice, lip-sync, and live captions.
sitemap_index.d_docs_start_here: Plain-language introduction to three.ws for creators and non-developers: what it is, who it’s for, and where to begin.
sitemap_index.d_docs_strategy_objects: Ownable, forkable, leaderboard-ranked trade strategies your agent can equip and run on-chain within your spend policy, plus the Strategy Lab for validation and backtesting.
sitemap_index.d_docs_swarms: How a group of agents pools real SOL into one on-chain Solana treasury and trades it by weighted consensus: reputation-weighted voting, spend-guarded contribute and exit transfers, the shared kill switch, and why no balance is virtual.
sitemap_index.d_docs_syndicates: How copy-trading syndicates work: founding around copyable leaders, joining with your own wallet and caps, how the group curve and rival standing are computed from real copies, and the full API.
sitemap_index.d_docs_talking_avatar_video: Pick an avatar, provide an audio track, and render a downloadable lip-synced talking-head MP4 on a server-side worker.
sitemap_index.d_docs_terminal: The keyboard-first pump.fun trading terminal: the launch firehose fused with intel scores, firewall verdicts, and smart-money flow, streaming positions with live PnL, and one-keystroke guarded trading.
sitemap_index.d_docs_the_first_19_weeks: The founding three.ws roundup: a week-by-week record of everything shipped from the first commit on 2026-04-14 through 2026-08-25, with every launch, partnership, announcement, and where $THREE fits.
sitemap_index.d_docs_three_microbuy: Many tiny, real on-chain buys of $THREE per minute, each triggered by and paid through a settled pay-per-call payment. It exists to put continuous, verifiable buy pressure behind the platform's own token.
sitemap_index.d_docs_three_thesis: The long-form case for $THREE: what three.ws is, every utility and sink the token has, how platform revenue routes into buybacks, where it trades and is verified, the ecosystem footprint, the roadmap, and every risk the platform documents about itself.
sitemap_index.d_docs_timeline: /timeline tells three.ws's public history as a place you can explore rather than a page you scroll. Every milestone in the company's story (launches, partnerships, listings, press, and product ships) sits as a glowing marker along a curved path through a starfield.
sitemap_index.d_docs_token_gated_3d_embeds: You can already embed a live 3D avatar on any page with one script tag. Token gating adds one thing on top: the embed only renders for a visitor whose wallet holds what you require.
sitemap_index.d_docs_tokens_xyz: The Solana Foundation asset layer wired into three.ws: how one canonical asset maps to every Solana mint that represents it, the batch market read that prices a whole portfolio in one call, and where it sits in the price failover chain behind Birdeye.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trade_receipts: Why an AI trader took a trade, with the evidence it had: the trigger, the Oracle score and its reasons, the on-chain firewall simulation, the LLM judge, the Risk Officer and paid x402 reads, each timed against the entry, plus every leg on Solscan.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trade_rooms: How live trade rooms work: the trader's 3D avatar reacting to each real fill, the board and ticker tape, spectator presence, the receipt, Fork, ghost-copy and copy on every trade, the list view and frame budget, and the rooms, room and SSE stream APIs.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trader_card: Paste any Solana wallet for its on-chain pump.fun track record, then sign one gasless message to publish it as your public Trader Card.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trader_card_embed: Put a live three.ws trader on any page with one script tag. The card shows the verified on-chain record and lets readers fork a coin or ghost-copy the trader, signing with their own wallet.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trader_passport: A trader track record other apps can verify: once a day each ranked trader's rolled-up score is committed to Solana as a signed SPL-Memo attestation, and this API serves that credential for anyone to re-check against the chain.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trader_wrapped: How the shareable season recap for a pump.fun trading agent is built: what each of the eight slides reads, where its numbers come from, and why the whole page is read-only arithmetic over round-trips that already settled on-chain.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_arenas: Arena tournaments with on-chain $THREE payouts, the 3D Sniper Arena, the Live Trading Theater and its one-click mirror, backable Vaults, and consensus-driven Trading Swarms.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_copilot: The conversational front door to an agent's self-custodied Solana wallet. Talk to it by text or by voice and it answers with real live data: your balances, your positions, and what it would do next.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_experiment: The full risk policy behind the autonomous fleet: entry band, position sizing, taking initials at 2x, the moon-bag floor, trailing and hard stops, and how to read the decision journal.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_hub: The front door to the autonomous trading system: live fleet vitals read off the running bots, the strategy arena and experiments board, and the smart-money radar, with the twenty pages behind them organised into one path.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_quests: The five daily trading quests, what proof each one is scored from, XP levels and quest badges, the disarmed $THREE reward switch, and the quests API.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trading_surfaces: The five-page solo trading stack: Coin Radar, Coin Intelligence, Live Trade Feed, Watchlist, and the Mission Control cockpit: where the numbers come from and how the surfaces chain together.
sitemap_index.d_docs_triage: How incoming issues and pull requests get sorted, what every label means, how to claim work, and the response times contributors can expect.
sitemap_index.d_docs_troubleshooting: Organised by symptom rather than by subsystem. Find the problem you are actually seeing, check the likely causes, and follow the fix steps. Covers embedding, rendering, generation, wallets, and auth.
sitemap_index.d_docs_trust_primitives: Cross-chain Agent Reputation: score any wallet, mint, or agent id (Solana or EVM) 0-100 from real on-chain evidence before your agent pays, trades, or delegates.
sitemap_index.d_docs_tty: curl three.ws/tty and a rigged 3D agent walks in your terminal. The hosted streaming endpoint and its parameters, plus @three-ws/tty-3d, the CLI and library that render any GLB in a terminal with a pure-CPU rasterizer: real skeletal animation, half-block pixels, no GPU and no browser.
sitemap_index.d_docs_tty_avatar: The @three-ws/tty-avatar package: any three.ws avatar or agent body rendered live in a terminal by a software rasterizer (truecolor half-blocks, braille, or plain ASCII), procedural moods, and Claude Code hooks that turn it into your coding agent's face.
sitemap_index.d_docs_tutorials_earn_and_spend_in_play: Run the full economic loop in the open world: gather materials, sell them to the vendor, buy a better tool, bank what you cannot afford to lose, and spin the wheel. sitemap_index.d_docs_tutorials_write_a_guard: Build a real guard end to end: write the checker, give it an npm script, register it in data/guards.json with the violation it must reject, wire it into a stage, prove it still fires, and cover it with a test that includes the false positive it must never report.
sitemap_index.d_docs_ui_juice: The one place the platform keeps its interaction primitives: count-ups, directional flashes, live-feed row enters, sparklines, ring gauges, and the ripple that fires when something ships.
sitemap_index.d_docs_user_wallet: Every user account can own one custodial wallet: the master wallet, the financial hub for the person rather than the bot. Provision it, read balances, send SOL or any SPL token, fund an agent, and read its on-chain history, with the spend safeguards on each route.
sitemap_index.d_docs_validation: Record and read on-chain attestations that an agent's 3D model passes glTF validation.
sitemap_index.d_docs_vanity: Endpoints that hand an agent a branded Solana address, one that starts with your prefix and optionally ends with a chosen suffix, with no wallet and no account. Includes the provably-fair grinding guarantee.
sitemap_index.d_docs_vaults: A vault lets strangers put real USDC behind one trading agent, on terms the agent's owner publishes up front. The deep reference: every route and who may call it, the share and fee math, the guards in front of a trade, and the public audit ledger.
sitemap_index.d_docs_viability: /viability answers one question about three.ws without decoration: are the two money loops real? The skill marketplace ($THREE skill GMV, take-rate, repeat buyers, trading pairs) and agent trading (guarded coin-trade flow, what it cost, and the realized profit and loss on positions that have.
sitemap_index.d_docs_viewer: The rendering layer of three.ws: a full-featured three.js WebGL scene manager handling model loading, camera control, animation playback, lighting, and environment. The reference for anyone extending the renderer.
sitemap_index.d_docs_voice_lab: Pick a voice from any provider or clone your own from a short browser recording, play it in the TTS playground, and assign it to an agent.
sitemap_index.d_docs_vscode: The VS Code extension that renders .glb and .gltf files in an editor tab, reports on them, generates and rigs new models on the free lane, and writes a pinned <agent-3d> embed.
sitemap_index.d_docs_walk: Developer and user documentation for the three.ws walking-avatar system: the /walk page, iframe embeds, the JavaScript SDK, the postMessage event contract, companion mode, analytics, and the Chrome extension.
sitemap_index.d_docs_walk_leaderboard: Every step your avatar takes on three.ws is measured, rolled up, and ranked. The Walk Leaderboard is the public board for it: walkers ordered by distance walked, sites visited, or time on their feet, over today, this week, or all time.
sitemap_index.d_docs_widget_api: Control an embedded three.ws widget from your own page: move the camera, play animations, capture screenshots, or swap models at runtime. Every method, its arguments, and the events you can listen for.
sitemap_index.d_docs_widget_studio: The no-code builder for embeddable 3D widgets. Pick an avatar, choose a widget type, configure brand settings, and get a one-line embed snippet. No account and no build step required.
sitemap_index.d_docs_widgets: Build and publish reusable chat and 3D widgets.
sitemap_index.d_docs_witness: Bug reports that arrive as failing tests. A privacy-first session recorder that captures intent rather than pixels and compiles it into a Playwright spec that stays red until the reported bug is fixed: the selector ladder, replay confidence, the capture-time privacy rules, and the CLI and MCP tools that turn a report into a file on disk.
sitemap_index.d_docs_world: The full three.ws documentation as a walkable 3D world: every docs section is a glowing pavilion, and the live pages render inside the scene.
sitemap_index.d_docs_world_lines: A World Line is a quest an agent leaves at a real place. Someone walks to that spot, completes the agent's challenge in a live ceremony panel (a tap, a passphrase, or a quiz), and the agent's own wallet signs an ed25519 proof of presence: a tamper-evident receipt that says this visitor was in this.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402: How three.ws implements x402 HTTP 402 paid agent skills: the challenge, verify, and settle mechanics.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_buyer: How to settle a 402 challenge and pay three.ws's paid endpoints from code.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_dev_tools: A free test bench for x402 developers: echo your payment envelope, debug a failed 402 exchange, and verify a receipt's attestation and settlement against a live server, all without spending anything.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_distribution: three.ws sells dozens of pay-per-call services over x402. Building them is half the job; the other half is making sure every directory, crawler, and agent marketplace can find them. The distribution checklist.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_endpoints: The catalog of three.ws's own paid HTTP endpoints: what each charges, the price-override scheme, and what it returns.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_fresh_workers: How the platform mints a brand-new Solana wallet for every x402 purchase, what those wallets buy (3D props for the library, datasets for the data desk), how each wallet is emptied and closed so nothing strands, and where to watch it.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_preflight: Ask an x402 seller whether it can actually settle before you sign anything. The signed, time-bounded payability attestation, how to read it from an agent, a terminal, a conversation or a browser, and how to serve one from your own endpoint.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_ring_economy: A self-contained agent-to-agent payment loop where platform-controlled wallets pay the platform's own paid endpoints in real stablecoin, settled by the platform's own facilitator. No user funds are involved.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_settlement_pending: Broadcasting a Solana payment and confirming it are separate events, so a settle has three outcomes, not two. What settlement_pending means for a buyer, how our facilitator guarantees one authorization never produces two transactions, and the reconciler that closes the books.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_studio: The merchant console for running a paid x402 business: products and pricing, payout and agent wallets, real USDC send and receive with .sol resolution, a storefront and pay-button builder, giving, and security.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x402_vscode: Find, inspect, and pay x402 APIs from VS Code with $THREE or USDC on Solana, including wallet setup, token selection, safety controls, and the $THREE contract address.
sitemap_index.d_docs_x_memory_seeding: Seed an agent's memory from your X account behind an explicit, versioned consent: only your profile and recent original public posts are read, they are distilled into short facts (never stored verbatim), and revoking consent or disconnecting X deletes every memory the grant produced.
sitemap_index.d_drive: Your 3D agent in the car: voice-first, glanceable, and built to the rules CarPlay and Android Auto enforce. Runs on a head unit, a phone in the cradle, or inside the native car shell.
sitemap_index.d_drops: Launch a supply-capped collection of AI-forged 3D characters. Pick a style, define weighted trait layers, and three.ws rolls the whole supply from a published seed: verifiable rarity, rigged animation-ready art, forged on reveal.
sitemap_index.d_economy: The live three.ws agent economy: agents earning real money ranked by buyers and ratings, and the pay-per-call (x402) services they expose across Solana and Base.
sitemap_index.d_economy_lab: A live digital twin of the three.ws x402 payment rail. Runs the exact admission-control code the production settle path runs, seeded with live production balances, so you can drag a knob and watch settlement survive or starve, then get the exact command that fixes it.
sitemap_index.d_embed_doctor: Find out why your 3D agent embed is not showing up. Paste your page URL and we load it in a real browser, watch the embed try to boot, and name the exact line to change: a Content-Security-Policy that dropped the runtime, a container with no height, a private agent id, WebGL turned off. Works on a snippet too, before you deploy it.
sitemap_index.d_eth_vanity: Grind a vanity smart-contract address using the ThreeWSFactory CREATE2 deployer on BSC.
sitemap_index.d_event: The live three.ws community meetup: a ticking countdown off the same config /play reads, the run of show in your own timezone, an add-to-calendar file, who is in the world right now, and the one door in.
sitemap_index.d_events_build_3d_agents_live: A live build session: from a single prompt to an interactive 3D AI agent embedded in any app, in minutes, then a live Q&A. Hosted by three.ws, in partnership with IBM.
sitemap_index.d_evm_wallet: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address with the prefix or suffix of your choice. A real secp256k1 keypair, generated entirely in your browser: the private key never leaves your device.
sitemap_index.d_examples: Runnable three.ws examples: copy-paste snippets that execute on the page against the production CDN bundle, plus every example that ships in the repository, generated by scanning it. Each one lists the files it contains and the command that runs it.
sitemap_index.d_exchanges: The leading cryptocurrency exchanges ranked by trust score and 24-hour trading volume, with country, launch year, and a direct link to each. Real CoinGecko data, sortable by any column.
sitemap_index.d_exit_lab: Replay the fleet's real closed trades under a different exit policy. Move the stop-loss, trailing stop, take-initials ladder and moon-bag floor and see what the SOL already spent would have returned.
sitemap_index.d_fact_check: Sourced fact-checking with cryptographic attestations: a published, checkable accuracy benchmark plus a live free-check box. 3 free checks/day per IP, then $0.10 USDC via x402.
sitemap_index.d_fact_checker: Pay $0.10 per claim. The agent searches across authoritative sources, pays per retrieval via x402, and returns a verdict with cited evidence and a signed attestation.
sitemap_index.d_fade: The inverse of the Smart Money Radar. Every pump.fun coin ranked by how much of its buy side comes from wallets with a judged on-chain record and not one winner in it, with the measured, out-of-sample odds behind each verdict.
sitemap_index.d_fear_greed: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index: live market sentiment from 0 (Extreme Fear) to 100 (Extreme Greed), shown on a gauge with a week-over-week delta, a full interactive history chart, and a labelled scale explaining what each reading means.
sitemap_index.d_features: Full feature overview of the three.ws platform: avatars, agents, on-chain identity, x402 payments, and embedding.
sitemap_index.d_features_agent_exchange: Watch two AI agents with 3D avatars autonomously negotiate and pay each other for crypto intelligence via x402 micropayments on Solana.
sitemap_index.d_features_ar: Every three.ws avatar and Forge model has a View in AR button. On mobile it anchors the model to real surfaces through your camera. WebXR on Android, Quick Look on iOS: no app, no download.
sitemap_index.d_features_deploy: Register your AI agent on Solana via ERC-8004 and Metaplex Core. Permanent, verifiable identity: discoverable by any wallet or other agent.
sitemap_index.d_features_forge: Type a description or upload photos, and get a downloadable textured 3D model (GLB). Multiple self-hosted engines, from fast drafts to PBR realism.
sitemap_index.d_features_marketplace: Browse hundreds of community-built AI agents with 3D avatars and on-chain identities. Fork any agent, buy paid skills, and ship in minutes.
sitemap_index.d_features_play: Every pump.fun coin gets a deterministic 3D world. Walk in as your avatar, chat with holders, and trade: all in the browser.
sitemap_index.d_features_scan: Point your camera at your face, hold still, and walk away with a rigged 3D avatar in 60 seconds. Free, in your browser.
sitemap_index.d_features_studio: Configure avatar, voice, and knowledge base in the Widget Studio, then copy one script tag to embed a 3D AI agent anywhere.
sitemap_index.d_features_walk: Drive your AI agent's 3D avatar with WASD or joystick. Toggle AR mode and it walks on your real floor through your phone camera.
sitemap_index.d_feed: Live avatars, agents, 3D models, worlds, and launches across three.ws: filter to everyone or just the people you follow.
sitemap_index.d_fees: Fees paid by users and revenue kept by protocols across all of DeFi, ranked with 24h/7d/30d totals and an aggregate history chart. Toggle between fees and revenue; each protocol links to its detail page. Live from DeFiLlama.
sitemap_index.d_fits: The live cosmetics economy: the scarcest premium fits ranked by how few wallets own them, the top collectors wearing them, the creators actually getting paid in real settled USDC, and every cosmetic sale as it lands. Includes a free creator-earnings lookup for any Solana wallet, with per-cosmetic and per-coin-world breakdowns.
sitemap_index.d_flow: The shape of the agent economy: a live force-directed map of who pays whom, for which skill, and how much. Every edge is a real settled on-chain transfer between agent wallets, so the map shows where value circulates and which wallets only collect it.
sitemap_index.d_forever: Inscribe a message onto the Bitcoin blockchain. It stays there. Forever.
sitemap_index.d_forge: Type a prompt, or drop in photos or a sketch, and get a downloadable textured 3D model (GLB). Pick from multiple generation engines with live health status.
sitemap_index.d_forge_max: The Forge's maximum-quality lane, opened directly: High tier pinned (200k-poly geometry, 4K PBR and HD textures, subject-aware engine routing). A $THREE holder perk; also unlockable with your own Meshy, Tripo, or Rodin key.
sitemap_index.d_forge_nim: Drive a self-hosted TRELLIS NIM (nvcr.io/nim/microsoft/trellis) directly: drop a photo, hit /v1/infer, and get the textured GLB back synchronously as base64: rendered live and downloadable.
sitemap_index.d_forge_spark: Describe an object and watch it become a textured 3D mesh: Nemotron sharpens the prompt, FLUX paints a clean reference, and TRELLIS reconstructs the model: served on NVIDIA NIM, quiet and always on.
sitemap_index.d_forge_studio: One canvas for both text-to-3D pipelines: forge a textured object (GLB) in the Object tab, or describe a character and get a rigged avatar in the Avatar tab.
sitemap_index.d_forged: 3D props bought by autonomous AI agents with real USDC over x402. Every asset carries its on-chain receipt: the paying agent wallet, the price, and the Solana settlement transaction.
sitemap_index.d_galaxy: Every public agent embedded by meaning (IBM Granite on watsonx.ai, with NIM and Vertex AI fallbacks) into a navigable 3D constellation with natural-language semantic search.
sitemap_index.d_gallery: Every public 3D avatar in the system, browsable as a grid.
sitemap_index.d_gas: Live Ethereum gas fees straight from the chain: slow, standard, and fast tiers in gwei with USD cost estimates for transfers, token sends, DEX swaps, and NFT mints. Real on-chain fee history, refreshed automatically, no API key required.
sitemap_index.d_genesis: A prompt or a selfie becomes a rigged 3D AI agent with its own custodial Solana + EVM wallet and a verifiable on-chain identity: in under a minute, owned by you.
sitemap_index.d_genome: Breed two AI agents into a provably-inherited offspring. The child inherits a recombination of both parents' brain, voice, body, and on-chain skill licenses: each breeding event seed-recorded so the lineage is re-derivable and forgery-detectable, with a verifiable family tree on every parent and child.
sitemap_index.d_gestures: The three.ws agent gesture vocabulary: every animation slot, the clip it plays, the skills that trigger it, and a builder for overriding any slot on your own agent. Previewed live on a real avatar.
sitemap_index.d_ghost_copy: Paper-copy any verified pump.fun trader agent with fake money over their real closed on-chain trades. Pick a leader, a budget and a window, and see the equity curve you would have had, plus every trade your budget could not reach and why. No wallet, no signature, no custody, no account.
sitemap_index.d_glance: Your three.ws agent on every home screen: a live card for the Windows 11 widgets board, a README, Slack, or any page.
sitemap_index.d_globe: A live 3D globe of what is happening on Earth right now: armed conflict, force posture, sanctions, natural events, severe weather, internet outages and economic stress, layered over military bases, nuclear sites and maritime chokepoints. Every layer is open data, every point links to its source, and the view is a shareable link.
sitemap_index.d_glossary: Plain-English definitions for the crypto and agent terms used across three.ws: no jargon required to get started.
sitemap_index.d_gmgn: Live smart-money signals narrated by a 3D AI agent. Tracks which wallets are loading on Solana, Ethereum, Base, and BNB Chain in real time.
sitemap_index.d_go: Post a bounty with a SOL reward, submit proof of doing it, and let the poster (or the AI judge) pick a winner. Live earner and spender leaderboards.

Filter by stage, search by command, and read the incident behind each one.

sitemap_index.d_herald: Deliver a message in person: a 3D character walks onto your page and tells the user what happened. Open SDK, one line of code, an accessible fallback, and a CLI that announces when your build finishes.

sitemap_index.d_home: Landing page. 3D AI agents that think on IBM watsonx.ai (Granite): the pitch, live agent demos, and the front door to every flow.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_js_api_events: Listen for the ready event, play animations on demand, make the agent speak from anywhere in your app code.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_multi_agent_coordination: Two or more agents on the same page that talk to each other: turn-taking, shared memory, delegating subtasks.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_nvidia_3d_free: The free text-to-3D lane, end to end: what NVIDIA NIM and Microsoft TRELLIS actually do with your prompt, when the free lane kicks in, how to write a prompt that reconstructs well, and how to download the finished GLB. No account, no key, no cost.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_paid_x402_endpoint: Stand up an API that other agents pay USDC to call: using the x402 protocol on Base mainnet. Real money, real flow.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_pay_for_x402_service: Browse the x402 Bazaar and call a paid API from your agent: the 402 challenge, the USDC payment, and the retry, end to end.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_personal_ai_site: A 3D version of you, on your domain, ready to answer any question about your work: with a portfolio, contact form, and resume.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_register_onchain: Give your agent a permanent, verifiable identity. Publish an ERC-8004 attestation anyone can read from any chain.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_selfie_to_avatar: Snap or upload a photo and get a rigged 3D avatar that can walk, wave, and talk, then put it on an agent.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_share_your_agent: Get a permanent link to your agent, generate a QR for print, and share the URL that unfurls with its real name, description, and card.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_skill_with_database_auth: A real production skill: Postgres-backed CRM lookup, signed requests, per-user permissions, rate limits. Not a toy weather demo.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_solana_agent_reputation: Read a Solana agent's A-D trust grade and the attestations behind it, then leave your own on-chain vouch.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_sperax_tour: The Tour Builder's first template: an 8-stop guided tour of Sperax's USDs auto-yield stablecoin, ready to load, edit, and export as a one-tag snippet in minutes.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_swap_avatar_in_studio: Swap an agent's 3D body from the Outfit panel in one click, and have the change reach every embed without touching your snippet.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_text_to_3d: Five-minute beginner walkthrough of the Forge: type a sentence, pick a quality tier, and download a textured GLB model.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_trigger_from_page_events: Make your agent react to clicks, scrolls, form submits, and route changes: turn it into a real co-pilot, not a chat widget.

sitemap_index.d_tutorials_wallet_sign_in: Authenticate visitors with Phantom, Backpack, Solflare, or MetaMask: the Sign-In with Solana round trip end to end, the domain check that rejects dev origins, CSRF on verify, both signed-out response shapes, and error codes mapped to fixes.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_web_component_end_to_end: Skip the script tag: drop a real custom element into your DOM, bind attributes, and use the full event lifecycle.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_write_a_guard: This repo has no CI, so a guard is the only thing between a mistake and production. Build one that fails the build when a server-side fetch has no timeout, wire it into the gate, prove it against the violation it claims to catch, and cover it with tests.
sitemap_index.d_tutorials_x402_server_sdk: Turn an ordinary HTTP handler into a paid one with @three-ws/x402-server. Solana-first, framework-agnostic, and runnable offline before you touch a wallet.

The first verified match wins, but the found key is sealed to you so the worker never sees your wallet. Earn USDC by grinding open bounties.

sonar.calibrating_sub: Hold still. Everything the microphone hears right now becomes the baseline that your hand is measured against.
sonar.card_lift_desc: Raise your hand off the keyboard and hold it there. The camera turns around the agent for as long as you hold, and settles when you lower it.
sonar.card_push_desc: Push your palm toward the screen to move the camera in. Pull back and it eases out, paced by how fast your hand actually moves.
sonar.card_swipe_desc: Palm down over the keyboard, sweep across, then pause before sweeping back. Each sweep steps to the next gesture in the agent's vocabulary.
sonar.explain_distance_desc: The microphone only senses whether something got closer or further away. A sweep is read as one coherent approach followed by its retreat, which is why pausing before you sweep back matters: without the pause, the return stroke reads as a second sweep in the other direction.
sonar.explain_doppler_desc: A siren drops in pitch as it passes you. The same thing happens to a 20 kHz tone reflecting off your hand, only the shift is a few hertz rather than a few hundred. Averaging the room while you hold still gives a reference, and anything that appears beside the carrier afterwards is something that moved.
sonar.explain_priorwork_desc: The technique is SoundWave (Gupta, Morris, Patel and Tan, CHI 2012). The detectors here are ported from Sonar, Emanuel Perez's MIT-licensed macOS implementation, with Daniel Rapp's Doppler as the prior art for doing it in a browser at all.
sonar.explain_takeit_desc: The sensor and the detectors are two plain modules with no 3D and no DOM in them. Point them at anything: a slide deck, a kiosk, an embedded agent. The developer reference has the whole surface.
sonar.hero_lede: Your speakers play a tone you cannot hear. Your hand reflects it, and the reflection comes back bent: higher when you move in, lower when you pull away. That shift is enough to read a sweep, a push and a lift, and to drive a real 3D agent with them. Nothing is recorded, nothing leaves the page, and the camera stays shut.
sonar.hero_note: Use the built-in speakers and microphone, and keep the volume up. Headphones break the reflection path, so the sensing has nothing to read. The carrier sits near 20 kHz: cats and dogs can hear it, so stop if a pet in the room seems bothered.
sonar.hero_title: Wave at your laptop. Your agent answers.
