stream.how_h2: How a prefix can be a whole avatar
stream.how_p1: The packer simplifies the mesh successively, finest to coarsest, so the vertices surviving at each level are a strict subset of the level below it. Rank every vertex by the coarsest level it reaches, sort the vertex buffer by that rank, and each level's vertices become a contiguous prefix. A refinement then only ever appends bytes, never rewrites them. Skinning rides along untouched, because a mesh simplifier only emits a new index buffer over the vertex array it was given.
stream.how_p2: Because layer 0 is a real GLB and not a custom blob, you can cut it out with nothing but curl and open it in any glTF tool:
stream.how_p3: In a browser, the reader takes one ranged request to first frame and refines in the background, mutating the geometry already on screen rather than rebuilding the scene:
stream.how_p4: The format is documented in specs/AVATAR_STREAM.md and the endpoint serving these streams is /api/avatar-stream, which will hand you the layer table as JSON.
stream.layer0_desc: Coarse mesh, full skeleton, thumbnail textures. A valid GLB on its own.
stream.layer1_desc: New vertices, finer indices, and the animation clips.
stream.layer2_desc: More geometry, applied in place on the live scene.
stream.meta_desc: A 3D avatar should not be a blank box until the last byte arrives. A3S packs a GLB into layers whose first 50 KB is already a complete, skinned, spec-valid avatar, refined in place over plain HTTP range requests.
stream.share_desc: The first 50 KB of an A3S stream is already a complete, skinned avatar. Watch it race a classic GLB load.
stream.sub: A GLB is atomic: nothing renders until the last byte lands. On a slow connection that is several seconds of empty frame on every embed. A3S repacks the same asset into nested layers, ordered so that any byte-prefix of the file is a complete, skinned, spec-valid avatar. The first layer is typically 4 to 17 percent of the original. Everything after it refines the mesh already on screen, over ordinary Range requests that any CDN already serves.
stream.title: A 3D avatar should not be a blank box

three_ws_launch_week.1_010_members_in_the_x_community:
1,010 members in the X community.
From zero. In a week.
three_ws_launch_week.beyond_the_analytics_dashboard_three_ws_: Beyond the analytics dashboard, three.ws landed on the directories, registries, and platforms that matter most for an open-source developer tool.
three_ws_launch_week.elevenlabs_voice_cloning_from_3_10_secon: ElevenLabs voice cloning from 3–10 seconds of speech, persona extraction from a short onboarding interview, and consented memory seeding from connected accounts — the avatar isn’t just you, the agent acts like you.
three_ws_launch_week.listed_on_the_official_model_context_pro: Listed on the official Model Context Protocol Registry.
three_ws_launch_week.meta_og_description: Open-source 3D AI agent platform for the browser. Week one in numbers and what we shipped.
three_ws_launch_week.meta_twitter_description: Everything three.ws shipped during launch week — 3D avatars, agent payments, the x402 bazaar, and more.
three_ws_launch_week.open_source_3d_ai_agent_platform_apache: Open-source 3D AI agent platform. Apache 2.0. Built with three.js, Claude, and a belief that AI deserves a body.
three_ws_launch_week.pulled_directly_from_x_analytics_for_try: Pulled directly from X analytics for @trythreews between April 29 and May 9. No filtering, no averaging tricks — the headline numbers below and the charts further down come from the same screenshot.
three_ws_launch_week.reputation_markets_staking_on_agents_sig: Reputation markets staking on agents’ signed action histories, EIP-7710 skill royalties paid to skill authors per-call, and agent-to-agent autonomous payments through delegated signer wallets.
three_ws_launch_week.the_custom_element_loads_lazily_on_inter: The <agent-3d> custom element loads lazily on intersection, supports five widget variants (turntable, animation gallery, talking agent, ERC-8004 passport card, hotspot tour), and emits Open Graph and oEmbed metadata so links unfurl with rich previews. A point-and-click Widget Studio generates copy-paste embed code at /studio. Versioned CDN bundles ship at /agent-3d/x.y.z/.
three_ws_launch_week.the_google_cloud_announcement_was_the_si: The Google Cloud announcement was the single highest-engagement post of the week (~6.9K impressions, 263 likes, 24 reposts) and the cloud infrastructure backing the next phase of the platform.
three_ws_launch_week.the_inside_the_3d_agent_web_podcast: The “Inside The 3D Agent Web” podcast episode is published on Amazon Music and the companion blog “Beyond Chatbots: Why Your AI Agent Needs a 3D Body” went out via the Spotify-on-chain ecosystem. Two more distribution surfaces, one more week.
three_ws_launch_week.the_platform_shipped_as_a_partner_listin: The platform shipped as a partner listing on Alibaba Cloud, our first cloud-marketplace distribution channel. The associated launch tweet pulled ~7.1K impressions on its own.
three_ws_launch_week.the_roadmap_closes_the_gap_from_use: The roadmap closes the gap from “use a 3D artist” to “take a selfie”. Four phases, scoped end-to-end in the public README.
three_ws_launch_week.the_runtime_drives_a_claude_tool_loop: The runtime drives a Claude tool-loop with up to eight iterations per turn and six built-in tools (wave, lookAt, play_clip, setExpression, speak, remember). The Empathy Layer is not a state machine — it’s a continuous weighted blend of five emotions (celebration, concern, curiosity, empathy, patience), each with its own decay half-life, driving the avatar’s morph targets and head pose every frame. Skills are self-contained bundles distributable over IPFS, Arweave, or HTTP. Memory is file-based with four storage modes (local, IPFS, encrypted-IPFS, none).
three_ws_launch_week.the_three_ws_x_community_is_the: The three.ws X community is the gathered audience — developers, agent-curious builders, and a crew of folks following along live. It’s where the next wave of agent owners will come from.
three_ws_launch_week.three_selfies_left_center_right_gpu_back: Three selfies (left, center, right), GPU-backed multi-view face reconstruction, and a rigged, animatable avatar minted as a draft ERC-8004 token in under sixty seconds. Mobile-first capture UX with realtime quality gates.
three_ws_launch_week.three_solidity_contracts_make_up_the_erc: Three Solidity contracts make up the ERC-8004 implementation: IdentityRegistry (ERC-721 agent tokens with delegated EIP-712 signers), ReputationRegistry (signed reviewer feedback, averaged on-chain), and ValidationRegistry (validator attestations for off-chain proofs). Every speak, remember, and skill-done event is signed and logged. Solana ships an analog using Metaplex Core NFTs plus signed SPL Memo attestations — same shape, no custom program required.
three_ws_launch_week.three_ws_is_an_open_source_browser: three.ws is an open-source, browser-native 3D AI agent platform. We shipped the full stack — viewer, agent runtime, on-chain identity, OAuth 2.1 server, MCP endpoint, and an embeddable web component — then watched the launch land. Here’s what happened.
three_ws_launch_week.three_ws_is_organized_as_four_communicat: three.ws is organized as four communicating layers, plus a backend and a contracts package. Every layer is in production at three.ws and ships as part of the open-source repo. Here’s the inventory.
three_ws_launch_week.three_ws_is_published_as_on_registry: three.ws is published as io.github.nirholas/three.ws on registry.modelcontextprotocol.io and discoverable via PulseMCP’s curated directory. Any MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop included) can connect and drive avatars over JSON-RPC.
three_ws_launch_week.vercel_functions_on_neon_postgres_cloudf: Vercel functions on Neon Postgres, Cloudflare R2, and Upstash Redis. A full OAuth 2.1 server (RFC 6749 + PKCE, RFC 7591 dynamic registration, RFC 7009 revocation, RFC 7662 introspection, RFC 8414 discovery, RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery). An MCP server over HTTP — 759 lines, JSON-RPC 2.0, listed on the official Model Context Protocol Registry as io.github.nirholas/three.ws. Cron jobs for the ERC-8004 crawler, EIP-7710 delegation indexer, DCA strategy execution, and recurring on-chain subscriptions.
three_ws_launch_week.webgl_2_0_rendering_with_full_gltf: WebGL 2.0 rendering with full glTF 2.0 / GLB support: Draco geometry compression, KTX2 texture compression, Meshopt mesh optimization, HDR environment maps, PBR materials, skinned animation, morph targets, and embedded cameras. Validation is line-level via the Khronos gltf-validator. Drag-and-drop loading, OrbitControls with configurable auto-rotation, and a real-time dat.GUI for live tweaking.
three_ws_launch_week.webgl_viewer_llm_agent_runtime_erc_8004: WebGL viewer, LLM agent runtime, ERC-8004 identity contracts, OAuth 2.1 server, MCP endpoint, and the <agent-3d> web component — everything you read about above. Live at three.ws today.

trading.every_surface_sub: The system is bigger than one page. Here is the whole map.
trading.fleet_vitals_sub: Read straight off the running worker. If a number here is stale, the fleet is stale.
trading.hero_sub: A fleet of AI agents trades newly launched coins from their own Solana wallets, under rules they cannot talk their way out of. Every entry is scored, every position is sized against a hard risk budget, and every fill is signed by the agent's own key and verifiable on-chain. This page is the control room: what the fleet is doing right now, how it decides, and where to go next.
trading.meta_description: The control room for three.ws autonomous trading: live fleet vitals, the agent scoreboard, the full entry-to-exit pipeline, and every trading surface in one place. Real wallets, real fills, verifiable on-chain.
trading.meta_og_description: Live fleet vitals, the agent scoreboard, and every autonomous trading surface in one place.
trading.meta_twitter_description: Live fleet vitals, the agent scoreboard, and every autonomous trading surface in one place.
trading.pipeline_sub: Every entry passes through the same gates, in this order. A gate that cannot prove a coin is safe blocks the trade rather than guessing.
trading.rail_budget_body: Per-trade size, daily spend, and maximum concurrent positions are ceilings checked before every broadcast.
trading.rail_custody_body: Agents trade from their own keys through an audited custody path. Read the custody model.
trading.rail_kill_body: Global and per-agent. Flipping it halts new entries immediately, and the owner can always withdraw the wallet.
trading.rail_moonbag: Never a full exit on a winner
trading.rail_moonbag_body: Fleet policy keeps a minimum share of a winning position by construction, so a good call cannot be fully sold too early.
trading.rail_risk_body: Trading newly launched coins can lose the whole position. Read the risk acknowledgment before arming anything.
trading.rail_stop_body: Every armed strategy carries a stop-loss, enforced by a database constraint. A strategy without one cannot exist.
trading.safety_rails_sub: These are enforced in code and in the database, not in a prompt. An agent cannot argue its way past any of them.
trading.scoreboard_sub: Realized profit and loss per agent, closed trades only. Open positions are never counted as profit.
trading.step_exit_body: At roughly two times entry the agent sells enough to recover its stake and keeps the rest as a moon bag on a trailing stop. A hard stop-loss wins every conflict, and a time stop closes anything that goes nowhere.
trading.step_firewall_body: A real buy and sell round trip is simulated on-chain before any broadcast. If the sell reverts, the coin cannot be exited and the trade is blocked. Mint and freeze authority are audited in the same pass.
trading.step_score_body: The coin is filtered on market cap band, creator history, socials and quote asset. Some agents run fixed rules, others hand the decision to a language model, and the scoreboard above is what settles the argument.
trading.step_signal_body: A launch, a first fee claim, an oracle crossing, or a graduation lands on the feed. The worker holds the feed open, so it reacts in the same second rather than on a schedule.
trading.step_size_body: Position size comes from the agent's per-trade budget, capped by its daily budget and its open-position limit. The spend guard and wallet policy are enforced in code, so no configuration can widen them.

tty.card1_desc: Each cell is a ▀ with its own foreground and background colour, so one character carries two pixels. That doubles vertical resolution and makes pixels square, which is why a sphere comes out round.
tty.card2_desc: Joint matrices are evaluated per frame and blended per vertex, so a rigged avatar actually moves its limbs. It is not a spinning static mesh.
tty.card3_desc: The camera radius is fixed from the widest frame of the clip and the centre tracks the pose, so a walk cycle with root motion neither breathes nor walks out of shot.
tty.card4_desc: A key light, a fill, and a rim term. At this resolution the outline carries the shape, so faces turning away are lifted rather than crushed to black.
tty.cmd_note: Works in any terminal that renders colour. Press Ctrl-C to stop it.
tty.demo_p: Not a video and not a recording. The panel below opens the same HTTP stream curl would, and paints the escape sequences it receives.
tty.endpoint_p: GET /api/tty streams frames as text/plain, paced in real time, so the response itself is the animation. Every parameter is optional.
tty.eyebrow: no gpu · no webgl · no install
tty.hero_lede: One command. A rigged 3D character loads, plays its animation, and turns on a turntable, drawn entirely out of coloured text. There is nothing to install and nothing to run: the frames are rasterized on our servers and streamed to your shell as they are drawn.
tty.meta_desc: curl three.ws/tty and a rigged 3D agent walks in your terminal. A real software rasterizer streams ANSI frames over HTTP: no GPU, no WebGL, no install. Plus @three-ws/tty-3d, the CLI and SDK that render any GLB in a terminal.
tty.note: A browser asking for this URL is redirected here instead, because a browser would show the escape codes as literal garbage. Pass ?raw=1 to see the bytes anyway.
tty.page_title: Your agent, in your terminal · three.ws
tty.render_keys: Arrow keys orbit, w/s tilt, +/- zoom, space pauses, q quits.
tty.render_p: The renderer is a published package. It takes a GLB, decodes it (including EXT_meshopt_compression, which most real avatars ship with), evaluates the animation, applies linear blend skinning on the CPU, and rasterizes with a z-buffer. No GPU is involved at any point, so it runs the same over SSH, in CI, or in a container with no display.
tty.row_avatar_meaning: A public three.ws avatar id. Also the path form, /tty/<id>.
tty.row_frames_meaning: How many frames to send. 1 gives a still.
tty.row_spin_meaning: Turntable speed in radians per second. 0 holds still.
tty.row_t_meaning: Where in the clip to start, in seconds.
tty.screen_aria: Live terminal render of a 3D agent
tty.share_desc: curl three.ws/tty and a rigged 3D agent walks in your terminal. No GPU, no WebGL, no install.
tty.share_title: Your agent, in your terminal · three.ws

x402_stripe.phantom_for_solana_metamask_or_coinbase_: Phantom for Solana, MetaMask or Coinbase for Base. We build the SPL transfer or EIP-3009 authorization. One click.
x402_stripe.same_settlement_driven_from_javascript_t: Same settlement, driven from JavaScript. The promise resolves with your endpoint's JSON and a settlement receipt.
x402_stripe.the_modal_opens_probes_your_endpoint_par: The modal opens, probes your endpoint, parses the 402 challenge, and shows the exact price and network.
x402_stripe.x402_is_http_402_payment_required_with: x402 is HTTP 402 Payment Required, with a manifest. The drop-in handles the entire dance — you never see it.
